Sumatran Striped Caecilian.Name: Sumatran Striped Caecilian
Sumatran Striped Caecilian.Description: These legless amphibians can be easily mistakened for worms or snakes with their elongated bodies and smooth skin. They have small eyes covered by a layer of skin. This species has a yellow stripe running down both sides of its body.
Sumatran Striped Caecilian.Habitat: Burrows in the ground and is elusive. Rarely encountered except after a heavy rainfall or in areas of recently disturbed soil

Crab-eating Frog.Name: Crab-eating Frog
Crab-eating Frog.Description: As its name suggests, this species is known to prey on crabs  found swampland and mangroves. Its skin is grey or brown with irregular black markings, and short low ridges. This species is also found in fields and disturbed forests. It is the only known amphibian that can tolerate salt water for short periods.
Crab-eating Frog.Habitat: occurs in a range of habitats including coastal scrub, marshes, disturbed forests and mangroves

Field Frog.Name: Field Frog
Field Frog.Description: This common frog has mottled green and brown skin with irregular black markings, and faint yellowish oblique strip on its side. It has short raised skin ridges along its back.
Field Frog.Habitat: Nocturnal and dwells in rice paddies, forest clearings, parks and gardens

Golden-eared Rough-sided Frog.Name: Golden-eared Rough-sided Frog
Golden-eared Rough-sided Frog.Description: One obvious characteristic of this species is its large  tympanum (eardrum) which has a yellowish spot in the middle.
Golden-eared Rough-sided Frog.Habitat: Found close to forest streams and swamPS.jpg in lowland primary and disturbed secondary forests.

Common Greenback.Name: Common Greenback
Common Greenback.Description: With its bright green back and distinct white stripes on either side of its back, as well as its white upper lip, this species is easily recognisable.
Common Greenback.Habitat: Often seen clinging to shrubs, or in puddles of water or by small streams.

Copper-cheeked Frog.Name: Copper-cheeked Frog
Copper-cheeked Frog.Description: This rather slender bright green to brownish or yellowish-green frog gets its name from its copper-coloured tympanum (eardrum), and can be found in forest streams.
Copper-cheeked Frog.Habitat: Occurs in shallow streams in lowland primary forest, adjacent secondary forest and freshwater swamp forest. Adults tend to perch low on streamside branches or fallen forest debris.

Masked Rough-sided Frog.Name: Masked Rough-sided Frog
Masked Rough-sided Frog.Description: This leaf-litter dwelling frog has a dark tympanum (eardrum), a brown back with blackish markings and a pale underside.
Masked Rough-sided Frog.Habitat: Occurs in freshwater swamp forests in Singapore.

Banded\u00a0Bull Frog.Name: Banded Bull Frog
Banded\u00a0Bull Frog.Description: This frog can be easily recognised by its round and stocky body, small head, and broad orange bands on both sides of its back. Common in disturbed habitats.
Banded\u00a0Bull Frog.Habitat: A highly adaptable species able to survive in disturbed habitat including flooded grassland, roadside puddles and urban storm drains. Hides in holes in the ground, under leaf litter or in cracks of walls

Black-eyed Litter Frog.Name: Black-eyed Litter Frog
Black-eyed Litter Frog.Description: So named for their large black eyes, this small frog has a grey to brown mottled pattern on its back. It's limbs are short and slender, and its call is a loud rapid rattle..
Black-eyed Litter Frog.Habitat: Dwells amongst the leaf litter of primary and mature secondary rainforests. Breeds in shallow water streams.

Malayan Giant Frog.Name: Malayan Giant Frog
Malayan Giant Frog.Description: This large frog which grows up to 26 cm is mainly found in forests  and forest edges. Its grey, brown or greenish skin is warty when young, but becomes smooth as an adult. Its body is robust and hind legs muscular.
Malayan Giant Frog.Habitat: Mainly found in the forest, but at night, it can be found in puddles or wet grass in forest clearings.

Malesian Frog.Name: Malesian Frog
Malesian Frog.Description: This nocturnal frog can be recognised by the dark patch on its tympanum (eardrum) and skin folds on its back. It can be distinguished from similar species by the 'W'-shaped fold of skin behind its head.
Malesian Frog.Habitat: A nocturnal species mainly found in the forest, but may venture into clearings.

Masked Swamp Frog.Name: Masked Swamp Frog
Masked Swamp Frog.Description: A freshwater swamp forest specialist, the Masked Swamp Frog has uniformly brown skin on its back, and a characterstic dark stripe running from its snout through its eye.
Masked Swamp Frog.Habitat: An elusive species that lives in acidic freshwater swamp forests

Rhinoceros Frog.Name: Rhinoceros Frog
Rhinoceros Frog.Description: A small species that has a distinct stocky body and large head. It has several low ridges on its back. The male has a bony protrusion at the top of its head.
Rhinoceros Frog.Habitat: Dwells in shallow, forest streams. It inhabits primary and secondary forests up to 1200 m elevation.

American Bullfrog.Name: American Bullfrog
American Bullfrog.Description: First introduced into and bred in Singapore for food, many have be released into the wild as part of religious merit-making offerings. This frog is greenish brown with a green head, and has a large tympanium.
American Bullfrog.Habitat: Found in ponds and reservoirs , where it is released for religious reasons.

Malayan Horned Frog.Name: Malayan Horned Frog
Malayan Horned Frog.Description: A rare species found in the forest, this mottled brown frog has distinct horn-like protrusions above its eyes and a wide mouth. It is often mistaken for leaf litter on the forest floor. Its call is a distinct metallic honk.
Malayan Horned Frog.Habitat: This mimic of tree litter can be found on the forest floor.

Painted\u00a0Chorus Frog.Name: Painted Chorus Frog
Painted\u00a0Chorus Frog.Description: The tiny Painted Chorus Frog is a small species that has a characteristic hourglass pattern on its back.
Painted\u00a0Chorus Frog.Habitat: Inhabits leaf litter and grassy areas in secondary forest, rural areas, parks and gardens. Can sometimes be found clinging to walls, tree trunks or low vegetation.

Dark-sided Chorus Frog.Name: Dark-sided Chorus Frog
Dark-sided Chorus Frog.Description: This tiny species has a flat brown back that helPS.jpg keep it out of sight in leaf-litter. As its name suggests, this frog has a thick black stripe along each side of its head and body.
Dark-sided Chorus Frog.Habitat: Lives close to small puddles and ponds in rural areas and secondary forest, where it hides in the grass and under leaf litter.

Manthey's Chorus Frog.Name: Manthey's Chorus Frog
Manthey's Chorus Frog.Description: This small frog has a triangular body shape with a small pointed head, brown mottled skin on its back which gets paler on its side, and black spots on its liPS.jpg.
Manthey's Chorus Frog.Habitat: Lives on the forest floor of damp, lowland rainforest. Tends to hide itself under leaf litter but occasionally visible on low vegetation.

Spotted Tree Frog.Name: Spotted Tree Frog
Spotted Tree Frog.Description: A small but striking frog with orange or brown skin and small white spots on its back, and pale undersides.
Spotted Tree Frog.Habitat: Occurs mainly in primary forest, in low vegetation. Its eggs can be found in tree cavities.

Yellow-bellied Puddle Frog.Name: Yellow-bellied Puddle Frog
Yellow-bellied Puddle Frog.Description: So named for its yellow belly, this forest species thrives in our forest streams, and is often well camouflaged by its grey-brown mottled skin. Often seen in shallow streams with its relatively small head protruding above the water surface.
Yellow-bellied Puddle Frog.Habitat: Occurs mainly in small streams and gullies in lowland primary and secondary forests. Can be spotted sitting in shallow water with its head emerged.

Four-lined Tree Frog.Name: Four-lined Tree Frog
Four-lined Tree Frog.Description: This slender species has a brown to yellow-brown back, often with four distinct lines from which it derives its common name. In some individuals, these stripes are absent. Common in disturbed habitats.
Four-lined Tree Frog.Habitat: Inhabits disturbed forests, scrubland, parks and gardens. May be spotted a few feet from the ground clinging on to small stems, or in puddles on wet ground.

Blue-legged Tree Frog.Name: Blue-legged Tree Frog
Blue-legged Tree Frog.Description: A small brown or beige frog with a slender body and legs. It also has large eyes with a white patches underneath.
Blue-legged Tree Frog.Habitat: An elusive species that dwells in moist lowland rainforest and freshwater swamp forest where it lives alongside streamside vegetation. Stays hidden amongst leaf clumPS.jpg or tree crevices in the day, but emerges to the upperside of large leaves at night.

Thorny Tree Frog.Name: Thorny Tree Frog
Thorny Tree Frog.Description: A very rare species in Singapore that can be very well camouflaged by its green-brown and bumpy skin.
Thorny Tree Frog.Habitat: Occurs in lowland rainforest. Eggs may be found above water-filled cavities in trees.

G\u00fcnther\u2019s Frog.Name: Günther’s Frog
G\u00fcnther\u2019s Frog.Description: This large frog is known from East Asia, and can be identified by its pale brown back, darker brown bands along the sides of its body, and a pale outline around its tympanum (eardrum).
G\u00fcnther\u2019s Frog.Habitat: Typically found in open swampy habitats and agricultural areas. Have been found in ponds in Singapore.

Lim's Black-spotted Sticky Frog.Name: Lim's Black-spotted Sticky Frog
Lim's Black-spotted Sticky Frog.Description: This nocturnal frog has a distinct flat and triangular body with a brown/orange back skin separated from its sides by a thin white stripe. It camouflages itself well in the forest leaf-litter.
Lim's Black-spotted Sticky Frog.Habitat: Solitary and nocturnal, this species is primarily found in leaf litter on the forest floor.

Asian Toad.Name: Asian Toad
Asian Toad.Description: This common species can often be heard calling after a rainy day. It has warty grey-green skin and has a blackish raised ridge behind each eye (paratoid glands).
Asian Toad.Habitat: found on grass lawns at night, on patHS.jpg and roads and concretised drains

Four-ridged Toad.Name: Four-ridged Toad
Four-ridged Toad.Description: Commonly found in swampy forests, this toad species can be recognised by its uniform orange-brown distinctly warty skin, four low ridges on top of  its head and dual-syllabic call.
Four-ridged Toad.Habitat: Occupies leaf litter of primary and secondary lowland forest. However it can be found in heavily modified habitats such as plantations.

Saint Andrew's Cross Toadlet.Name: Saint Andrew's Cross Toadlet
Saint Andrew's Cross Toadlet.Description: This rare species inhabits primary forests. Adults of this tiny species measures just 25mm, and are named for the cross-shaped pattern of bands on their backs. Their backs are mottled brown, with several orange or yellow spots.
Saint Andrew's Cross Toadlet.Habitat: Largely confined to lowland primary forest. Eggs are laid in small accumulations of water in the crooks of trees.

Black Dwarf Honey Bee.Name: Black Dwarf Honey Bee
Black Dwarf Honey Bee.Description: Small, brown to black bee with pale abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened.

Red Dwarf Honey Bee.Name: Red Dwarf Honey Bee
Red Dwarf Honey Bee.Description: Small bee with a grey thorax, orange and black abdomen, and pale abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened.

Asian Honey Bee.Name: Asian Honey Bee
Asian Honey Bee.Description:
Medium-sized orange bee with a brown thorax and dark brown abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened. 

Males (known as drones) are entirely black and have large eyes that converge on top.

Giant Honey Bee.Name: Giant Honey Bee
Giant Honey Bee.Description: Large bee with a black head and thorax and dark wings. Its abdomen is orange and black with pale abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened.

Valdez's Stingless Bee.Name: Valdez's Stingless Bee
Valdez's Stingless Bee.Description: Tiny bee with a grey to black thorax and chestnut brown abdomen. Hind legs broad and flattened. Often hovers in flight.
Valdez's Stingless Bee.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

Gold-margined Stingless Bee.Name: Gold-margined Stingless Bee
Gold-margined Stingless Bee.Description: Tiny bee with yellow hairs lining a grey thorax. Hind legs broad and flattened. Has a hovering flight pattern.
Gold-margined Stingless Bee.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

White-cheeked Carpenter Bee.Name: White-cheeked Carpenter Bee
White-cheeked Carpenter Bee.Description:
Large bee with a yellow thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have purple iridescence. Unlike the similar Yellow-and-black Carpenter Bee (X. flavonigrescens), the sides of its face have white hairs and the first segment of its abdomen does not have yellow hairs. 

Males are entirely covered with yellow hair.

Cerulean Carpenter Bee.Name: Cerulean Carpenter Bee
Cerulean Carpenter Bee.Description: A large bee with a bright blue thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have a bluish iridescence.

Sunda Blue-Banded Digger Bee.Name: Sunda Blue-Banded Digger Bee
Sunda Blue-Banded Digger Bee.Description: Large bee with a bright blue thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have a bluish iridescence.

Himalayan Cloak-and-Dagger Bee.Name: Himalayan Cloak-and-Dagger Bee
Himalayan Cloak-and-Dagger Bee.Description: Medium-sized bee with a pale blue body with distinct black markings. This bee has a cuckoo lifestyle.
Himalayan Cloak-and-Dagger Bee.Nesting: Lays in eggs in the nest of digger bees.

Notch-toothed Stingless Bee.Name: Notch-toothed Stingless Bee
Notch-toothed Stingless Bee.Description: Small black bee with dark. Hind legs broad and flattened. Has a hovering flight pattern.
Notch-toothed Stingless Bee.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

Milky-tipped Stingless Bee.Name: Milky-tipped Stingless Bee
Milky-tipped Stingless Bee.Description: Small brown bee with white-tipped wings. Hind legs broad and flattened. Has a hovering flight pattern.
Milky-tipped Stingless Bee.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

Companion Small Carpenter Bee.Name: Companion Small Carpenter Bee
Companion Small Carpenter Bee.Description: A small black and yellow bee. Antennal scapes are entirely black. Marking on the first abdominal segment is a yellow band with two black spots.

Emerald Small Carpenter Bee.Name: Emerald Small Carpenter Bee
Emerald Small Carpenter Bee.Description: A small, cylindrical bee with a bright metallic green appearance. Its integument is heavily pitted.

Puang Reed Bee.Name: Puang Reed Bee
Puang Reed Bee.Description: A tiny, slender black bee. Its face has a pale patch, the shape of a slender inverted triangle. It carries pollen using white hairs on its hind legs.

Yellow-and-black Carpenter Bee.Name: Yellow-and-black Carpenter Bee
Yellow-and-black Carpenter Bee.Description: Large bee with a yellow thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have blueish green iridescence. Unlike the similar White-cheeked Carpenter Bee (X. aestuans), the sides of its face lacks white hairs and the first segment of its abdomen has sparse yellow hairs.

Island Forest-Digger Bee.Name: Island Forest-Digger Bee
Island Forest-Digger Bee.Description: Medium-sized bee covered with orange hairs. Its face is yellow with brown markings. It is larger than the Sunda Blue-Banded Digger Bee (Amegilla andrewsi).

Lieftinck\u2019s Small Carpenter Bee.Name: Lieftinck’s Small Carpenter Bee
Lieftinck\u2019s Small Carpenter Bee.Description: Small black and yellow bee. Antennal scapes are partially yellow. Marking on the first abdominal segment is a yellow band with two black spots.

Broad-handed Carpenter Bee.Name: Broad-handed Carpenter Bee
Broad-handed Carpenter Bee.Description:
A very large, black bee. Its wings have bright purple and green iridescence. Females tend to visit large open flowers. 

Males possess white feather-like front legs, and tend to perch on structures.

Black-sided Small Carpenter Bee.Name: Black-sided Small Carpenter Bee
Black-sided Small Carpenter Bee.Description: A small black and yellow bee. Antennal scapes are entirely black. Marking on the first abdominal segment is a yellow band with two black spots.

One-spotted Small Carpenter Bee.Name: One-spotted Small Carpenter Bee
One-spotted Small Carpenter Bee.Description: A small, cylindrical bee with a metallic purple appearance. Its integument is heavily pitted.

Penang Masked Bee.Name: Penang Masked Bee
Penang Masked Bee.Description: A tiny black bee with yellow legs and facial markings.

Striped Nomia.Name: Striped Nomia
Striped Nomia.Description: A medium-sized bee with a black thorax and iridescent abdominal bands. Hairs on the head and body are mostly yellow.

Wandering Combed-Sweat Bee.Name: Wandering Combed-Sweat Bee
Wandering Combed-Sweat Bee.Description: Tiny bee with grey body and white abdominal banding.

Palm Plume-vented Bee.Name: Palm Plume-vented Bee
Palm Plume-vented Bee.Description: Small metallic green bee with pollen-collecting hairs on its legs an underneath the abdomen. Often found visiting the inflorescences of palms.

Red-waisted Grass-Nomia.Name: Red-waisted Grass-Nomia
Red-waisted Grass-Nomia.Description: A tiny bee. Females are orange with yellow abdominal bands. Males are slender and have a red first abdominal segment.  Females collect pollen strictly from grasses.

Singapore Plume-vented Bee.Name: Singapore Plume-vented Bee
Singapore Plume-vented Bee.Description: Tiny bee with dark, metallic green integument. Possesses pollen-collecting hairs on legs and underneath the abdomen. Often found visiting the inflorescences of palms. Smaller than the Palm Plume-vented Bee (L. adonidiae)

White Combed-Sweat Bee.Name: White Combed-Sweat Bee
White Combed-Sweat Bee.Description: A small bee with black body and white abdominal banding. Larger than the Wandering Combed-Sweat Bee.

Black-waisted Pronged-Nomia.Name: Black-waisted Pronged-Nomia
Black-waisted Pronged-Nomia.Description: Medium-sized bee with a grey thorax and iridescent bands on all abdominal segments except the first. Hairs on the head and body are mostly white or grey.

Broad-headed Leafcutter Bee.Name: Broad-headed Leafcutter Bee
Broad-headed Leafcutter Bee.Description: Medium-sized bee covered with orange to reddish hairs and black abdominal banding. Possesses yellow pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Broad-headed Leafcutter Bee.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using cut pieces of leaves.

Disjunct Resin Bee.Name: Disjunct Resin Bee
Disjunct Resin Bee.Description: Medium-sized, slender bee with a black body except for patches of white hairs behind its thorax. Possesses black pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Disjunct Resin Bee.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using plant resin.

Shadow-winged Resin Bee.Name: Shadow-winged Resin Bee
Shadow-winged Resin Bee.Description: A small to medium-sized, slender bee with a thorax covered with orange hairs. Its wings are dark purple. Possesses yellow pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Shadow-winged Resin Bee.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using plant resin.

Dimorphic Leafcutter Bee.Name: Dimorphic Leafcutter Bee
Dimorphic Leafcutter Bee.Description: Medium-sized bee with a black body except for patches of white hairs behind its thorax. Easily distinguished from the Disjunct Resin Bee (M. disjuncta) in having red pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Dimorphic Leafcutter Bee.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using cut pieces of leaves.

Orange-bellied Leafcutter Bee.Name: Orange-bellied Leafcutter Bee
Orange-bellied Leafcutter Bee.Description: A small bee. Females are dark grey with pale abdominal bands. Possesses pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen that are partially orange and white. Males are covered with yellow to brown hairs.
Orange-bellied Leafcutter Bee.Nesting: Nests in the soil using cut pieces of leaves.

Orange-winged Resin Bee.Name: Orange-winged Resin Bee
Orange-winged Resin Bee.Description: A medium-sized to large, slender bee with a black body and orange wings.
Orange-winged Resin Bee.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using plant resin.

Confusing Sharp-tailed Bee.Name: Confusing Sharp-tailed Bee
Confusing Sharp-tailed Bee.Description: A small cuckoo bee with a grey body and white abdominal bands. Females have an abdomen that constricts to a sharp point. Males have spines at the tip of the abdomen.
Confusing Sharp-tailed Bee.Nesting: Lays eggs in the nests of leafcutter bees.

Sunda Chilli-tail Bee.Name: Sunda Chilli-tail Bee
Sunda Chilli-tail Bee.Description: A small to medium-sized, stocky bee with a grey head and thorax, and bright red abdomen. It has a cuckoo lifestyle.
Sunda Chilli-tail Bee.Nesting: Lays eggs in the nests of resin bees.

Lineated Barbet.Name: Lineated Barbet
Lineated Barbet.Description: The head, nape and breast of this bird are white with brown streaks, and has green wings, back and tail, and a pink bill. It has also has a distinct yellow eye-ring.

Red-crowned Barbet.Name: Red-crowned Barbet
Red-crowned Barbet.Description: This striking bird has a distinctly colourful head - with a red crown and a blue eyebrow and throat.

Coppersmith Barbet.Name: Coppersmith Barbet
Coppersmith Barbet.Description: This small species has a red forehead and a black and yellow mask. It also has a distinct red and yellow patch on its throat.

Golden-bellied Gerygone.Name: Golden-bellied Gerygone
Golden-bellied Gerygone.Description: This tiny songbird has a brown head and upperparts and yellow underparts.

Moustached Babbler.Name: Moustached Babbler
Moustached Babbler.Description: This babbler is moustached, from which its common name is derived. It can also be recognised by its red eyes. Tail is strongly rufous.

Chestnut-winged Babbler.Name: Chestnut-winged Babbler
Chestnut-winged Babbler.Description: An easily identifiable babbler with chestnut upperparts, a grey head and breast, blue eye-ring and pale belly.

Pin-striped Tit-Babbler.Name: Pin-striped Tit-Babbler
Pin-striped Tit-Babbler.Description: This babbler has characteristic fine black streaks on its throat and breast, yellowish underparts and brown upperparts.

Eastern Barn Owl.Name: Eastern Barn Owl
Eastern Barn Owl.Description: Distinctive owl identified by its pale white and brown plumage and heart-shaped face.

Blue-throated Bee-Eater.Name: Blue-throated Bee-Eater
Blue-throated Bee-Eater.Description: While similar to the blue-tailed bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its brown head and bright blue throat.

Blue-tailed Bee-Eater.Name: Blue-tailed Bee-Eater
Blue-tailed Bee-Eater.Description: While similar to the blue-throated bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its olive head and yellow-brown throat.

Red-footed Booby.Name: Red-footed Booby
Red-footed Booby.Description: This large seabird has red legs, a blue bill, pinkish facial skin and a mostly white plumage and tail. Juveniles have pale brown plumage.

Brown Booby.Name: Brown Booby
Brown Booby.Description: This booby has a chocolate-brown head, upperparts and upper breast, while its belly is white. It has bluish facial skin and pale green bill and feet.

Straw-headed Bulbul.Name: Straw-headed Bulbul
Straw-headed Bulbul.Description: With its distinct call, this shy songbird is heard more often than it is seen. It has a brown streaked body, olive green wings, straw-coloured crown, black eyebrow and moustache.

Black-and-white Bulbul.Name: Black-and-white Bulbul
Black-and-white Bulbul.Description: This bulbul is completely black aside from a white wing patch.

Black-headed Bulbul.Name: Black-headed Bulbul
Black-headed Bulbul.Description: This bulbul is easily recognisable with its yellow plumage, black head and blue eyes.

Red-whiskered Bulbul.Name: Red-whiskered Bulbul
Red-whiskered Bulbul.Description: This bird has a striking black crest, red eye-patch and vent. Has white cheeks and underparts and partial blackish-brown necklace.

Sooty-headed Bulbul.Name: Sooty-headed Bulbul
Sooty-headed Bulbul.Description: Similar plumage to the Yellow-vented Bulbul but has a prominent black head and either a red or orange vent.

Yellow-vented Bulbul.Name: Yellow-vented Bulbul
Yellow-vented Bulbul.Description: A common bird with brown upperparts, pale underparts, a black lore and a bright yellow vent.

Olive-winged Bulbul.Name: Olive-winged Bulbul
Olive-winged Bulbul.Description: This is a drab olive brown bird with red eyes and greenish-yellow tinged wings.

Cream-vented Bulbul.Name: Cream-vented Bulbul
Cream-vented Bulbul.Description: A generally brown bird with paler undersides that can be recognised by its white eye.

Asian Red-eyed Bulbul.Name: Asian Red-eyed Bulbul
Asian Red-eyed Bulbul.Description: Similar to the Cream-vented Bulbul but has red eyes. Head and upperparts are uniformly brown.

Buff-vented Bulbul.Name: Buff-vented Bulbul
Buff-vented Bulbul.Description: Can be identified by its small crest and dark eyestripe.

Streaked Bulbul.Name: Streaked Bulbul
Streaked Bulbul.Description: This species has dull olive-green upperparts with grey throat and breast that is streaked white. Has a white belly.

Black-crested Bulbul.Name: Black-crested Bulbul
Black-crested Bulbul.Description: Similar plumage to the Black-headed Bulbul but has a prominent black crest.

Cinereous Bulbul.Name: Cinereous Bulbul
Cinereous Bulbul.Description: This bulbul has ashy brown upperparts, white underparts and a small crest .Has a prominent white throat that is often puffed out.

Barred Buttonquail.Name: Barred Buttonquail
Barred Buttonquail.Description: As its name suggests, the barred buttonquail has distinct barring on most of its upperparts. Females have a black throat, while males do not.

Black-naped Monarch.Name: Black-naped Monarch
Black-naped Monarch.Description: Males have mostly blue plummage with diagnostic black necklace and nape. Females mostly grey-brown on upperparts and underparts with blue restricted to the head.

White-throated Rock Thrush.Name: White-throated Rock Thrush
White-throated Rock Thrush.Description: Males of this species have a blue crown and orangey-red underparts. Females are brown above and white below and heavily scaled throughout. White throat patch visible in both sexes

Grey-streaked Flycatcher.Name: Grey-streaked Flycatcher
Grey-streaked Flycatcher.Description: This small flycatcher has grey-brown upperparts and white underparts which are heavily streaked throughout.

Dark-sided Flycatcher.Name: Dark-sided Flycatcher
Dark-sided Flycatcher.Description: Simiar to Asian Brown Flycatcher, but has more prominent streaked underparts, smaller bill and lacks broad white lores.

Brown-streaked Flycatcher.Name: Brown-streaked Flycatcher
Brown-streaked Flycatcher.Description: Similar to Asian Brown, but with richer brown upperparts and faint brown streaks on underparts.

Ferruginous Flycatcher.Name: Ferruginous Flycatcher
Ferruginous Flycatcher.Description: As its common name suggests, the Ferruginous Flycatcher has a rusty-orange pluamge with a grey head.

Yellow-rumped Flycatcher.Name: Yellow-rumped Flycatcher
Yellow-rumped Flycatcher.Description: Males have black upperparts with a white eyestripe and yellow underparts, while females have brown upperparts and brownish underparts with a yellowish tinge.

Mugimaki Flycatcher.Name: Mugimaki Flycatcher
Mugimaki Flycatcher.Description: Males have black upperparts, white patch behind the eye, orange breast and throat and white belly. Females have brown upperparts instead.

Blue-and-white Flycatcher.Name: Blue-and-white Flycatcher
Blue-and-white Flycatcher.Description: Males are easily recognised by blue upperparts, black face and throat. It is white from belly downwards. Females have brownish upperparts with distinct contrast between brownish breast and white belly.

Chinese Blue Flycatcher.Name: Chinese Blue Flycatcher
Chinese Blue Flycatcher.Description: Males have a distinctive fieldmark where there a narrow orange wedge which extends from breast to the throat.  Females have a white throat and belly separated by a brown breast band.

Oriental Magpie-Robin.Name: Oriental Magpie-Robin
Oriental Magpie-Robin.Description: This songbird has black and white plumage with a long tail that is often held high.  Females are grey on upperparts and breast.

White-rumped Shama.Name: White-rumped Shama
White-rumped Shama.Description: The white-rumped shama has black upperparts, orange breast and belly, white rump and long tail. Females are duller with shorter tail.

Indian Paradise Flycatcher.Name: Indian Paradise Flycatcher
Indian Paradise Flycatcher.Description: Breeding males have an exceptionally long tail and come in either rufous or white colour morphs. Females and non-breeding males have much shorter tail and either white or chestnut upperparts with varying amount of grey or black on head, throat and upper breast.

Japanese Paradise Flycatcher.Name: Japanese Paradise Flycatcher
Japanese Paradise Flycatcher.Description: Breeding males have an exceptionally long tail, dark purple plumage and white belly. Females and non-breeding males are generally darker than Asian Paradise Flycatchers with rusty-brown upperparts and black on the head, throat and upper breast.

Blue Rock Thrush.Name: Blue Rock Thrush
Blue Rock Thrush.Description: This species has blue upperparts and breast and a rusty-brown belly. Females are generally grey-brown, sometimes with faint bluish tinge, and heavily scaled throughout.

Brown-chested Jungle Flycatcher.Name: Brown-chested Jungle Flycatcher
Brown-chested Jungle Flycatcher.Description: This drab flycatcher may be confused with the other brown flycatchers like the Asian Brown and Brown-streaked. It can be identified by its completely yellow lower mandible, flesh coloured legs and also brown breast band which other flycatchers lack.

Asian Brown Flycatcher.Name: Asian Brown Flycatcher
Asian Brown Flycatcher.Description: The Asian Brown flycatcher has grey-brown throat and breast with white belly, prominent white lores and a fleshy base to its lower mandible.

Green-backed Flycatcher.Name: Green-backed Flycatcher
Green-backed Flycatcher.Description: With greenish brown upperparts and yellow underparts, females of this species look similar to the female Yellow-rumped Flycatcher. However, females of this species lack the yellow rump that the latter species has.  Males are distinctive – yellow eyebrow, greenish upperparts and bright yellow underparts with big white wing patch.

Mangrove Blue Flycatcher.Name: Mangrove Blue Flycatcher
Mangrove Blue Flycatcher.Description: Similar to the Chinese Blue Flycatcher, but has a dark blue chin as opposed to an orange one. Females have white lores (area between eyes and bill base) and throat.

Siberian Blue Robin.Name: Siberian Blue Robin
Siberian Blue Robin.Description: Male Siberian Blue Robins has blue upperparts and white underparts, while females are brown with pale underparts. Females have dull blue rump and tail.

Stejneger's Stonechat.Name: Stejneger's Stonechat
Stejneger's Stonechat.Description: Males have a black head, dark brown upperparts, white collar and rufous underparts. Females are brown with a thin white collar, pale underparts and a beige/ light pink rump.

Zappey's Flycatcher.Name: Zappey's Flycatcher
Zappey's Flycatcher.Description: Only males in breeding plumage can be distinguished from very similar Blue-and-white Flycatcher. Males of this species have bluish face and throat, not black as per the latter species.

Daurian Redstart.Name: Daurian Redstart
Daurian Redstart.Description: Males have greyish crown, black face and throat, and orange underparts with distinct white wing patch. Females are generally brownish with pale eyering and white wing patch.

Amur Paradise Flycatcher.Name: Amur Paradise Flycatcher
Amur Paradise Flycatcher.Description: Brown upperparts and tail, black head with grey underparts with white vent. Adult males can have tails longer than 27cm. White morphs exists but are rare. Compared with Blyth's Paradise Flycatcher, the blackish head contrasts noticeably with the greyish breast

Blyth's Paradise Flycatcher.Name: Blyth's Paradise Flycatcher
Blyth's Paradise Flycatcher.Description: Brown upperparts and tail, grey head and underparts with white vent. Adult males can have tails longer than 27cm. White morphs occur rarely. Compared with Amur Paradise Flycatcher, there is minimal contrast between the grey head and breast

Zitting Cisticola.Name: Zitting Cisticola
Zitting Cisticola.Description: A small bird with brown and black upperparts, white underparts, brown rump and flanks and pale face.

Yellow-bellied Prinia.Name: Yellow-bellied Prinia
Yellow-bellied Prinia.Description: A tiny bird with a high-pitched trilling song, long tail, and yellow belly and vent.

Common Tailorbird.Name: Common Tailorbird
Common Tailorbird.Description: Similar to the Dark-necked Tailorbird, but has a less extensive red cap and white vent. Males have a longer tail than females.

Dark-necked Tailorbird.Name: Dark-necked Tailorbird
Dark-necked Tailorbird.Description: Similar to the Common Tailorbird but has a more extensive red cap and a yellow vent. Males have black breast patch which is absent in females.

Rufous-tailed Tailorbird.Name: Rufous-tailed Tailorbird
Rufous-tailed Tailorbird.Description: This species possesses a red tail and crown, grey mantle and white underparts.

Ashy Tailorbird.Name: Ashy Tailorbird
Ashy Tailorbird.Description: This tailorbird has a rufous head and grey upperparts with brownish wings, with pale ashy underparts.

Yellow-crested Cockatoo.Name: Yellow-crested Cockatoo
Yellow-crested Cockatoo.Description: This white bird is easily identifiable by its yellow crest, and the local population is thought to be a result of escapees or released pet birds.

Tanimbar Corella.Name: Tanimbar Corella
Tanimbar Corella.Description: A non-native bird is generally white and the pink lores.

House Crow.Name: House Crow
House Crow.Description: This urban bird can be differentiated from the Large-billed Crow by its grey collar.

Large-billed Crow.Name: Large-billed Crow
Large-billed Crow.Description: Similar to the House Crow except that it is entirely black and has a distinctly larger bill.

Chestnut-winged Cuckoo.Name: Chestnut-winged Cuckoo
Chestnut-winged Cuckoo.Description: This cuckoo has a distinctive black crest and long black tail.

Large Hawk-Cuckoo.Name: Large Hawk-Cuckoo
Large Hawk-Cuckoo.Description: Largest hawk-cuckoo species in Singapore, has contrasting streaks and barring on its underparts. Juveniles have streaked underparts.

Malaysian Hawk-Cuckoo.Name: Malaysian Hawk-Cuckoo
Malaysian Hawk-Cuckoo.Description: Adults have greyish upperparts and underparts with thin, dark brown streaks, juveniles with weaker streaking and more spotting; distinct white nape patch and broad tail subterminal band.

Hodgson's Hawk-Cuckoo.Name: Hodgson's Hawk-Cuckoo
Hodgson's Hawk-Cuckoo.Description: Adults have dark streaking with extensive rufous wash, juveniles have strong dark streaking with slight rufous-tinge; narrow tail subterminal band.

Indian Cuckoo.Name: Indian Cuckoo
Indian Cuckoo.Description: This species has greyish-brown upperparts contrasting and white underparts with numerous black bands. Distinct black band on upperside of tail.

Banded Bay Cuckoo.Name: Banded Bay Cuckoo
Banded Bay Cuckoo.Description: This species has barred throughout with rufous upperparts and white underparts, and can be distinguished from the other cuckoos by its whitish eyebrow.

Plaintive Cuckoo.Name: Plaintive Cuckoo
Plaintive Cuckoo.Description: This species has rufous underparts and a grey head, throat and breast. Can be differentiaed from the rusty-breasted cuckoo by its rufous plumage which only extendsto its belly. Juveniles have more prominent black barring.

Rusty-breasted Cuckoo.Name: Rusty-breasted Cuckoo
Rusty-breasted Cuckoo.Description: Similar to the Plaintive Cuckoo, except that it has a yellow eye ring, and the rufous plumage extends to its throat.

Little Bronze Cuckoo.Name: Little Bronze Cuckoo
Little Bronze Cuckoo.Description: Underparts of this cuckoo are white with black barring, not black and white barring. Only males have a red eye-ring.

Horsfield's Bronze Cuckoo.Name: Horsfield's Bronze Cuckoo
Horsfield's Bronze Cuckoo.Description: This species looks similar to the Little Bronze Cuckoo but can be distinguished by its dark eyestripe and incomplete bars on its belly.

Asian Emerald Cuckoo.Name: Asian Emerald Cuckoo
Asian Emerald Cuckoo.Description: This species gets its name from its bright metallic green upperparts.

Violet Cuckoo.Name: Violet Cuckoo
Violet Cuckoo.Description: Males of this species have a violet sheen to its head, back and wings. Females are a lot more drab, with mostly rusty brown and green upperparts .

Chestnut-bellied Malkoha.Name: Chestnut-bellied Malkoha
Chestnut-bellied Malkoha.Description: This large bird has a grey head and breast, dark metallic green upperparts and a long tail. It can be easily identified by its red eye-patch.

Greater Coucal.Name: Greater Coucal
Greater Coucal.Description: The Greater Coucal has a distinct dark plumage with chestnut brown wings.

Lesser Coucal.Name: Lesser Coucal
Lesser Coucal.Description: Similar to the Greater Coucal but is smaller and paler, and has pale streaks on its head and underparts.

Himalayan Cuckoo.Name: Himalayan Cuckoo
Himalayan Cuckoo.Description: Like Indian Cuckoo but mantle and upper back grey, also lacks the broad dark subterminal band on the upperside of the tail.

Square-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo.Name: Square-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo
Square-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo.Description: Can be distinguished from a drongo by its thinner bill and slight white barring on its tail. Juveniles have white spots on their plumage.

Asian Koel.Name: Asian Koel
Asian Koel.Description: This large bird has a distinct loud call from which it derives its common name. They can be distinguished from crows with their long tails and red eyes.

Lesser Cuckooshrike.Name: Lesser Cuckooshrike
Lesser Cuckooshrike.Description: Males of this species are grey with darker wings, while females are grey with heavily barred underparts.

Pied Triller.Name: Pied Triller
Pied Triller.Description: Males have a distinct black and white pied plumage, while females are greyish-brown above with fine barring on the underparts.

Ashy Minivet.Name: Ashy Minivet
Ashy Minivet.Description: The Ashy Minivet has grey upperparts and white underparts and a distinct black loral line. Males have a black cap, females have a grey cap.

Scarlet Minivet.Name: Scarlet Minivet
Scarlet Minivet.Description: Males have red underparts, rump and wing patches on otherwise black wings. In females, areas of red replaced by yellow which also extends to throat and forecrown.

Oriental Darter.Name: Oriental Darter
Oriental Darter.Description: A large bird with a long snake-like neck and pointed bill. Glossy black plumage with a brown head and neck, and distinct white stripes along the neck.

Black Drongo.Name: Black Drongo
Black Drongo.Description: Completely black with a deeply forked tail.

Ashy Drongo.Name: Ashy Drongo
Ashy Drongo.Description: The Ashy Drongo can be differentiated from the Black Drongo by its paler grey plumage and shallower forked tail.

Crow-billed Drongo.Name: Crow-billed Drongo
Crow-billed Drongo.Description: The Crow-billed Drongo can be differentiated from the Black Drongo by its larger bill and upturned forked tail. Immatures have white spots on the underparts.

Greater Racket-tailed Drongo.Name: Greater Racket-tailed Drongo
Greater Racket-tailed Drongo.Description: This unmistakable bird has two extended tail feathers and a distinct song with a metallic trill at the end. Also has distinct tuft of feathers at base of the bill.

Wandering Whistling Duck.Name: Wandering Whistling Duck
Wandering Whistling Duck.Description: So called because of their high-pitched whistles, the wandering whistling duck may be confused with the similar lesser whistling duck. It can be differentiated by its white flank plumes.

Lesser Whistling Duck.Name: Lesser Whistling Duck
Lesser Whistling Duck.Description: This species is also sometimes called the lesser tree duck as they occasionally nest in tree holes. Can be confused with the wandering whistling duck.

Cotton Pygmy Goose.Name: Cotton Pygmy Goose
Cotton Pygmy Goose.Description: Males of this species have a black cap and collar, while females lack this collar and have a dark eye-stripe.

Eurasian Wigeon.Name: Eurasian Wigeon
Eurasian Wigeon.Description: Females of this species are almost entirely brown, while males have a  chestnut head and neck and finely barred whitish underparts.

Gadwall.Name: Gadwall
Gadwall.Description: Males are generally gray-brown with a white belly and black rump, while females uniformly mottled brown and have a black and orange bill.

Eurasian Teal.Name: Eurasian Teal
Eurasian Teal.Description: Male Eurasian teals have a distinct green eye-patch. Females are more drab, with a mottled brown plumage and lacking the green eye-patch that males possess.

Northern Pintail.Name: Northern Pintail
Northern Pintail.Description: Males of this sepcies have characteristic long tail-feathers, and a distinct slim and long neck. Females are generally brown.

Northern Shoveler.Name: Northern Shoveler
Northern Shoveler.Description: So called for its large shovel-shaped bill, the Nothern Shoveler is an easy bird to identify. Males have a green head and white breast, while females are uniformly brown with an orange bill.

Tufted Duck.Name: Tufted Duck
Tufted Duck.Description: Males have a characteristic drooping crest and black and white plumage. Females are uniformly brown and have a short crest.

Asian Fairy-bluebird.Name: Asian Fairy-bluebird
Asian Fairy-bluebird.Description: An easily identifiable bird, males have a characteristic blue and black plumage while females are uniformly dull-blue. Both sexes have reddish eyes.

Black-thighed Falconet.Name: Black-thighed Falconet
Black-thighed Falconet.Description: This is a small falcon with a rufous belly, white breast and mostly black upperparts.

Common Kestrel.Name: Common Kestrel
Common Kestrel.Description: Males can be distinguished from the Lesser Kestrel by streaked grey heads and boldly marked chestnut upperparts. Females have more prominent streaks on their heads and underparts and more prominent face mask and upperpart markings.

Amur Falcon.Name: Amur Falcon
Amur Falcon.Description: Males of this species has dark grey upperparts and a pale grey breast and chesnut vent. Females have grey upperparts and grey and white streaked underparts. Both sexes have distinctive orange-red eyering, bill base and legs.

Peregrine Falcon.Name: Peregrine Falcon
Peregrine Falcon.Description: Larger than all the other falcons, the Peregrine Falcon has with heavily barred underparts, greyish upperparts with white underparts, whitish cheeks and a broad facial “streak”.

Malaysian Pied Fantail.Name: Malaysian Pied Fantail
Malaysian Pied Fantail.Description: This passerine species has a distinct pied plumage with a white throat and underparts and black breast band. Often fans its tail out during displays.

Masked Finfoot.Name: Masked Finfoot
Masked Finfoot.Description: This endangered shorebird is a visitor can be recognised by its dark face and throat with a white border and thick yellow bill. Females have a whitish throat and upper foreneck.

Thick-billed Flowerpecker.Name: Thick-billed Flowerpecker
Thick-billed Flowerpecker.Description: With its thick bill, this flowerpecker looks distinctly different from the other flowerpeckers. It has olive-brown upperparts and pale streaked underparts. Also has a unique habit of wagging its tail to one side when perched.

Yellow-vented Flowerpecker.Name: Yellow-vented Flowerpecker
Yellow-vented Flowerpecker.Description: This rare small bird can be easily identified by is olive-green upperparts, white underparts with bold black streaks, yellow vent and red eyes.

Orange-bellied Flowerpecker.Name: Orange-bellied Flowerpecker
Orange-bellied Flowerpecker.Description: Males have a beautiful blue and orange-yellow plumage, while females are duller green and yellow.

Scarlet-backed Flowerpecker.Name: Scarlet-backed Flowerpecker
Scarlet-backed Flowerpecker.Description: This common garden bird has a red crown and back, black upperparts and white underparts. Females are generally grey with a red rump.

Black-winged Flycatcher-Shrike.Name: Black-winged Flycatcher-Shrike
Black-winged Flycatcher-Shrike.Description: This rare species has black upperparts and white underparts.

Lesser Frigatebird.Name: Lesser Frigatebird
Lesser Frigatebird.Description: Males appear all black from below with small white underwing  "armpits" (spurs). Females have white belly patch, but less extensive than in Christmas Frigatebird females. In flight, it has a deeply forked tail and long pointed wings.

Christmas Frigatebird.Name: Christmas Frigatebird
Christmas Frigatebird.Description: Males have a diagnostic white belly patch contrasting with black underwing. Females have are extensively white on the underparts with prominent white underwing spurs and black patches on the side of the upper breast.

Short-tailed Shearwater.Name: Short-tailed Shearwater
Short-tailed Shearwater.Description: This seabird has a  sooty-brown plumage, a relatively short slender bill and fan-shaped tail.

Lanceolated Warbler.Name: Lanceolated Warbler
Lanceolated Warbler.Description: This small warbler is brown with pale undersides and prominent dark streaking on its breast, sides and vent.

Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler.Name: Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler
Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler.Description: Similar to the Lanceolated Warbler but with unstreaked rufous rump and lack of underpart streaks.

Greater Painted Snipe.Name: Greater Painted Snipe
Greater Painted Snipe.Description: Females more colourful than males with chestnut head and breast and white eye patch. Males have a yellowish eye patch and are grey-brown on the head and breast.

Little Grebe.Name: Little Grebe
Little Grebe.Description: This waterbird has a rusty brown neck and cheeks, yellow eyes and black cap. Non-breeding birds have their rusty-brown areas fade to a duller brown.

White-chested Babbler.Name: White-chested Babbler
White-chested Babbler.Description: A small plain bird with brown upperparts and white underparts

Abbott's Babbler.Name: Abbott's Babbler
Abbott's Babbler.Description: Similar to the Short-tailed babbler with brown upperparts, white breast and rusty belly. Can be distinguished by lack of black moustache of latter and longer tail. Grey on head less extensive than Short-tailed.

Short-tailed Babbler.Name: Short-tailed Babbler
Short-tailed Babbler.Description: The Short-tailed babbler has  brown upperparts, a pale eyebrow, whitish breast and rufous belly and vent. Has more intensely coloured grey head than Abbott's Babbler and black moustache. Tail is very short.

Roseate Tern.Name: Roseate Tern
Roseate Tern.Description: This tern has a distinctly long white tail and bright red legs in breeding birds. In the winter, they have a black cap, bill and legs. Distinguished from Common Tern by white underwing which lacks any black trailing edge.

Black-naped Tern.Name: Black-naped Tern
Black-naped Tern.Description: This tern is easily identified with its black nape on a generally whitish plumage.

Common Tern.Name: Common Tern
Common Tern.Description: Similar to the Roseate Tern in non-breeding plumage but its underwing is greyish with black trailing edge.

Whiskered Tern.Name: Whiskered Tern
Whiskered Tern.Description: This small tern may be confused with the White-winged tern in non-breeding plumage, but has a grey rump, black-streaked white crown and facial markings which do not extend below the eye.

Lesser Black-backed Gull.Name: Lesser Black-backed Gull
Lesser Black-backed Gull.Description: This species has a white head and underparts and grey upperparts. Juveniles are a mottled grey.

Brown-headed Gull.Name: Brown-headed Gull
Brown-headed Gull.Description: Has a brown head and looks similar to the Black-headed gull but has a thicker bill and neck and diagnostic black wing tips in flight.

Black-headed Gull.Name: Black-headed Gull
Black-headed Gull.Description: Breeding adults have a dark-brown hood and reddish bill. Birds in winter plumage have a black ear spot and a reddish bill with a black tip.

Gull-billed Tern.Name: Gull-billed Tern
Gull-billed Tern.Description: So called for possessing a gull-like bill. Breeding adults have a black cap from forehead to nape, while non-breeding adults have a black patch on their ear coverts.

Caspian Tern.Name: Caspian Tern
Caspian Tern.Description: This tern has a black cap and red bill. Non-breeding indivduals have a streaked cap.

Lesser Crested Tern.Name: Lesser Crested Tern
Lesser Crested Tern.Description: This species has a black cap extending to the bill, which is reduced to the area around the nape in non-breeders. Has white underparts and a bright orange bill.

Greater Crested Tern.Name: Greater Crested Tern
Greater Crested Tern.Description: Distinguished from Lesser Crested Tern by larger size and dull yellow bill.

Little Tern.Name: Little Tern
Little Tern.Description: This is the smallest tern in Singapore and therefore easily recognised. In breeding plumage, it has a white forehead on a black cap, which becomes more extensively white in winter. Breeding birds have yellow bill with black tip.

Aleutian Tern.Name: Aleutian Tern
Aleutian Tern.Description: In breeding plumage, the Aleutian tern has  a black crown and nape and eye-stripe, which becomes paler in winter. It can be recognised by its black trailing edge on underwing secondaries (i.e. the tip of the rear flight feathers closest to the bird’s body).

Bridled Tern.Name: Bridled Tern
Bridled Tern.Description: Dark brownish-grey upperparts with white underparts, flight feathers are dark and form a dark trailing edge in flight/

White-winged Tern.Name: White-winged Tern
White-winged Tern.Description: This small tern may be confused with the Whiskered tern in non-breeding plumage, but has a white rump and distinct facial markings reminiscent of headphones which extend below the eye.

Little Egret.Name: Little Egret
Little Egret.Description: This all-white egret can be differentiated from the others by its black bill and black legs with yellow feet.

Chinese Egret.Name: Chinese Egret
Chinese Egret.Description: In non-breeding plumage, this egret can be differentiated from other similar egrets by a combination of features, greenish facial skin, thick dagger-like bill, greenish-yellow legs and feet, two-tone bill (black towards tip and yellow towards base). Moves very actively when feeding, which is a characteristic behaviour for this egret.

Pacific Reef Heron.Name: Pacific Reef Heron
Pacific Reef Heron.Description: This species has both a dark morph, which is unmistakably slate-grey, and a light morph, which is white. Light morph has thick greenish legs and feet, yellowish bill and appears shorter-legged than other white egrets.

Grey Heron.Name: Grey Heron
Grey Heron.Description: This tall bird has a light grey plumage with a black stripe above its eyes and black stripes on its neck.

Great-billed Heron.Name: Great-billed Heron
Great-billed Heron.Description: This heron gets its name from its large bill and is the tallest bird in Singapore at  115cm. It has dark grey plumage with pale streaks on its wings and neck.

Purple Heron.Name: Purple Heron
Purple Heron.Description: This heron can be easily identified by its rusty red neck and purplish grey plumage.

Chinese Pond Heron.Name: Chinese Pond Heron
Chinese Pond Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a brown head and breast, black back and white belly and wings. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Javan Pond Heron.Name: Javan Pond Heron
Javan Pond Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a pale rufous head, brown breast, black back. and white belly. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Black-crowned Night Heron.Name: Black-crowned Night Heron
Black-crowned Night Heron.Description: This distinctive heron has a black crown and back, red eyes and white underparts.

Malayan Night Heron.Name: Malayan Night Heron
Malayan Night Heron.Description: This heron has a black crown and reddish-brown plumage with streaked underparts. Juveniles have mottled brown upperparts with numerous white spots and black barring on  their underparts.

Yellow Bittern.Name: Yellow Bittern
Yellow Bittern.Description: A shy bird that is often found in pondside vegetation, the Yellow Bittern can be identified by the contrast between its yellowish brown wing coverts and black flight feathers in flight.

Von Schrenck's Bittern.Name: Von Schrenck's Bittern
Von Schrenck's Bittern.Description: The male of this species has chesnut upperparts and pale underparts, while the females have numerous white spots on brown upperparts and are boldly streaked on their underparts.

Cinnamon Bittern.Name: Cinnamon Bittern
Cinnamon Bittern.Description: This species has cinnamon upperparts with streaked underparts, and appears uniformly reddish-brown in flight.

Black Bittern.Name: Black Bittern
Black Bittern.Description: The black bittern is so called for its dark upperparts and underparts which are streaked with white.

Great Egret.Name: Great Egret
Great Egret.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill and black legs, and can be differentiated from other similar egrets by its large size and prominent kink in its long S-shaped neck.

Intermediate Egret.Name: Intermediate Egret
Intermediate Egret.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill with a black tip and black legs and feet. Its S-shaped neck is roughly equal to its body length.

Eastern Cattle Egret.Name: Eastern Cattle Egret
Eastern Cattle Egret.Description: Easter cattle egrets are white with a rufous head and breast. In non-breeding plumage, it is completely white and can be differentiated by its small size.

Striated Heron.Name: Striated Heron
Striated Heron.Description: A small heron with dark crown, grey mantle and underparts and yellowish legs. It can be confused with the Black-crowned Night Heron.

Indian Pond Heron.Name: Indian Pond Heron
Indian Pond Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a pale brown head, neck and breast, white throat and belly, and dark maroon-brown back. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Oriental Pied Hornbill.Name: Oriental Pied Hornbill
Oriental Pied Hornbill.Description: This large striking bird was once rare in Singapore, but local populations have increased after a successful re-introduction programme. They can be found outside forests as well.

Glossy Ibis.Name: Glossy Ibis
Glossy Ibis.Description: This tall bird is unmistakable with its characteristic long down-curved bill. It has a rusty brown head and underparts and glossy black upperparts.

Common Iora.Name: Common Iora
Common Iora.Description: Males have black upperparts and yellow underparts, while females have olive-green upperparts and yellow underparts. Two white wing bars distinctive in both sexes

Pheasant-tailed Jacana.Name: Pheasant-tailed Jacana
Pheasant-tailed Jacana.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has a long prominent tail from which it gets its name from. In non-breeding plumage, it has white underparts, a black breast band, yellow hindneck, black neck-line and brown upperparts.

Pomarine Jaeger.Name: Pomarine Jaeger
Pomarine Jaeger.Description: The Pomarine Jaeger is more bulky than the Parasitic  Jawger with generally broader wings It has has diagnostic spoon-shaped tail feathers that are sometimes visible in immatures as well.

Parasitic Jaeger.Name: Parasitic Jaeger
Parasitic Jaeger.Description: Adults have pointed tail streamers while juveniles have pointed central tail feathers. Generally more compact that Pomarine Jaeger with a more streamlined flight profile.

Long-tailed Jaeger.Name: Long-tailed Jaeger
Long-tailed Jaeger.Description: This species of jaeger is smallest and greyest of the three and has a distinctly long tail. Adults of this species lack the white flashes on the wings compared to the other two jaeger species.

Common Kingfisher.Name: Common Kingfisher
Common Kingfisher.Description: Common Kingfishers can usually be seen perching just above the water's edge. They migrate south to countries like Singapore where they spend the winter months.

Blue-eared Kingfisher.Name: Blue-eared Kingfisher
Blue-eared Kingfisher.Description: This species is similar to the Common Kingfisher but has a deeper blue blue plumage. It is a resident species.

Stork-billed Kingfisher.Name: Stork-billed Kingfisher
Stork-billed Kingfisher.Description: This large kingfisher gets its name from its strong large bill which calls to mind a stork's bill.

Ruddy Kingfisher.Name: Ruddy Kingfisher
Ruddy Kingfisher.Description: This species is easy to recognise as it has a pinkish-brown plumage and red bill.

White-throated Kingfisher.Name: White-throated Kingfisher
White-throated Kingfisher.Description: A common species in Singapore, this bird can be recognised by the white-breast and throat on its otherwise brown underparts.

Black-capped Kingfisher.Name: Black-capped Kingfisher
Black-capped Kingfisher.Description: This species has a characteristic black cap, as well as a red bill and legs.

Oriental Dwarf Kingfisher.Name: Oriental Dwarf Kingfisher
Oriental Dwarf Kingfisher.Description: Also known as the Black-backed Kingfisher, this small kingfisher has blue-black wings along with a distinct purplish-pink crown and rump. Underparts are orange.

Collared Kingfisher.Name: Collared Kingfisher
Collared Kingfisher.Description: This common species has a turquoise cap, wings back and tail, and a white collar and underparts.

Jerdon's Baza.Name: Jerdon's Baza
Jerdon's Baza.Description: This species has a white-tipped black crest, brown upperparts and rufous bands on its underparts. When viewed from below, it shows shows distinct black bars on flight feathers (i.e. wing tips).

Black Baza.Name: Black Baza
Black Baza.Description: As with the Jerdon's Baza, this species has a black crest as well, but has black upperparts, white underparts with brown bands and a black breast band. In flight, grey patches visible on underwing.

Bat Hawk.Name: Bat Hawk
Bat Hawk.Description: Generally black with a white throat and vent and pale legs, and has bright yellow eyes with white “spectacles” aroud it.

Black-winged Kite.Name: Black-winged Kite
Black-winged Kite.Description: This kite has grey upperparts and white underparts and head, a black shoulder patch, as well as red eyes. When viewed from below, the outer half of the wings are dark

Black Kite.Name: Black Kite
Black Kite.Description: Looks similar to juvenile brahminy kites, can be recognised by its prominent forked tail.

Brahminy Kite.Name: Brahminy Kite
Brahminy Kite.Description: Easily recognished by its white head and chest and chestnut brown belly. One of the most common raptors in Singapore.

White-bellied Sea Eagle.Name: White-bellied Sea Eagle
White-bellied Sea Eagle.Description: This large raptor can be identified by its white underparts and mostly black wings.

Himalayan Vulture.Name: Himalayan Vulture
Himalayan Vulture.Description: This species is much larger than any other raptors seen in Singapore, and has much broader wings compared to the other raptors. They are heavily streaked on the underparts.

Short-toed Snake Eagle.Name: Short-toed Snake Eagle
Short-toed Snake Eagle.Description: This snake-eating eagle has a distinct brown head, and white underparts with black speckles and barring when viewed from below. Its wings are barred and black-tipped.

Crested Serpent Eagle.Name: Crested Serpent Eagle
Crested Serpent Eagle.Description: This bird is mostly brown and has a yellow patch between its eyes and beak. In flight, it can be recognised by a broad white band across the length of the wing bordered by black.

Western Marsh Harrier.Name: Western Marsh Harrier
Western Marsh Harrier.Description: Similar to the Eastern marsh harrier but female is less streaked and males have strong brown upperparts and underparts.

Eastern Marsh Harrier.Name: Eastern Marsh Harrier
Eastern Marsh Harrier.Description: Males streaked black on head, mantle and upper breast, lacks white wing patch, while in females, rufous thighs and vent distinctive.

Pied Harrier.Name: Pied Harrier
Pied Harrier.Description: Males have black heads, mantle and upper breast, a large white wing patch and white underparts. Females have white underparts, and grey and white streaked upperparts.

Crested Goshawk.Name: Crested Goshawk
Crested Goshawk.Description: This species has streaked breast contrasting sharply with dark bands on belly, and bold vertical throat stripe. In flight, comparatively long tail shows four dark tail bands.

Chinese Sparrowhawk.Name: Chinese Sparrowhawk
Chinese Sparrowhawk.Description: This is an easily identifiable species with its grey upperparts, mostly white underparts and rufous breast. In flight, wing tips are black and 4 "fingers" are visible.

Japanese Sparrowhawk.Name: Japanese Sparrowhawk
Japanese Sparrowhawk.Description: Might be confused with the Chinese Sparrowhawk, but lacks black wing tips and underparts are visibly barred. Has 5 "fingers" visible in flight.

Besra.Name: Besra
Besra.Description: Similar to the Japanese Sparrowhawk but with bold mesial stripe in all plumages and bands in underwing are thicker.

Grey-faced Buzzard.Name: Grey-faced Buzzard
Grey-faced Buzzard.Description: This species has brown upperparts and breast, barred underparts, grey head-sides  and banded tail.

Common Buzzard.Name: Common Buzzard
Common Buzzard.Description: Plumage of this raptor can be variable but is generally brown above with buffy underparts and a brown belly patch. In flight, it has black tips to flight feathers and black trailing edges along the length of its wings.

Steppe Eagle.Name: Steppe Eagle
Steppe Eagle.Description: May be confused with the Greater Spotted Eagle but is generally larger, paler and longer wings. When viewed from below, its wings are two-toned.

Booted Eagle.Name: Booted Eagle
Booted Eagle.Description: In flight, this species has pale or chestnut underparts with dark flight feathers. There is also a light morph which has diagnostic contrast between white underparts and underwing coverts and black primary and secondaries. Both morphs have white shoulder patches that look like headlights when viewed head-on.

Crested Honey Buzzard.Name: Crested Honey Buzzard
Crested Honey Buzzard.Description: Plumagen of this raptor can be highly variable but its flight shape is distinctive, featuring proportionally small, pigeon-like head, comparatively long tail and wings with 6 "fingers" in flight.

Grey-headed Fish Eagle.Name: Grey-headed Fish Eagle
Grey-headed Fish Eagle.Description: This species has a distinct white tail with black terminal band visible in flight. It also has a sharp demarcation between its brown breast and white belly.

Hen Harrier.Name: Hen Harrier
Hen Harrier.Description: Males are grey with white underparts and vent, while females can be distinguished from other harriers by streaked thighs and vent.

Greater Spotted Eagle.Name: Greater Spotted Eagle
Greater Spotted Eagle.Description: Has uniformly dark plumage with broad wings and a short tail. Juveniles have numerous large white spots on their wings.

Eastern Imperial Eagle.Name: Eastern Imperial Eagle
Eastern Imperial Eagle.Description: A very large eagle, with a straw-coloured crown and hindneck distinctive in adults, while juveniles have diagnostic broad white band across the underwing

Rufous-bellied Eagle.Name: Rufous-bellied Eagle
Rufous-bellied Eagle.Description: As its name suggests, it has a rusty-red belly, with a white breast and throat and dark brown upperparts. Juveniles are generally brown above and white below with distinctive white eye-brow and black face mask.

Changeable Hawk-Eagle.Name: Changeable Hawk-Eagle
Changeable Hawk-Eagle.Description: This species has a light and dark morph. Compared to Crested Honey Buzzard, has a bulging trailing edge and 7 "fingers" in flight, shorter tail and feathered legs.

Blyth's Hawk-Eagle.Name: Blyth's Hawk-Eagle
Blyth's Hawk-Eagle.Description: This striking raptor has a characteristic black and white plumage and back crest. Its belly is banded and wings has barring. Can be distinguished from all other hawk-eagles by broad white band on otherwise dark tail.

Shikra.Name: Shikra
Shikra.Description: A small raptor with brown plumage and barrings on its breast and belly, and a greyish head and back.

White-crested Laughingthrush.Name: White-crested Laughingthrush
White-crested Laughingthrush.Description: An unmistakable bird with its white crest and breast, black mask and rich brown upperparts.

Chinese Hwamei.Name: Chinese Hwamei
Chinese Hwamei.Description: With its distinctive white spectacles and eye-stripe, this bird is a popular cagebird due to its fantastic singing ability. Escapees have established themselves in several areas throughout Singapore.

Dusky Warbler.Name: Dusky Warbler
Dusky Warbler.Description: A ashy brown warbler with pale underparts that can be identified by its bold white eyebrow.

Yellow-browed Warbler.Name: Yellow-browed Warbler
Yellow-browed Warbler.Description: This rare warbler has olive-brown upperparts and yellowish eyebrow. It has two distinct whitish bars and lack of a crown stripe.

Arctic Warbler.Name: Arctic Warbler
Arctic Warbler.Description: Arctic Warbler differs from Eastern Crowned Warbler by having a white, not yellow, vent and lacks a crown stripe.

Eastern Crowned Warbler.Name: Eastern Crowned Warbler
Eastern Crowned Warbler.Description: This warbler species can be discerned from the other warblers by its dinstinctive pale crown stripe and yellow vent.

Sakhalin Leaf Warbler.Name: Sakhalin Leaf Warbler
Sakhalin Leaf Warbler.Description: Greyish crown contrasts with olive-brown upperparts with long, thin white supercilium that contrasts sharply with dark eyestripe; underparts whitish with flesh-coloured legs.

Greater Green Leafbird.Name: Greater Green Leafbird
Greater Green Leafbird.Description: This bird has an all-green plumage, with a black face and throat for males, and yellow eye-ring and throat for females.

Blue-winged Leafbird.Name: Blue-winged Leafbird
Blue-winged Leafbird.Description: The most easily identified leafbird due to blue patches on the wings and tail in both sexes. Both sexes also have a yellow cap.

Lesser Green Leafbird.Name: Lesser Green Leafbird
Lesser Green Leafbird.Description: Similar to the Greater Green Leafbird but is smaller in size with a slimmer bill. Males have a smaller black mask and females lack yellow eyering and throat.

Red Avadavat.Name: Red Avadavat
Red Avadavat.Description: A tiny stout bird with a thick  bill. Males are bright red with white spots on its flank, while females are brown with a red rump.

White-rumped Munia.Name: White-rumped Munia
White-rumped Munia.Description: Has dark brown plumage with a white belly and rump. Upperparts streaked white.

Javan Munia.Name: Javan Munia
Javan Munia.Description: Similar to the White-rumped munia except that it lacks the white-rump. Upperparts unstreaked.

Scaly-breasted Munia.Name: Scaly-breasted Munia
Scaly-breasted Munia.Description: This bird gets its common name from the scaling on its breast. Has a dark brown head and upperparts.

White-headed Munia.Name: White-headed Munia
White-headed Munia.Description: Has a white head and throat, which distinguishes it from the similar White-capped munia.

Chestnut Munia.Name: Chestnut Munia
Chestnut Munia.Description: Easily recognised by its entirely black head and chesnut brown body.

Large-tailed Nightjar.Name: Large-tailed Nightjar
Large-tailed Nightjar.Description: This species has bold dark streaks on its upperparts and has a long tail.

Savanna Nightjar.Name: Savanna Nightjar
Savanna Nightjar.Description: Can be distinguished from the Large-tailed Nightjar by its slimmer body and lack of black streaks on its upperparts

Malaysian Eared Nightjar.Name: Malaysian Eared Nightjar
Malaysian Eared Nightjar.Description: Distinguished from other nightjars by long-tailed appearance in flight recalling a small raptor. At rest appears uniformly brown and ear tufts are sometimes visible.

Grey Nightjar.Name: Grey Nightjar
Grey Nightjar.Description: Has a darker and greyer plumage than the other nightjars. They are frequently encountered roosting in trees.

House Sparrow.Name: House Sparrow
House Sparrow.Description: While similar to the common Eurasian Tree Sparrow, this rare introduced species can be distinguished by its gray crown and lack of black cheek spot.

Eurasian Tree Sparrow.Name: Eurasian Tree Sparrow
Eurasian Tree Sparrow.Description: This common species has a brown cap and prominent black patches on its cheeks and chin.

Black-naped Oriole.Name: Black-naped Oriole
Black-naped Oriole.Description: This common garden bird is unmistakable with its bright yellow plumage, black nape and wings, and pink bill.

Western Osprey.Name: Western Osprey
Western Osprey.Description: This fish-eating raptor has brown upperparts and grey-white underparts and head. It also has a black eye stripe and brown breast band.

Oriental Scops Owl.Name: Oriental Scops Owl
Oriental Scops Owl.Description: May be confused with the Sunda Scops Owl but it is smaller, underparts generally contain more white and has bright yellow eyes.

Buffy Fish Owl.Name: Buffy Fish Owl
Buffy Fish Owl.Description: This large owl has prominent ear tufts, a sharp grey beak and large yellow eyes. It is often found near water as it mainly preys on fish.

Spotted Wood Owl.Name: Spotted Wood Owl
Spotted Wood Owl.Description: The spotted wood owl can be identified by its rusty-brown face with large dark eyes and dark beak. Might be confused with the Brown Wood Owl which has a dark outline around its face.

Brown Wood Owl.Name: Brown Wood Owl
Brown Wood Owl.Description: This large owl can be recognised by its paler facial disc which contrasts against its dark head, and has also dark “spectacles” around its eyes.

Brown Hawk-Owl.Name: Brown Hawk-Owl
Brown Hawk-Owl.Description: This owl has white underparts with distinct heart-shaped spots and a brown head.

Short-eared Owl.Name: Short-eared Owl
Short-eared Owl.Description: A distinctive owl with straw-brown upperparts and underparts which are boldly streaked. Unlike most owls, it is active in the daytime as well.

Sunda Scops Owl.Name: Sunda Scops Owl
Sunda Scops Owl.Description: May be confused with the Oriental Scops Owl but it is larger, underparts are generally brownish and eyes are dark brown/orange.

Barred Eagle-Owl.Name: Barred Eagle-Owl
Barred Eagle-Owl.Description: This striking bird has large ear tufts and yellow beak. As its name suggests, it has prominent barring on most of its body.

Northern Boobook.Name: Northern Boobook
Northern Boobook.Description: Similar to Brown Hawk-owl but has large yellow eyes and vertical, not heart-shaped streaks, on its underparts

Blue-rumped Parrot.Name: Blue-rumped Parrot
Blue-rumped Parrot.Description: Males of this species have a blue head while females have a brown head.

Blue-crowned Hanging Parrot.Name: Blue-crowned Hanging Parrot
Blue-crowned Hanging Parrot.Description: Males of this species have a generally green with a red breast patch and blue spot on its crown. Females lack the red breast patch.

Rose-ringed Parakeet.Name: Rose-ringed Parakeet
Rose-ringed Parakeet.Description: Male Rose-ringed Parakeets have a thin red and black ring around their necks which females lack.

Red-breasted Parakeet.Name: Red-breasted Parakeet
Red-breasted Parakeet.Description: Males of this species have a red/pink beak, while females have a black beak.

Long-tailed Parakeet.Name: Long-tailed Parakeet
Long-tailed Parakeet.Description: This species has an exceptionally long tail, and can be idneitifed by its red/pink head and green cap.

Coconut Lorikeet.Name: Coconut Lorikeet
Coconut Lorikeet.Description: This colourful bird can be easily identified from its bright red beak, green plumage and yellow nape.

Black-and-red Broadbill.Name: Black-and-red Broadbill
Black-and-red Broadbill.Description: This bird has black-and-red plumage, white wing stripe and a large broad bill. The upper mandible is bright blue, while the lower mandible is yellow.

Red Junglefowl.Name: Red Junglefowl
Red Junglefowl.Description: This nationally-threatened species is one of the main ancestral species of the domestic chicken. It is able to interbreed with domestic chickens.

King Quail.Name: King Quail
King Quail.Description: Males have a black and white face with bluish sides and chestnut belly. Females are uniformly brown.

Red Turtle Dove.Name: Red Turtle Dove
Red Turtle Dove.Description: This dove has a black line on its nape and a grey head. Males appear more rusty-brown, while females are  grey-brown.

Common Emerald Dove.Name: Common Emerald Dove
Common Emerald Dove.Description: This dove can be easily identified by its emerald-green wings.

Zebra Dove.Name: Zebra Dove
Zebra Dove.Description: This dove may be confused with the Spotted Dove but has a striped neck and has a slimmer build.

Cinnamon-headed Green Pigeon.Name: Cinnamon-headed Green Pigeon
Cinnamon-headed Green Pigeon.Description: As its name suggests, the males of the Cinnamon-headed Green Pigeon has a cinnamon coloured head. Females have a green head instead.

Little Green Pigeon.Name: Little Green Pigeon
Little Green Pigeon.Description: This colourful bird has an orange breast , grey head, maroon wings and green belly. Females are mostly green. It is considerably smaller than the Pink-necked Green Pigeon.

Pink-necked Green Pigeon.Name: Pink-necked Green Pigeon
Pink-necked Green Pigeon.Description: Similar colouration to the Little Green Pigeon but males have a pink neck and green wings, and are much larger. Females are mostly green.

Thick-billed Green Pigeon.Name: Thick-billed Green Pigeon
Thick-billed Green Pigeon.Description: This pigeon has a thicker bill compared to the other pigeon species, and also has a distinct green eye-ring. Males have maroon wings, while females are a duller green.

Jambu Fruit Dove.Name: Jambu Fruit Dove
Jambu Fruit Dove.Description: Males are easily identifiable by their white underparts and distinct pink breast patch. Females are dark green with a pale belly.

Green Imperial Pigeon.Name: Green Imperial Pigeon
Green Imperial Pigeon.Description: This large pigeon has a distinct chestnut-coloured vent, and has a grey head and underparts and dark green wings and upperparts.

Mountain Imperial Pigeon.Name: Mountain Imperial Pigeon
Mountain Imperial Pigeon.Description: Similar to the Green Imperial Pigeon but has creamy vent and grey tail bands.

Pied Imperial Pigeon.Name: Pied Imperial Pigeon
Pied Imperial Pigeon.Description: An unmistakable large pigeon which has a striking black and white plumage.

Rock Dove.Name: Rock Dove
Rock Dove.Description: This urban bird typically appears grey, but can include brown, black and white morphs.

Spotted Dove.Name: Spotted Dove
Spotted Dove.Description: This dove may be confused with the Zebra Dove but has a spotted neck and is larger.

Oriental Turtle-Dove.Name: Oriental Turtle-Dove
Oriental Turtle-Dove.Description: Dark brown plumage, with distinct black and white markings on neck. Rufous scaling on its wings gave rise to its common name.

Hooded Pitta.Name: Hooded Pitta
Hooded Pitta.Description: This striking bird has a black head with brown cap, green body and red vent.

Mangrove Pitta.Name: Mangrove Pitta
Mangrove Pitta.Description: Similar to the Blue-Winged Pitta, but has a more robust bill and brown supercilium is much thinner.

Blue-winged Pitta.Name: Blue-winged Pitta
Blue-winged Pitta.Description: This colourful pitta has a black head with pale crown and collar, rufous underparts, red vent, green upperparts and blue wings.

Pacific Golden Plover.Name: Pacific Golden Plover
Pacific Golden Plover.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has a black face and undersides bordered by a white line, and upperparts  are black and gold. In non-breeding plumage, the  bird is mottled golden-brown, and white plumage is restricted to belly, though not particularly distinct.

Grey Plover.Name: Grey Plover
Grey Plover.Description: As the name suggests, this plover has a grey plumage. In breeding season, it has a black face and underparts, which become pale in winter. Its key diagnostic feature is its  black “armpits” on underside of wings which is visible in flight.

Little Ringed Plover.Name: Little Ringed Plover
Little Ringed Plover.Description: This small plover has brown upperparts, white underparts, a black breast band and distinct yellow eyering. It can be confused with the Common Ringed Plover, but has a yellow eye ring.

Kentish Plover.Name: Kentish Plover
Kentish Plover.Description: This plover has white underparts and brown upperparts, and black legs and bill. Unlike both Lesser and Greater Sand Plovers, it has a complete white neck collar.

Malaysian Plover.Name: Malaysian Plover
Malaysian Plover.Description: Males have a black “collar” which in females is rufous. This distinguishes them from non-breeding Kentish Plover.

Lesser Sand Plover.Name: Lesser Sand Plover
Lesser Sand Plover.Description: In breeding plumage, this plover has a rusty breast and black band over its eyes. In non-breeding plumage, the plover has brown upperparts and white underparts.

Greater Sand Plover.Name: Greater Sand Plover
Greater Sand Plover.Description: Similar to the Lesser Sand Plover but is larger, has longer, greenish-yellow legs and a more robust bill.

Oriental Plover.Name: Oriental Plover
Oriental Plover.Description: In breeding plumage, this species has a chestnut breast band with black border and white face and belly. In winter, it has brown upperparts and pale underparts.

Grey-headed Lapwing.Name: Grey-headed Lapwing
Grey-headed Lapwing.Description: This large lapwing has a grey head, neck and upper breast, black breastband and brown upperparts and white belly.

Red-wattled Lapwing.Name: Red-wattled Lapwing
Red-wattled Lapwing.Description: The Red-Wattled Lapwing has a striking black head and breast, white belly, brown upperparts and red beak. It also has a distinct white ear patch.

Oriental Pratincole.Name: Oriental Pratincole
Oriental Pratincole.Description: Resembling an oversized swallow, this bird has a black mark under its eyes that borders the throat.

Small Pratincole.Name: Small Pratincole
Small Pratincole.Description: The Small Prantincole has a white eye-ring and a generally grey plumage with whitish underparts. It has distinctive white wing bars on upperwing and underwing area visible in flight which the Oriental Pratincole lacks.

Red-legged Crake.Name: Red-legged Crake
