Red-legged Crake.Description: This small waterbird gets its name from its bright red legs. Adults also have a distinctive chestnut head and breast and black and white barring on their underparts.

Slaty-legged Crake.Name: Slaty-legged Crake
Slaty-legged Crake.Description: Similar to the Red-legged Crake except for grey legs and lacks the whitish spots on its wings.

Slaty-breasted Rail.Name: Slaty-breasted Rail
Slaty-breasted Rail.Description: This rail has grey underparts and dark mottled upperparts. Crown and nape are chestnut, while bill is red.

White-breasted Waterhen.Name: White-breasted Waterhen
White-breasted Waterhen.Description: This common waterbird has a white face and breast, and blackish upperparts and brown vent.

Ruddy-breasted Crake.Name: Ruddy-breasted Crake
Ruddy-breasted Crake.Description: This crake has a rusty-red breast, head and belly, and a black and white barred vent.

White-browed Crake.Name: White-browed Crake
White-browed Crake.Description: The White-browed crake is easily recognised by the two white stripes above and below its eyes.

Watercock.Name: Watercock
Watercock.Description: When in breeding plumage, this water bird is black with a bright red facial shield.  Females and males in non-breeding plumage is a duller mottled brown.

Common Moorhen.Name: Common Moorhen
Common Moorhen.Description: The Common Moorhen is largely black with a prominent red bill with yellow tip. Adults  have a red frontal shield.

Eurasian Coot.Name: Eurasian Coot
Eurasian Coot.Description: Similar to the Common Moorhen except that its shield and beak are white.

Baillons Crake.Name: Baillons Crake
Baillons Crake.Description: This crake has a white, brown and black mottled plumage, with a greenish bill and legs.

Black-backed Swamphen.Name: Black-backed Swamphen
Black-backed Swamphen.Description: This bird can be easily identified by its brilliant purple-blue plumage and red bill, facial shield and legs.

Band-bellied Crake.Name: Band-bellied Crake
Band-bellied Crake.Description: Dull brown upperparts, rufous breast and black belly with white bars.

Black-browed Reed Warbler.Name: Black-browed Reed Warbler
Black-browed Reed Warbler.Description: Named after its distinct black eyebrow, the Black-browed reed warbler has brown upperparts and pale underparts.

Oriental Reed Warbler.Name: Oriental Reed Warbler
Oriental Reed Warbler.Description: This large warbler may be confused with the smaller Black-browed reed warbler, but can generally be distinguished by the lack of a dark eyebrow.

Booted Warbler.Name: Booted Warbler
Booted Warbler.Description: Pale brown head and upperparts, and pale underparts. Note also long, white supercilium that fades behind the eye.

Oriental Dollarbird.Name: Oriental Dollarbird
Oriental Dollarbird.Description: This bird has two white circular patches under its wings, which are visible when in flight.

Eurasian Woodcock.Name: Eurasian Woodcock
Eurasian Woodcock.Description: This species has a reddish-brown upperparts and cream underparts that help it camouflage in woodlands.

Pin-tailed Snipe.Name: Pin-tailed Snipe
Pin-tailed Snipe.Description: Only reliable way to differentiate between the two is by the shape of the outer tail feathers. In Pin-tailed Snipes, the outer eight pairs of tail feathers (sometimes six to nine pairs) are very thin (all less than 2mm wide) while in Swinhoe’s the outermost pair is narrowest (between 2 to 4mm), and subsequent tail feathers becoming increasingly broader towards the center. However, this feature is exceptionally difficult to observe in the field.

Swinhoe's Snipe.Name: Swinhoe's Snipe
Swinhoe's Snipe.Description: Only reliable way to differentiate between the two is by the shape of the outer tail feathers. In Pin-tailed Snipes, the outer eight pairs of tail feathers (sometimes six to nine pairs) are very thin (all less than 2mm wide) while in Swinhoe’s the outermost pair is narrowest (between 2 to 4mm), and subsequent tail feathers becoming increasingly broader towards the center. However, this feature is exceptionally difficult to observe in the field.

Common Snipe.Name: Common Snipe
Common Snipe.Description: In flight, white trailing edge to secondaries distinctive and unique among all local snipes; underwing coverts (i.e. armpits) generally white and unbarred. At rest, from “Swintail” snipes by white only on outer edge of scapular feathers.

Black-tailed Godwit.Name: Black-tailed Godwit
Black-tailed Godwit.Description: Similar to the Bar-tailed Godwit, except that its bill is straight, and has white wing bars (mainly visible in flight) and black tail bands. In breeding plumage, this bird has a rufous coloured head and breast.

Bar-tailed Godwit.Name: Bar-tailed Godwit
Bar-tailed Godwit.Description: Similar to the Black-tailed Godwit, except that its bill is slightly upturned, and lacks white wing bars and black tail bands.

Little Curlew.Name: Little Curlew
Little Curlew.Description: The Little Curlew has a black stripe across its head, a slightly down-curved beak, brown upperparts and pale underparts. Its bill is comparatively fine relative to that of the Whimbrel.

Whimbrel.Name: Whimbrel
Whimbrel.Description: Similar to the Little Curlew but has a larger and with a longer bill.

Eurasian Curlew.Name: Eurasian Curlew
Eurasian Curlew.Description: The Eurasian Curlew has a long down-curved bil and can be distinguished from the Far Eastern Curlew by its white rump and underwing coverts (i.e. armpits; mainly seen in flight).

Far Eastern Curlew.Name: Far Eastern Curlew
Far Eastern Curlew.Description: Similar to the Eurasian Curlew but has a longer bill and heavier streaking on its underparts.

Spotted Redshank.Name: Spotted Redshank
Spotted Redshank.Description: The Spotted Redshank has a longer and finer bill than Common Redshank, and lacks white wing patch in flight. In breeding plumage,it is all black with numerous white spots on upperparts.

Common Redshank.Name: Common Redshank
Common Redshank.Description: The Common Redshank has shorter legs and bill compared to the Spotted redshank, and as has prominent white wing patches (in flight).

Marsh Sandpiper.Name: Marsh Sandpiper
Marsh Sandpiper.Description: This waterbird has greyish upperparts and white underparts, greenish-yellow legs and a thin black bill.

Common Greenshank.Name: Common Greenshank
Common Greenshank.Description: So called for its greenish long legs, the Common Greenshank can be differentiated from the Marsh Sandpiper by its larger size and slightly upturned bill.

Nordmann's Greenshank.Name: Nordmann's Greenshank
Nordmann's Greenshank.Description: The Nordmann's Greenshank may be confused with the Common Greenshank, but has shorter, yellow legs and a characteristic two-tone bill which is paler at the base and darker towards the tip.

Green Sandpiper.Name: Green Sandpiper
Green Sandpiper.Description: Has less spotting on upperparts and dark underwing compared to Wood Sandpiper; can also be distinguished from Common Sandpiper by larger size and white rump.

Wood Sandpiper.Name: Wood Sandpiper
Wood Sandpiper.Description: Looks similar to the Green Sandpiper but distinguished by the whitish patches on its underwing and distinctly more white spotting on its upperparts.

Grey-tailed Tattler.Name: Grey-tailed Tattler
Grey-tailed Tattler.Description: This species has a prominent white eyebrow and yellow legs. Breast is greyish while belly is white.

Ruddy Turnstone.Name: Ruddy Turnstone
Ruddy Turnstone.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has rusty-brown upperparts, which becomes a dull grey-brown in winter. Legs are a distinct orange.

Asian Dowitcher.Name: Asian Dowitcher
Asian Dowitcher.Description: In breeding plumage, the Asian Dowitcher has reddish brown upperparts, which becomes a dull grey in winter. Unlike the Godwits, its bill is uniformly black.

Great Knot.Name: Great Knot
Great Knot.Description: The Great Knot has brown streaky upperparts and white underparts. It has distinctive black spots on its breast.

Sanderling.Name: Sanderling
Sanderling.Description: In breeding plumage, the Sanderling has brown upperparts and white underparts. In non-breeding plumage, upperparts are greyish. It has a short black bill and legs.

Red-necked Stint.Name: Red-necked Stint
Red-necked Stint.Description: This species gets its name from its reddish neck when it is in breeding plumage. In winter, its neck is pale.

Temminck's Stint.Name: Temminck's Stint
Temminck's Stint.Description: Temminck's stint have brown upperparts and white underparts, a black beak and yellow legs.

Long-toed Stint.Name: Long-toed Stint
Long-toed Stint.Description: This stint has a long neck with short black bill and yellow legs. In non-breeding plumage, upperparts are greyish brown, and underparts white.

Sharp-tailed Sandpiper.Name: Sharp-tailed Sandpiper
Sharp-tailed Sandpiper.Description: May be confused with the Pectoral Sandpiper but has a strong contrast between rufous crown and white eyebrow, and has streaks on flanks.

Curlew Sandpiper.Name: Curlew Sandpiper
Curlew Sandpiper.Description: The Curlew Sandpiper has a relatively long, decurved bill and rusty-red underparts during the breeding season, which become pale in winter.

Broad-billed Sandpiper.Name: Broad-billed Sandpiper
Broad-billed Sandpiper.Description: This sandpiper has a broad bill that droops at the tip and a prominent split eyebrow (supercilium).

Ruff.Name: Ruff
Ruff.Description: Males of this species are larger than the females, and in breeding plumage have  brightly coloured head tufts. In winter, both males and females are grey-brown upperparts and white underparts.

Red-necked Phalarope.Name: Red-necked Phalarope
Red-necked Phalarope.Description: In breeding plumage, this species has a rusty red neck, which becomes white in winter. Upperparts grey-brown and underparts white, and possesses a black eye-stripe. It is generally observed floating on a water body like a tiny duck.

Terek Sandpiper.Name: Terek Sandpiper
Terek Sandpiper.Description: This sandpiper has a dark upcurved bill and short orangey-yellow legs.

Common Sandpiper.Name: Common Sandpiper
Common Sandpiper.Description: The Common Sandpiper feeds with a distinct tail-bobbing movement.

Spoon-billed Sandpiper.Name: Spoon-billed Sandpiper
Spoon-billed Sandpiper.Description: This sandpiper has an unmistakeable spoon-shaped bill that sweeps from side to side on the mud to feed.

Beach Stone-curlew.Name: Beach Stone-curlew
Beach Stone-curlew.Description: This coastal bird has a characteristic stout black beak and robust yellow legs..

Tiger Shrike.Name: Tiger Shrike
Tiger Shrike.Description: Adults have a grey head, black face mask, barred chestnut upperparts and white underparts. The more commonly encountered immatures are chestnut above and white below with heavy barring on both upperparts and underparts.

Brown Shrike.Name: Brown Shrike
Brown Shrike.Description: Not similar to the Tiger Shrike. Adults have brown cap, white eye-brow above black face mask, unbarred brown upperparts and whitish underparts with a brownish wash.

Long-tailed Shrike.Name: Long-tailed Shrike
Long-tailed Shrike.Description: This large shrike has a long black tail which the other two species do not possess. Also differentiated from the other local shrikes by black wings and a white wing patch that is mainly visible in flight.

Java Sparrow.Name: Java Sparrow
Java Sparrow.Description: A striking bird with a large red beak and feet, black head with white cheek patch and grey body with pale belly.

Asian Glossy Starling.Name: Asian Glossy Starling
Asian Glossy Starling.Description: This bird is glossy dark green with red eyes is often seen in flocks. Juveniles are grey above and white below and covered in bold streaks.

Common Myna.Name: Common Myna
Common Myna.Description: Despite its name, it is less common than the White-vented myna. Distinguishable by its brown body and yellow eye-patch.

Javan Myna.Name: Javan Myna
Javan Myna.Description: The most common bird in Singapore, this species can be found in most urban areas.It has a black plumage, white vent and yellow beak.

Crested Myna.Name: Crested Myna
Crested Myna.Description: This is a rare myna that looks similar to the White-vented Myna that can be identified by its crest, red eyes and white barrings on vent.

Common Hill Myna.Name: Common Hill Myna
Common Hill Myna.Description: This large myna is black with a prominent orange bill and bare yellow patches of skin on head.

Daurian Starling.Name: Daurian Starling
Daurian Starling.Description: This bird is a creamy white with metallic green wings with a white wingbar.

White-shouldered Starling.Name: White-shouldered Starling
White-shouldered Starling.Description: This starling is mostly grey with a large white shoulder patch. It has white eyes.

Rosy Starling.Name: Rosy Starling
Rosy Starling.Description: This distinct bird has a rosy pink and black plumage. Juveniles are brown without the two toned plumage.

Black-winged Stilt.Name: Black-winged Stilt
Black-winged Stilt.Description: This bird has a needle-like bill and striking red legs, and black and white plumage.

Asian Openbill.Name: Asian Openbill
Asian Openbill.Description: This stork gets its common name from the gap in its large bill when closed. Uses bill to feed on favoured diet of snails.

Lesser Adjutant.Name: Lesser Adjutant
Lesser Adjutant.Description: This large stork has a distinct unfeathered neck and head, and has white underparts and dark grey upperparts.

Swinhoe's Storm Petrel.Name: Swinhoe's Storm Petrel
Swinhoe's Storm Petrel.Description: This seabird is entirely dark brown with a short forked tail.

Plain Sunbird.Name: Plain Sunbird
Plain Sunbird.Description: This rather dull looking sunbird has olive upperparts, greyish underparts and a short bill. Males have a dark blue patch at the base of their beak.

Brown-throated Sunbird.Name: Brown-throated Sunbird
Brown-throated Sunbird.Description: Males of this species have a beautiful metallic blue crown and back, brown throat and yellow underparts. Females are duller with olive upperparts and yellow underparts. Both sexes have red eyes, female also has distinct split yellow eye-ring.

Crimson Sunbird.Name: Crimson Sunbird
Crimson Sunbird.Description: With its bright red plumage (in males), this tiny bird is Singapore's unofficial national bird.

Thick-billed Spiderhunter.Name: Thick-billed Spiderhunter
Thick-billed Spiderhunter.Description: Similarly coloured to the Little Spiderhunter, but without a white throat. Has a split yellow eye-ring.

Yellow-eared Spiderhunter.Name: Yellow-eared Spiderhunter
Yellow-eared Spiderhunter.Description: This spiderhunter has a bright yellow eyering, ear coverts and underparts. The yellow on the eye-ring and ears is much brighter than that on the underparts.

Van Hasselt's Sunbird.Name: Van Hasselt's Sunbird
Van Hasselt's Sunbird.Description: Males have a metallic purple throat, green crown and deep red underparts. Females are duller olive and have white tips to tail feathers compared to female Crimson Sunbirds.

Copper-throated Sunbird.Name: Copper-throated Sunbird
Copper-throated Sunbird.Description: Males have a metallic green cap and wings, copper throat and purple-blue belly. Females have grey head and white throat, olive upper parts, yellow underparts and split white, not yellow, eye ring.

Olive-backed Sunbird.Name: Olive-backed Sunbird
Olive-backed Sunbird.Description: A commonly seen bird that has olive green upperparts and yellow underparts, with male birds possessing a metallic blue bib.

Little Spiderhunter.Name: Little Spiderhunter
Little Spiderhunter.Description: This small bird has a long downcurved bill, olive-brown upperparts, whitish throat and yellow underparts.

Sand Martin.Name: Sand Martin
Sand Martin.Description: This swallow has brown upperparts with white underparts, a brown band across its breast and a forked tail.

Barn Swallow.Name: Barn Swallow
Barn Swallow.Description: Similar to the Pacific Swallow but has a breast band. Other differences include clean white underparts and deeper tail fork.

Pacific Swallow.Name: Pacific Swallow
Pacific Swallow.Description: Similar to the Barn Swallow but has lacks a breast band. This species has glossy blue upperparts with orange forehead and throat and a forked tail. Underparts whitish with brownish flanks.

Asian House Martin.Name: Asian House Martin
Asian House Martin.Description: This species might look similar to the Sand Martin, but has a white rump and no breast  band. Also has glossy blue, not brown, upperparts.

Red-rumped Swallow.Name: Red-rumped Swallow
Red-rumped Swallow.Description: This swallow has a orangey-red rump and nape, and streaked underparts. Rump colour in the migrants that winter here is beige / light pink.

White-throated Needletail.Name: White-throated Needletail
White-throated Needletail.Description: This species has a distinct white throat and vent when seen from below.

Brown-backed Needletail.Name: Brown-backed Needletail
Brown-backed Needletail.Description: This species has a brown saddle which is less contrasting than that of the silver-backed or white-throated. It also lacks the pale throat patch seen in the other two species.

Asian Palm Swift.Name: Asian Palm Swift
Asian Palm Swift.Description: This swift can be recognised by its obvious forked tail and lack of markings on its dark plumage.

House Swift.Name: House Swift
House Swift.Description: This species has a squarish tail, white rump and throat.

Plume-toed Swiftlet.Name: Plume-toed Swiftlet
Plume-toed Swiftlet.Description: This species has glossy black upperparts and a whitish underparts with grey scalloping.

Black-nest Swiftlet.Name: Black-nest Swiftlet
Black-nest Swiftlet.Description: This species is named after its black nests, which are built with saliva and feathers. The similar Germain's swiftlet builds white nests.

Germain's Swiftlet.Name: Germain's Swiftlet
Germain's Swiftlet.Description: This species is easily confused with the Black-nest swiftlet and is practically impossible to differentiate in flight. Germain’s swiftlets build their nests from saliva which are commonly harvested for the Asian delicacy of bird's nest soup.

Pacific Swift.Name: Pacific Swift
Pacific Swift.Description: This species has a white rump and can be distinguished from the House Swift by its deeply forked tail and longer wings.

Eyebrowed Thrush.Name: Eyebrowed Thrush
Eyebrowed Thrush.Description: This thrush species has brown upperparts, a prominent white eyebrow, orange breast and flanks, and white belly. Males have grey head and throat; females have brownish heads.

Orange-headed Thrush.Name: Orange-headed Thrush
Orange-headed Thrush.Description: Males of this species have a orange head and underparts, and grey upperparts. Females generally have brownish wash on grey upperparts

Siberian Thrush.Name: Siberian Thrush
Siberian Thrush.Description: This species has a distinct white eyebrow. Males are black while females are brown with white and show numerous scales in the underparts.

Grey-rumped Treeswift.Name: Grey-rumped Treeswift
Grey-rumped Treeswift.Description: This species has a greyish-green upperparts, and greyish underparts. Males have a rusty-brown patch below their eyes.

Whiskered Treeswift.Name: Whiskered Treeswift
Whiskered Treeswift.Description: This species has two distinct white stripes above and below its eyes. Males have a rusty-brown patch below their eyes.

Forest Wagtail.Name: Forest Wagtail
Forest Wagtail.Description: This wagtail can be easily identified by the bold black and white bars on its wings and breast.

White Wagtail.Name: White Wagtail
White Wagtail.Description: Black-and-white pied plumage unique among Singapore’s wagtails. Generally black on crown, upperparts and breast, rest of plumage white. As it is a migrant, all birds in Singapore are in non-breeding plummage.

Citrine Wagtail.Name: Citrine Wagtail
Citrine Wagtail.Description: Breeding males have a bright yellow head and underparts, and grey-black upperparts. Non-breeding males and females may be confused with Yellow Wagtail but has yellow on the forehead and ear coverts.

Grey Wagtail.Name: Grey Wagtail
Grey Wagtail.Description: Has grey and black upperparts and yellow and white underparts. Breeding males of this species have a black throat which is white in females. Non breeding males also have whitish throat. Distinguished from all other wagtails by bright yellow rump and vent.

Paddyfield Pipit.Name: Paddyfield Pipit
Paddyfield Pipit.Description: A rather drab bird with heavily streaked brown upperparts and breast, and lighter brown underparts. Has a dark eyestripe and pale eyebrow.

Olive-backed Pipit.Name: Olive-backed Pipit
Olive-backed Pipit.Description: Has brown upperparts, pale underparts and heavy dark brown streaking on breast. Also has a distinctive ear patch which is white above and black below at the end of white eye-brow.

Red-throated Pipit.Name: Red-throated Pipit
Red-throated Pipit.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has a pink head. In winter, it may look similar to the Olive-backed pipit but has heavy streaking on both under and uppersides. In non breeding plumage, it is unique among local pipits in having a heavily streaked rump.

Eastern Yellow Wagtail.Name: Eastern Yellow Wagtail
Eastern Yellow Wagtail.Description: Breeding males have yellow underparts and blackish wings with variable crown colour. Non-breeding males and females generally have whitish underparts, brownish upperparts and a white eyebrow.

Streaked Weaver.Name: Streaked Weaver
Streaked Weaver.Description: Breeding males have a yellow cap and a black face and breast is streaked. Females and non-breeding males have yellowish neck patch and eye-brow, and throat and breast is streaked.

Baya Weaver.Name: Baya Weaver
Baya Weaver.Description: Breeding males have yellow cap and dark face, females and non-breeding birds generally brown overall with streaked upperparts. All plumages distinguished from Streaked Weaver by clean underparts.

Mangrove Whistler.Name: Mangrove Whistler
Mangrove Whistler.Description: This mangrove passerine has dull brown upperparts and whitish underparts. Also has an entire black hooked bill.

Swinhoe's White-Eye.Name: Swinhoe's White-Eye
Swinhoe's White-Eye.Description: A common garden bird with greenish-yellow head and upperparts, grey underparts, yellow vent and a prominent white eye-ring.

Sunda Pygmy Woodpecker.Name: Sunda Pygmy Woodpecker
Sunda Pygmy Woodpecker.Description: This is the smallest woodpecker species in Singapore and is well camouflaged on trees with its brown and white mottled plumage.

White-bellied Woodpecker.Name: White-bellied Woodpecker
White-bellied Woodpecker.Description: This large woodpecker is black with a white belly and red crest. Males have a red cap, while females have a black cap.

Laced Woodpecker.Name: Laced Woodpecker
Laced Woodpecker.Description: This woodpecker is characteristically green. Males have a red cap, while females have a black cap.

Buff-rumped Woodpecker.Name: Buff-rumped Woodpecker
Buff-rumped Woodpecker.Description: So called for the cream patch on its rump. This woodpecker is otherwise identifiable by its finely-barred head and crest, and black and white mottled plumage.

Rufous Woodpecker.Name: Rufous Woodpecker
Rufous Woodpecker.Description: This woodpecker has a rusty-red plumage with black barring on its upperparts.

Banded Woodpecker.Name: Banded Woodpecker
Banded Woodpecker.Description: This species has a distinct yellow crest, bright red upperparts and black and white barring on its underparts.

Common Flameback.Name: Common Flameback
Common Flameback.Description: Named after its distinctive golden-yellow plumage on its upperparts. Males have a red cap while females have a black cap.

Great Slaty Woodpecker.Name: Great Slaty Woodpecker
Great Slaty Woodpecker.Description: Large woodpecker with grey plumage, and a buffy throat. Males have a red cheek stripe.

Purple Duke.Name: Purple Duke
Purple Duke.Description: Underside pale silvery, with two faint eyespots. Males have a black upperside with a white bar while females are primarily brown.

Courtesan (M).Name: Courtesan (M)
Courtesan (M).Description: Males are black with white streaks and spots on upperside, but chocolate brown on underside. Females take two forms, one resembling the Magpie Crow.

Courtesan (F).Name: Courtesan (F)
Courtesan (F).Description: This form of the Courtesan mimicks the Magpie Crow, but differ in wing shape and eye colour.

Black Rajah.Name: Black Rajah
Black Rajah.Description: Upperside dark brown, and underside grey with reddish brown patches, and two pointed tails typical of Rajahs and Nawabs.

Plain Nawab.Name: Plain Nawab
Plain Nawab.Description: Similar to the Malayan Nawab, but upperwing forewing margin decreases markedly towards the tornus.

Blue Nawab.Name: Blue Nawab
Blue Nawab.Description: Upperside bluish black, with a white band across both wings. Underside silvery and marked with brown and purple patterns, setting it apart from other Nawabs.

Malayan Nawab.Name: Malayan Nawab
Malayan Nawab.Description: Similar to the Plain Nawab, but upperwing forewing margin does not decrease greatly towards the tornus.

Great Orange Awlet.Name: Great Orange Awlet
Great Orange Awlet.Description: Similar in appearance to the Orange Awlet but larger. Underside orange-brown with pale streaks on both wings. Upperside of males dark brown, while females deep blue.

Orange Awlet.Name: Orange Awlet
Orange Awlet.Description: Similar in appearance to the Great Orange Awlet but much smaller. Underside purplish-brown, streaked with orange. Upperside of males coppery-brown with darkened veins, while females steely blue.

Orange-Tail Awl.Name: Orange-Tail Awl
Orange-Tail Awl.Description: Underside dark brown with a broad white discal band on both wings. Hindwing tornal region diagnostically deep orange.

Common Banded Awl.Name: Common Banded Awl
Common Banded Awl.Description: Hindwing underside pale brown with a narrow post-discal band, washed with bluish purple.

White Banded Awl.Name: White Banded Awl
White Banded Awl.Description: Hindwing underside fades from bluish-green at the base to purple near the termen. Post-discal band narrow.

Yellow Banded Awl.Name: Yellow Banded Awl
Yellow Banded Awl.Description: Easily distinguished from the other awls by its broad yellow discal band on the underside.

Common Awl.Name: Common Awl
Common Awl.Description: Underside brown, with a light purplish glaze and a small white spot in the hindwing cell.

Plain Banded Awl.Name: Plain Banded Awl
Plain Banded Awl.Description: This awl can be identified from similar species by its broad hindwing post-discal band and a small forewing sub-apical spot.

Brown Awl.Name: Brown Awl
Brown Awl.Description: The bold black bands on the abdomen help distinguish it from other awls. Underside pale greyish-brown. Upperside brown with long white translucent streaks in the cell.

Mottled Emigrant.Name: Mottled Emigrant
Mottled Emigrant.Description: Underside greenish white with faint brown streaks, giving a mottled appearance. Upperside greenish white.

Lemon Emigrant.Name: Lemon Emigrant
Lemon Emigrant.Description: Represented by several forms; varied patterns present on wings. Distinguished from other emigrants by pale yellow or white upperside.

Orange Emigrant.Name: Orange Emigrant
Orange Emigrant.Description: Underside pale yellow. Upperside forewing white while hindwing deep orange.

No Brand Grass Yellow.Name: No Brand Grass Yellow
No Brand Grass Yellow.Description: Has no cell spots on underside forewing and many tiny freckles throughout underside.

Common Grass Yellow.Name: Common Grass Yellow
Common Grass Yellow.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside lacks the large brown apical spot found in the Forest Grass Yellow.

Forest Grass Yellow.Name: Forest Grass Yellow
Forest Grass Yellow.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside has a large partially divided, brown apical spot.

Three Spot Grass Yellow.Name: Three Spot Grass Yellow
Three Spot Grass Yellow.Description: Has three cell spots on underside forewing.

Anderson\u2019s Grass Yellow.Name: Anderson’s Grass Yellow
Anderson\u2019s Grass Yellow.Description: Has a single cell spot on underside of forewing.  Unlike the Chocolate Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is not completely darkened on the underside.

Chocolate Grass Yellow.Name: Chocolate Grass Yellow
Chocolate Grass Yellow.Description: Has a single cell spot on its forewing underside.  Unlike the Anderson's Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is completely darkened on the underside.

Tree Yellow.Name: Tree Yellow
Tree Yellow.Description: Has a pale yellow colour on both sides of its wings. Entirely unmarked except for black borders on upperside.

Grass Yellows.Name: Grass Yellows
Grass Yellows.Description: Small yellow butterflies with irregular black borders on the upperside and small dark spots on the underside.

Malayan Sunbeam.Name: Malayan Sunbeam
Malayan Sunbeam.Description: Underside silvery-white, peppered with small black spots on both wings. Both its upperside and the bands on its legs copper red.

Sumatran Sunbeam.Name: Sumatran Sunbeam
Sumatran Sunbeam.Description: Underside silvery-white, with a line of crescent-shaped markings on both wings. Both its upperside and the bands of its legs orange. The extent and shade of orange colouration differ between sexes.

Little Maplet.Name: Little Maplet
Little Maplet.Description: Upperside orange-brown, with reddish-brown bands across both wings. Underside paler but similar in marking to upperside.

Plain Tiger.Name: Plain Tiger
Plain Tiger.Description: The only tiger butterfly in Singapore without veins on both sides of hindwing. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white.

Common Tiger.Name: Common Tiger
Common Tiger.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins and exists in two forms. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white. Submarginal bands narrower than Black Veined Tiger

Black Veined Tiger.Name: Black Veined Tiger
Black Veined Tiger.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins. Unlike the Common Tiger, its hindwing is white without any orange. With a broader sub-marginal border than the Common Tiger.

Dark Glassy Tiger.Name: Dark Glassy Tiger
Dark Glassy Tiger.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Blue Glassy Tiger, but differs in direction of black streak within its forewing cell.

Yellow Glassy Tiger.Name: Yellow Glassy Tiger
Yellow Glassy Tiger.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly with yellow basal patches on each  wing. Mimicked by the Wanderer, but has more prominent colours on underside.

Blue Glassy Tiger.Name: Blue Glassy Tiger
Blue Glassy Tiger.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Dark Glassy Tiger, but has a black bar transversing its forewing cell.

Grey Glassy Tiger.Name: Grey Glassy Tiger
Grey Glassy Tiger.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Distinguishable from the rest of the glassy tigers by its large elongate spot on the forewing upperside usually with a thin central black stripe within the spot.

Common Tree Nymph.Name: Common Tree Nymph
Common Tree Nymph.Description: A large, white butterfly with black spots and veins. Distinguished from the Mangrove Tree Nymph by its small disjointed spots and absence of black border on its hindwing.

Mangrove Tree Nymph.Name: Mangrove Tree Nymph
Mangrove Tree Nymph.Description: A large, white butterfly with black spots and veins. Distinguished from the Common Tree Nymph by its conjointed black spots and black border on its hindwing.

Spotted Black Crow.Name: Spotted Black Crow
Spotted Black Crow.Description: Has a prominent patch at forewing apex on its underside consisting of 5 elongated spots. Similar to the Blue Spotted Crow.

Malayan Crow.Name: Malayan Crow
Malayan Crow.Description: Similar to the King Crow, but has smaller inner series of white spots on its underside, especially near apex of forewing.

Striped Black Crow.Name: Striped Black Crow
Striped Black Crow.Description: Identified by the series of long streaks and spots along margins of its hindwing.

Striped Blue Crow (F).Name: Striped Blue Crow (F)
Striped Blue Crow (F).Description: Females have striped hindwings on both sides and an iridescent blue patches on forewing apex of the upperside.

Striped Blue Crow (M).Name: Striped Blue Crow (M)
Striped Blue Crow (M).Description: Has an iridescent blue patch on its forewing apex like the Dwarf Crow, but has more spots on underside.

King Crow.Name: King Crow
King Crow.Description: Similar to the Malayan Crow, but has larger violet-tinged spots on the forewing apex of the upperside.

Blue Spotted Crow.Name: Blue Spotted Crow
Blue Spotted Crow.Description: Prominent patch at forewing apex of the underside comprising 4 elongated spots. Similar to the Spotted Black Crow.

Dwarf Crow.Name: Dwarf Crow
Dwarf Crow.Description: Iridescent blue patch on forewing apex like the Striped Blue Crow, but primarily unmarked on underside.

Magpie Crow.Name: Magpie Crow
Magpie Crow.Description: Magpie crows exhibit sexual dimorphism, both sexes have characteristic white patch on underside of each wing. Mimicked by the Courtesan, but told apart by its black eyes and round hindwing.

Tawny Coster.Name: Tawny Coster
Tawny Coster.Description: Orange upperside with a black border and black spots, but paler in females. Its thorax and hindwing border are black with white spots.

Malay Lacewing.Name: Malay Lacewing
Malay Lacewing.Description: Upperside orange with black borders and a white band. Distinguishable from other lacewings by absence of submarginal white band.

Plain Lacewing.Name: Plain Lacewing
Plain Lacewing.Description: Upperside orange with black border and white band. Similar to Malay Lacewing, but with submarginal white band along row of short black stripes.

Leopard Lacewing.Name: Leopard Lacewing
Leopard Lacewing.Description: Upperside orange with black borders and a white band. Distinguishable from other lacewings from its large spots in submarginal white band.

Leopard.Name: Leopard
Leopard.Description: Orange-brown on upperside with many black spots. Underside a lighter shade of orange with a purplish sheen in the side light.

Rustic.Name: Rustic
Rustic.Description: Orange-brown with a characteristic yellow patch, adjacent to broad black area around the upperside forewing apex. Similar to Branded Yeoman, but with black spots within the yellow patch.

Banded Yeoman.Name: Banded Yeoman
Banded Yeoman.Description: Orange-brown with a characteristic yellow patch, adjacent to broad black area around the upperside forewing apex. Similar to the Rustic, but without black spots within yellow patch.

Malay Yeoman.Name: Malay Yeoman
Malay Yeoman.Description: Upperside deep orange with black borders. Underside pale brown with white band adjacent to a series of black spots on the hindwing.

Cruiser (M).Name: Cruiser (M)
Cruiser (M).Description: Males orange-brown on the upperside with eyespots and a short, pointed tail on the hindwing.

Cruiser (F).Name: Cruiser (F)
Cruiser (F).Description: Females pale greenish-grey on the upperside, with eyespots and a short tail on its hindwing. A white band cuts across both wings.

Royal Assyrian.Name: Royal Assyrian
Royal Assyrian.Description: Upperside rich purple, with a white area on the hindwing. Underside purple-brown, with pale dull blue lines and orange-tinged spots.

Bush Hopper.Name: Bush Hopper
Bush Hopper.Description: Upperside brown with yellow markings, but reduced and paler in females. Hindwing yellowish and checkered with a dark-brown pattern.

Dark Banded Ace.Name: Dark Banded Ace
Dark Banded Ace.Description: Upperside dark brown, with a series of translucent forewing spots. Underside dark brown, overlain with greenish-brown scales and a prominent white hindwing band.

Chestnut Bob.Name: Chestnut Bob
Chestnut Bob.Description: Characterised by its reddish-brown underside and its series of small white discal spots and forewing cell spot. Similar to the Starry Bob, but lacks a white spot in the hindwing cell.

Starry Bob.Name: Starry Bob
Starry Bob.Description: Characterised by its reddish-brown underside and its series of small white discal spots and forewing cell spot. Similar to the Chestnut Bob, but with an additional white spot in the hindwing cell.

Forest Hopper.Name: Forest Hopper
Forest Hopper.Description: Dark greyish brown throughout, sometimes with small white costal spots near the forewing apex. Hindwing underside peppered with pale spots.

Chocolate Demon.Name: Chocolate Demon
Chocolate Demon.Description: Dark brown throughout, with the marginal regions of the underside slightly paler. This skipper has an exceptionally long proboscis.

Banded Demon.Name: Banded Demon
Banded Demon.Description: Upperside blackish-brown; paler on the underside, especially so in the marginal regions. The forewing has a characteristic bent white band and usually has a white translucent post-discal spot.

Grass Demon.Name: Grass Demon
Grass Demon.Description: Dark grey-brown on both sides, with a mosaic of white spots and bands. The antenna has a whitish band just below the tip.

Palm Bob.Name: Palm Bob
Palm Bob.Description: Upperside dark brown, with whitish forewing spots. Underside greyish brown, with several prominent black discal spots. Individuals with obscured black spots have been spotted.

White Palm Bob.Name: White Palm Bob
White Palm Bob.Description: Upperside dark brown and mostly unmarked, except for a narrow white area in the hindwing. Hindwing underside largely whitened with a large dark grey spot in the dorsal area and several smaller ones adjacent to it.

Spotted Flitter.Name: Spotted Flitter
Spotted Flitter.Description: Upperside brown, with translucent forewing sub-apical spots. Hindwing underside yellowish, with darker discal and post-discal spots.

Tree Flitter.Name: Tree Flitter
Tree Flitter.Description: Dark brown on both sides. Forewing carries several translucent sub-apical spots. Underside has a characteristic irregular white discal band across both wings.

Quedara monteithi monteithi (M).Name: Quedara monteithi monteithi (M)
Quedara monteithi monteithi (M).Description: Males dark brown and unmarked on both sides of its wings. Antennae dark brown without any markings.

Quedara monteithi monteithi (F).Name: Quedara monteithi monteithi (F)
Quedara monteithi monteithi (F).Description: Females dark brown with a broad oblique white bar on the forewing. Antennae dark brown without any markings.

Chequered Lancer.Name: Chequered Lancer
Chequered Lancer.Description: Underside characteristically black, with silvery-white streaks and spots throughout both wings. Abdomen striped black and white.

Yellow Chequered Lancer.Name: Yellow Chequered Lancer
Yellow Chequered Lancer.Description: Similar in pattern to the Chequered Lancer, but underside black with yellow streaks and spots instead. Abdomen striped black and yellow.

Pugnacious Lancer.Name: Pugnacious Lancer
Pugnacious Lancer.Description: Upperside dark brown with a series of pale yellowish translucent forewing spots. Underside overlaid with orange-brown scaling, with a pair of black sub-apical spots beside a large translucent spot.

Yellow Vein Lancer.Name: Yellow Vein Lancer
Yellow Vein Lancer.Description: Underside characteristically black with yellow veins and margins. Large translucent spots can be found between the veins too.

Storey's Palmer.Name: Storey's Palmer
Storey's Palmer.Description: A red-eyed skipper that is dark brown throughout. Hindwing cilia deep orange-yellow.

Giant Redeye.Name: Giant Redeye
Giant Redeye.Description: Dark brown with three large and three small yellowish translucent spots on the forewing. Bluish-violet scaling forms forewing apical patch and several transverse bands on the hindwing. The largest skipper in the region.

Banded Redeye.Name: Banded Redeye
Banded Redeye.Description: A red-eyed skipper, easily recognised by the broad purplish-white band across the discal region of the hindwing, which connects to the forewing. Tornal cilia yellowish orange. Males dark brown and unmarked on the upperside, while females have transluscent

Common Redeye.Name: Common Redeye
Common Redeye.Description: Red-eyed, underside orange brown with yellowish-white cilia. Upperside brown and unmarked except for two bowed brands on the forewing of males.

Torus Skipper.Name: Torus Skipper
Torus Skipper.Description: Upperside dark brown with three large translucent spots on the forewing. Underside paler with obscure streaks on the hindwing. Very similar to the Banana Skipper, but with a more restricted faint band in the hindwing.

Banana Skipper.Name: Banana Skipper
Banana Skipper.Description: Upperside dark brown with three large translucent spots on the forewing. Underside paler with obscure streaks on the hindwing. Very similar to Erionota torus, but with a more extensive band in the hindwing.

White Tipped Skipper.Name: White Tipped Skipper
White Tipped Skipper.Description: Males have a distinctive whitened apical patch on the forewing on both sides. Underside paler brown than the upperside. The antennal club is entirely white above.

Hoary Palmer.Name: Hoary Palmer
Hoary Palmer.Description: Underside mostly dark brown, but with a partially whitened forewing and strongly whitened hindwing. Upperside dark brown, with translucent forewing spots.

Coconut Skipper.Name: Coconut Skipper
Coconut Skipper.Description: Underside pale buff brown, with a faint purple wash. Has a series of dark spots on the post-discal regions of both wings and a white spot above the hindwing cell.

White Spotted Palmer.Name: White Spotted Palmer
White Spotted Palmer.Description: Underside brown with a white triangular band in contact with several translucent spots on the hindwing. Forewing contains a series of translucent discal spots. Abdomen dark brown; white banded above and completely white beneath.

Spotted Grass Dart.Name: Spotted Grass Dart
Spotted Grass Dart.Description: Upperside dark brown, with pale yellowish spots on both wings. Underside yellowish brown, with yellow spots.

Yellow Grass Dart.Name: Yellow Grass Dart
Yellow Grass Dart.Description: Upperside dark brown, with overlapping orange spots on both wings. Underside paler and more orange. Lacks a pointed hook on the clubbed antennal tip like most other skippers.

Common Dartlet.Name: Common Dartlet
Common Dartlet.Description: Upperside black, with orange-yellow post-discal bands. Underside paler than upperside.

Lesser Dart.Name: Lesser Dart
Lesser Dart.Description: Similar in appearance to the Large Dart, but smaller and with blackened veins. Additionally, the dislocated spot on the forewing underside is closer in size to the spots above it on the forewing underside.

Large Dart.Name: Large Dart
Large Dart.Description: Similar in appearance to the Lesser Dart, but larger and with unmarked veins. Additionally, the dislocated spot on the forewing underside is smaller relative to the spots above it.

Plain Palm Dart (M).Name: Plain Palm Dart (M)
Plain Palm Dart (M).Description: Underside of males unicolourous and orange.

Plain Palm Dart (F).Name: Plain Palm Dart (F)
Plain Palm Dart (F).Description: Underside of females dull greyish-brown with a purplish sheen. Hindwing generally defined by dark spots, but these could be absent in some individuals.

Yellow Palm Dart.Name: Yellow Palm Dart
Yellow Palm Dart.Description: Difficult to distinguish from other darts in the field.

Common Palm Dart.Name: Common Palm Dart
Common Palm Dart.Description: Difficult to distinguish from other darts in the field.

Besta Palm Dart.Name: Besta Palm Dart
Besta Palm Dart.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Palm Dart in the field.

Palm Dart.Name: Palm Dart
Palm Dart.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Besta Palm Dart in the field.

Small Branded Swift.Name: Small Branded Swift
Small Branded Swift.Description: Upperside golden-brown, with wing bases and upper surface of the thorax greenish. Underside light brown, with a series of translucent spots and two cell spots on the forewing and small post-discal spots and a cell spot on the hindwing.

Formosan Swift.Name: Formosan Swift
Formosan Swift.Description: Upperside brown with a greenish-golden basal area. Has a characteristic yellow opaque spot near the dorsum, in addition to the translucent spots on the forewing. Underside light brown, with greenish scaling and contains three small round white spots on th

Great Swift.Name: Great Swift
Great Swift.Description: Underside dark brown, with white translucent spots on the forewing, and one or two on the hindwing. Cell spots on the forewing conjoined, unlike in the Conjoined Swift.

Conjoined Swift.Name: Conjoined Swift
Conjoined Swift.Description: Underside dark brown, with pale yellow translucent spots and a distinctive spot near the forewing dorsum. Forewing cell spots separate, unlike in the Great Swift.

Contiguous Swift.Name: Contiguous Swift
Contiguous Swift.Description: Upperside golden-brown, with translucent spots on the forewing, including a small spot above the dorsum and two conjoined cell spots. Underside rusty orange-brown, with small spots on the hindwing.

Bamboo Paintbrush Swift.Name: Bamboo Paintbrush Swift
Bamboo Paintbrush Swift.Description: Dark brown on both sides, with variable spotting patterns between the sexes. Can only be distinguished with certainly from the Paintbrush Swift by dissection.

Paintbrush Swift.Name: Paintbrush Swift
Paintbrush Swift.Description: Dark brown on both sides, with highly variable spotting patterns. Can only be distinguished with certainly from the Bamboo Paintbrush Swift by dissection.

Full Stop Swift.Name: Full Stop Swift
Full Stop Swift.Description: Underside rusty brown, usually with a single forewing cell spot. Hindwing spots rare and, if present, only located on the underside.

Philippine Swift.Name: Philippine Swift
Philippine Swift.Description: Underside unicolorous and greenish compared to other similar swifts. Upperside dark brown, lacking any forewing cell spots, but the typical post-discal spots.

Commander.Name: Commander
Commander.Description: Upperside dark reddish-brown, with white band across both wings. Underside similar in markings as above, but with pale-greyish green base.

Knight.Name: Knight
Knight.Description: Upperside reddish-brown, with a narrow white band across both wings. Hindwing remains reddish brown, unlike the other subspecies of the Knight.

Lance Sergeant.Name: Lance Sergeant
Lance Sergeant.Description: Cell streak unbroken like the Colour Sergeant, but with its central white band disjointed.

Studded Sergeant.Name: Studded Sergeant
Studded Sergeant.Description: Cell streak broken into a band and short spot on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring, with black-centered spots on the forewing underside.

Dot-Dash Sergeant.Name: Dot-Dash Sergeant
Dot-Dash Sergeant.Description: Cell streak broken into a band and short spot on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring, lacks black-centered spots on the underside and has a relatively curved white-spotted margin on forewing upperside.

Malay Staff Sergeant.Name: Malay Staff Sergeant
Malay Staff Sergeant.Description: Cell streaks constricted twice to form three parts on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring.

Colour Sergeant (M).Name: Colour Sergeant (M)
Colour Sergeant (M).Description: Cell streak unbroken like the Lance Sergeant. Central band is continuous and markings are bluish-white.

Colour Sergeant (F).Name: Colour Sergeant (F)
Colour Sergeant (F).Description: Lacks a series of orange spots beside its black and orange border like the Common Lascar, but carries a thinner orange line within border. Some forms are dark brown in colour.

Colonel.Name: Colonel
Colonel.Description: Upperside orange with dark brown shadings towards the base. Underside similar in markings as above, but greenish-grey towards the base.

Common Sailor.Name: Common Sailor
Common Sailor.Description: Cell streak broken into two parts on each side and lack a whitish ring on abdomen like the Short-Banded Sailor. However, its forewing spot is more triangular and it has a golden-brown underside with black and white stripes.

Grey Sailor.Name: Grey Sailor
Grey Sailor.Description: Cell streak broken into a band and short spot on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring, lacks black-centered spots on its underside and has a relatively straight white-spotted margin on the forewing upperside.

Chocolate Sailor.Name: Chocolate Sailor
Chocolate Sailor.Description: Dark brown above with narrow white stripes.

Short Banded Sailor.Name: Short Banded Sailor
Short Banded Sailor.Description: Cell streak broken into two parts on each side and lack a whitish ring on the abdomen like the Common Sailor. However, its forewing spot is rounder than the Common Sailor's.

Burmese Lascar.Name: Burmese Lascar
Burmese Lascar.Description: A series of evenly-sized orange spots found adjacent to the black and orange border on its upperside.

Malayan Lascar.Name: Malayan Lascar
Malayan Lascar.Description: A series of orange spots adjacent to the black and orange border on its upperside. One of the spots in the middle broader than the others.

Common Lascar.Name: Common Lascar
Common Lascar.Description: Lacks a series of orange spots beside its black and orange border, like some females of the Colour Sergeant. Carries a thicker orange line within border and has marbled and striated underside.

Perak Lascar.Name: Perak Lascar
Perak Lascar.Description: The only lascar with two fine orange lines within black border of the upperside forewing.

Common Jester.Name: Common Jester
Common Jester.Description: Similar to the lascars, but with a completely black border on its upperside, a short tail and a marbled underside.

Malay Viscount.Name: Malay Viscount
Malay Viscount.Description: Upperside light brown, with variable white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are slightly disjointed.

Horsfield's Baron (M).Name: Horsfield's Baron (M)
Horsfield's Baron (M).Description: Upperside of males black, with broad bright blue marginal borders across both wings.

Horsfield's Baron (F).Name: Horsfield's Baron (F)
Horsfield's Baron (F).Description: Upperside of females light brown, with white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are less distinct that those of the Malay Viscount.

Malay Baron (M).Name: Malay Baron (M)
Malay Baron (M).Description: Males of the gardineri morph are dark brown above, lacking the blue hindwing border of the monina morph.

Malay Baron.Name: Malay Baron
Malay Baron.Description: Upperside brown, with variable white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are conjoined.

White Tipped Baron.Name: White Tipped Baron
White Tipped Baron.Description: Bluish tinge on upperside forewing helps distinguish from the Baron and the Malay Baron lack. Females have distinctive post-discal white spots.

Baron (M).Name: Baron (M)
Baron (M).Description: Upperside of males dark brown with broad post-discal bands on both wings. Lacks bluish tinge on forewing like in the White Tipped Baron.

Baron (F).Name: Baron (F)
Baron (F).Description: Upperside of females lighter brown, with prominent post-discal white spots. Lacks bluish tinge like in the White Tipped Baron.

Green Baron (M).Name: Green Baron (M)
Green Baron (M).Description: Identified by its lighter green tornal area and distinct apical red spots on the upperside hindwing. Underside marked with red spots on both wings.

Green Baron (F).Name: Green Baron (F)
Green Baron (F).Description: Identified from the upperside by the broad white band across both wings and distinct apical red spots in the hindwing. Underside marked with red spots on both wings.

Black Tipped Archduke (M).Name: Black Tipped Archduke (M)
Black Tipped Archduke (M).Description: Males black above, with a broad black-spotted border on the hindwing, and a pale green border on the forewing. Its black-tipped antennae distinguishes it from the Archduke.

Black Tipped Archduke (F).Name: Black Tipped Archduke (F)
Black Tipped Archduke (F).Description: Similar to the yellow archduke but with bluish scaling on the hindwing underside. It has black-tipped antennae which distinguishes it from the Archduke.

Archduke (M).Name: Archduke (M)
Archduke (M).Description: Males black above, with a broad black-spotted border on the hindwing, and a pale green border on the forewing. Its orange-tipped antennae distinguishes it from the Black Tipped Archduke.

Archduke (F).Name: Archduke (F)
Archduke (F).Description: Similar to the Yellow Archduke, but with bluish scaling on the underside hindwings. It has orange-tipped antennae which distinguishes it from the Black Tipped Archduke.

Yellow Archduke.Name: Yellow Archduke
Yellow Archduke.Description: Upperside of both sexes dark brown, with yellow spots on both wings. Differs from the females of the other archdukes in its yellowish scaling on the underside of its hindwing.

Sergeants and Sailors.Name: Sergeants and Sailors
Sergeants and Sailors.Description: Medium-sized butterflies with white bands across a dark ground colour on the upperside.

Lascars and Jesters.Name: Lascars and Jesters
Lascars and Jesters.Description: Medium-sized butterflies with orange bands across a dark ground colour on the upperside.

Common Pierrot.Name: Common Pierrot
Common Pierrot.Description: A black and white butterfly. More small black spots on its underside than the Elbowed Pierrot.

Elbowed Pierrot.Name: Elbowed Pierrot
Elbowed Pierrot.Description: A black and white butterfly. Few black bands and patches on its underside compared to the Common Pierrot.

Indian Cupid.Name: Indian Cupid
Indian Cupid.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two orange-crowned, black tornal spots. One of the black spots close to and above the post-discal spots.

The Quaker.Name: The Quaker
The Quaker.Description: Underside pure white, with light submarginal markings and a distinctive large black circular spot on the hindwing costa. Upperside blackish-brown, with a white patch that may be absent in males.

The Malayan.Name: The Malayan
The Malayan.Description: Very similar to the Common Hedge Blue, but brown on the upperside, has a small tail, and has its black outer spot clear of the submarginal markings.

Common Hedge Blue.Name: Common Hedge Blue
Common Hedge Blue.Description: Very similar to the Malayan, but shining blue on the upperside, lacks a tail, has a small black spot at the base on the underside.

Lesser Grass Blue.Name: Lesser Grass Blue
Lesser Grass Blue.Description: Upperside purplish-blue in males, while brown in females. The misaligned spot in the hindwing helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Pygmy Grass Blue.Name: Pygmy Grass Blue
Pygmy Grass Blue.Description: Upperside of males dull blue, while dark brown in females. The V-shaped marking on the forewing sub-apical region helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Pale Grass Blue.Name: Pale Grass Blue
Pale Grass Blue.Description: Upperside of males light blue, while dark greyish-blue in females. The more pronounced spots on the underside, particularly the sub-marginal spots along both wings help distinguish it from the other grass blues.

Cycad Blue.Name: Cycad Blue
Cycad Blue.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two black tornal spots, only one of which is orange-crowned. One of the hindwing black spots close to and above the post-discal spots.

Gram Blue.Name: Gram Blue
Gram Blue.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two orange-crowned, black tornal spots. The black spot close to the post-discal spots is further inwards than in the Indian Cupid.

Forget-Me-Not.Name: Forget-Me-Not
Forget-Me-Not.Description: Has a black spot on the forewing costa between the cell spot and post-discal band, in addition to the typical black spots in certain blue butterflies.

Silver Forget-Me-Not.Name: Silver Forget-Me-Not
Silver Forget-Me-Not.Description: Has a black spot on the forewing costa close to the post-discal band, in addition to the typical black spots in certain blue butterflies.

Pea Blue.Name: Pea Blue
Pea Blue.Description: Underside buff brown, with white streaks of varying thickness.

Dark Caerulean.Name: Dark Caerulean
Dark Caerulean.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. The smallest of all Caeruleans, with less distinct white markings.

Metallic Caerulean.Name: Metallic Caerulean
Metallic Caerulean.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Distinguished from other caeruleans by the acute V-shaped white marking in the hindwing.

Common Caerulean.Name: Common Caerulean
Common Caerulean.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside aligned to form continuous lines, like in the Malaccan Caerulean. However, white bands in hindwing mostly disjointed.

Malaccan\u00a0Caerulean.Name: Malaccan Caerulean
Malaccan\u00a0Caerulean.Description: The postdiscal bands on forewing underside aligned to form continuous lines, like in the Common Caerulean. Distinguishable from the latter by its thick continuous lines in the hindwing.

Sky Blue.Name: Sky Blue
Sky Blue.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Difficult to distinguish from the Glistening Caerulean.

Glistening Caerulean.Name: Glistening Caerulean
Glistening Caerulean.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Difficult to distinguish from the Sky Blue.

White Fourline Blue.Name: White Fourline Blue
White Fourline Blue.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Has a distinctive sub-apical spot in the hindwing.

Jewel Fourline Blue.Name: Jewel Fourline Blue
Jewel Fourline Blue.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands unicolorous and same as the ground colour. Striae broad, diffuse and yellowish.

Large Fourline Blue.Name: Large Fourline Blue
Large Fourline Blue.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands unicolorous and same as the ground colour. Striae narrow and well-defined.

Singapore Fourline Blue.Name: Singapore Fourline Blue
Singapore Fourline Blue.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands inwardly bound by darker lines.

Opaque Sixline Blue.Name: Opaque Sixline Blue
Opaque Sixline Blue.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Rounded Sixline Blue.Name: Rounded Sixline Blue
Rounded Sixline Blue.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Dark Malayan Sixline Blue.Name: Dark Malayan Sixline Blue
Dark Malayan Sixline Blue.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Two Spotted Line Blue.Name: Two Spotted Line Blue
Two Spotted Line Blue.Description: Tailless. Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other Fourline Blues. Unique in having 2 black spots at the tornal region of its hindwing.

Pointed Line Blue.Name: Pointed Line Blue
Pointed Line Blue.Description: Tailed. Easily confused with several other Lycaenids.

Common Line Blue.Name: Common Line Blue
Common Line Blue.Description: Underside orange-yellow in males while greyish-beige in females.

Tailless Line Blue.Name: Tailless Line Blue
Tailless Line Blue.Description: Tailless, with a rather large tornal spot on the underside.

Barred Line Blue.Name: Barred Line Blue
Barred Line Blue.Description: Tailed. Easily confused with several other Lycaenids.

Banded Line Blue.Name: Banded Line Blue
Banded Line Blue.Description: Tailless, with one black sub-apical black spot and two uncrowned black spots in the tornal region on the hindwing underside.

Ancyra Blue.Name: Ancyra Blue
Ancyra Blue.Description: The orange crowns on the tornal region uniquely separated from the rest of the wings by black curved lines.

Dingy Line Blue.Name: Dingy Line Blue
Dingy Line Blue.Description: Tailless, with two uncrowned black spots in the tornal region on the hindwing underside.

Ciliate Blue.Name: Ciliate Blue
Ciliate Blue.Description: Posseses short fine tails like the Pointed Ciliate Blue. Underside carries prominent black spot on hindwing dorsum.

Pointed Ciliate Blue.Name: Pointed Ciliate Blue
Pointed Ciliate Blue.Description: Posseses short fine tails like the Ciliate Blue. Underside carries two black spots on the hindwing, near the costa and dorsum respectively.

Club Silverline.Name: Club Silverline
Club Silverline.Description: Bands surrounding silver streaks are usually black, but occasionally red. Upperside greyish-blue but variable. Key distinguishing characteristic is the shape of the basal streak on the forewing underside.

Long Banded Silverline.Name: Long Banded Silverline
Long Banded Silverline.Description: Bands surrounding silver streaks are red. Upperside of males deep blue, while females brown. Key distinguishing characteristic is the L-shaped basal streak on the forewing underside.

Centaur Oakblue.Name: Centaur Oakblue
Centaur Oakblue.Description: Can be immediately separated from the other oakblues by the silvery-green edging in the cell markings on the forewing underside. One of the largest oakblues.

Malayan Oakblue.Name: Malayan Oakblue
Malayan Oakblue.Description: Identifiable by its white markings on its reddish-brown underside, which shows a purplish wash in the side light.

Large Metallic Oakblue.Name: Large Metallic Oakblue
Large Metallic Oakblue.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Tailed Disc Oakblue.Name: Tailed Disc Oakblue
Tailed Disc Oakblue.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Common Disc Oakblue in the field.

Common Disc Oakblue.Name: Common Disc Oakblue
Common Disc Oakblue.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Tailed Disc Oakblue in the field.

Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta.Name: Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta
Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Arhopala major major in the field.

Arhopala major major.Name: Arhopala major major
Arhopala major major.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta in the field.

Small Tailless Oakblue.Name: Small Tailless Oakblue
Small Tailless Oakblue.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Raffles' Oakblue.Name: Raffles' Oakblue
Raffles' Oakblue.Description: Can be identified from other oakblues by its alternately arranged spots making up the postdiscal band on the underside forewing.

Vinous Oakblue.Name: Vinous Oakblue
Vinous Oakblue.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Sylhet Oakblue.Name: Sylhet Oakblue
Sylhet Oakblue.Description: Has a distinctively-shaped spot above the hindwing cell on the underside.

Green Oakblue.Name: Green Oakblue
Green Oakblue.Description: Can be identified from other oakblues by the outwardly displaced spot of the postdiscal band on the underside forewing.

Arhopala aurea.Name: Arhopala aurea
Arhopala aurea.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Arhopala trogon.Name: Arhopala trogon
Arhopala trogon.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Arhopala ammon ammon.Name: Arhopala ammon ammon
Arhopala ammon ammon.Description: This oakblue is characterised by the large white spot in the middle of the hindwing underside.

Aberrant Oakblue.Name: Aberrant Oakblue
Aberrant Oakblue.Description: This oakblue is brown on the underside, but with a series of cryptic markings in grey, black and brown giving it a distinctive appearance.

Bifid Plushblue.Name: Bifid Plushblue
Bifid Plushblue.Description: Tailed. Distinctive dark, bifid (cleft) costal spot on the hindwing underside. Pale markings contrast strongly against the brown ground colour.

Shining Plushblue.Name: Shining Plushblue
Shining Plushblue.Description: Tailed. On the hindwing underside, the mid-costal spot continues downwards as a dark band. Violet markings contrast strongly against the brown ground colour.

Darky Plushblue.Name: Darky Plushblue
Darky Plushblue.Description: Tailless. Underside mostly dark purple-brown with uncontrasted markings.

Plain Plushblue.Name: Plain Plushblue
Plain Plushblue.Description: Tailed, with diagnostic dark red patches at the bases of the costa on both wings. Underside dark brown with pale purple markings.

Semanga superba deliciosa.Name: Semanga superba deliciosa
Semanga superba deliciosa.Description: Underside buff brown, with a narrow reddish-brown post-discal line. Tornal area of hindwing red, black and metallic in colour.

Acacia Blue.Name: Acacia Blue
Acacia Blue.Description: Underside brown, with small obscure dark spots and dark submarginal lines. Upperside of males deep purple-blue, while females are steely blue.

Scarce Silverstreak.Name: Scarce Silverstreak
Scarce Silverstreak.Description: Underside brown, with broad white streaks and spots. Upperside of males shining blue with broad black forewing border, while brown and unmarked in females.

Spotted Silverstreak.Name: Spotted Silverstreak
Spotted Silverstreak.Description: Underside brown, with slighly darkened patches and white markings on both wings. Upperside of males purple, while steely blue in females.

Gray Tinsel.Name: Gray Tinsel
Gray Tinsel.Description: Underside pale grey, with brown and silver markings broken into several irregular spots. Upperside of males purple, while light blue in females.

Yamfly.Name: Yamfly
Yamfly.Description: Its hindwing extends to a filamentous tail, giving it a distinctive shape. Upperside bright orange with black apical border, while underside yellowish buff.

Branded Imperial.Name: Branded Imperial
Branded Imperial.Description: Underside mostly orange, with a white tornal area edged by post-discal black lines. Upperside black.

Common Imperial.Name: Common Imperial
Common Imperial.Description: Underside white, with the apical area of hindwing and most of the forewing orange.

Common Posy.Name: Common Posy
Common Posy.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies, but its hindwing lacks both the orange submarginal band of the Pygmy Posy and the white-filled black bands of the Dark Posy.

Pygmy Posy.Name: Pygmy Posy
Pygmy Posy.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies. Identified by its orange submarginal band extending midway up the hindwing underside.

Dark Posy.Name: Dark Posy
Dark Posy.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies. Identified by its white-filled black bands on the hindwing underside.

Ambon Onyx.Name: Ambon Onyx
Ambon Onyx.Description: Underside brownish yellow, with a white transverse line across both wings. Upperside bright blue with a broad black border and a white discal spot on the forewing.

White Royal.Name: White Royal
White Royal.Description: Underside greyish-white, with a post-discal series of narrow black streaks. Similar to the Peacock Royal, but has black-spotted green eyes.

Peacock Royal.Name: Peacock Royal
Peacock Royal.Description: Underside greyish-white, with a post-discal series of narrow black streaks. Similar to the White Royal, but has black eyes.

Felder's Royal.Name: Felder's Royal
Felder's Royal.Description: Underside greyish-brown, with two orange-crowned black spots like Tajuria dominus dominus, but underside forewing post-discal line closer to termen than to end-cell. Upperside bright blue.

Tajuria dominus dominus.Name: Tajuria dominus dominus
Tajuria dominus dominus.Description: Underside greyish-brown, with two orange-crowned black spots like Felder's Royal, but underside forewing post-discal line closer to end-cell than to termen. Upperside bright blue.

Banded Royal.Name: Banded Royal
Banded Royal.Description: Underside white, with a broad purple-brown border. Upperside of males shining blue, while females brown.

Great Imperial.Name: Great Imperial
Great Imperial.Description: Underside mostly orange, with partially white hindwing ending in a sword-like tail. Black spots limited to tornal half of hindwing.

Grand Imperial.Name: Grand Imperial
Grand Imperial.Description: Underside mostly orange, with partially white hindwing. Posesses the longest tail among the imperials. Black markings extend further along the termen than in the Great Imperial.

Green Imperial.Name: Green Imperial
Green Imperial.Description: Underside mostly orange, with a partially white hindwing and a relatively short tail. Black markings extend further along the termen than the Great Imperial. Upperside shining bluish-green.

Chocolate Royal.Name: Chocolate Royal
Chocolate Royal.Description: Underside dark brown, with a dark narrow post-discal line on both wings. Has two black tornal spots and metallic-green scaling on its hindwing.

Golden Royal.Name: Golden Royal
Golden Royal.Description: Forewing underside golden-yellow and unmarked. Has two black tornal spots and metallic-green scaling on the hindwing.

Silver Royal.Name: Silver Royal
Silver Royal.Description: Underside silvery on both wings. Has two black tornal spots adjacent to the orange patch on its hindwing.

Dark Tit.Name: Dark Tit
Dark Tit.Description: Underside mostly white, with a black-spotted orange tornal area. A short orange bar on the hindwing helps tell it apart it from the other tits.

Common Tit.Name: Common Tit
Common Tit.Description: Underside mostly white, resembling the Dark Tit and the Narrow Spark. However, it lacks the orange bar in the hindwing of the Dark Tit and has two tails, unlike the Narrow Spark.

Fluffy Tit.Name: Fluffy Tit
Fluffy Tit.Description: Underside white, with most of forewing and apical area of hindwing orange-brown. Has a prominent black spot on the hindwing.

Cornelian.Name: Cornelian
Cornelian.Description: Underside greyish brown with broad, white-edged bands. Males deep orange-red above whilst females dark brown and unmarked.

Eliot's Cornelian.Name: Eliot's Cornelian
Eliot's Cornelian.Description: Underside light grey, with rounded post-discal spots outlined in white. Males duller red on the upperside than the Cornelian whilst females have a faint brown marking in the hindwings.

Pitcher Blue.Name: Pitcher Blue
Pitcher Blue.Description: Tailed. Can be identified by the series of V-shaped markings making up the submarginal bands.

Narrow Spark.Name: Narrow Spark
Narrow Spark.Description: Underside mostly white like in the Common Tit, but has one tail, unlike in the Common Tit.

The Plane (M).Name: The Plane (M)
The Plane (M).Description: Upperside of males deep black-brown, with a pale yellow tornal area. Underside yellowish brown, with black and dark brown spots.

The Plane (F).Name: The Plane (F)
The Plane (F).Description: Upperside of females reddish-brown, with black spots in a whitened tornal area. Underside whitish, with black spots and stripes on the hindwing and orange bands on the forewing.

Yellow Flash.Name: Yellow Flash
Yellow Flash.Description: Underside bright yellow with black markings.

Suffused Flash.Name: Suffused Flash
Suffused Flash.Description: Underside slightly orange-yellow, with an faint outwardly whitened post-discal line. Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black forewing apical borders extending to the dorsum, while females brown and unmarked.

Copper Flash.Name: Copper Flash
Copper Flash.Description: Distinguished from other flashes by the absence of orange crown around its tornal spot. It usually has additional bars on the underside of both wings. Upperside of males reddish-brown, while females blue.

Scarlet Flash.Name: Scarlet Flash
Scarlet Flash.Description: Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black forewing apical borders extending to the dorsum, hindwings with black patch. Upperside of females brown and unmarked; difficult to tell apart from some other flashes.

Common Red Flash.Name: Common Red Flash
Common Red Flash.Description: Distinguished from other flashes on its underside by its outwardly whitened post-discal line. Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black apical borders on forewings that do not extend to the dorsum, while females brown and unmarked.

Slate Flash.Name: Slate Flash
Slate Flash.Description: Upperside blue in both sexes. Similar to Indigo Flash, but with narrower bands and fainter purple wash on its light brown underside.

Indigo Flash.Name: Indigo Flash
Indigo Flash.Description: Upperside blue in both sexes. Similar to Slate Flash, but with broader bands and stronger purple wash on its dark brown underside.

Oakblues.Name: Oakblues
Oakblues.Description: Underside a shade of brown with pale streaks, while upperside a shade of shining blue or purple.

Grass Blues.Name: Grass Blues
Grass Blues.Description: Extremely small butterflies with a black spotted pale grey underside. Upperside blue or brown depending on sex and species.

Blues and Caeruleans.Name: Blues and Caeruleans
Blues and Caeruleans.Description: The group of butterflies with a shining blue or brown upperside and grey undersides marked with streaks and bands.

Moth Butterfly.Name: Moth Butterfly
Moth Butterfly.Description: Has a uniquely deformed appearance. Wings brownish-orange on the upperside with black borders, while purple-brown on the underside.

Miletus gopara gopara.Name: Miletus gopara gopara
Miletus gopara gopara.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Bigg's Brownie in the field, has a tail.

Bigg's Brownie.Name: Bigg's Brownie
Bigg's Brownie.Description: Similar in appearance to the Blue Brownie on its underside. However, its upperside is light brown with an oblique white band.

Blue Brownie.Name: Blue Brownie
Blue Brownie.Description: Similar in appearance to the Bigg's Brownie on its underside. However, its forewing upperside is whitish, with a broad dark apical area, while its hindwing is light bluish-grey.

Lesser Darkie.Name: Lesser Darkie
Lesser Darkie.Description: Upperside dark brown and unmarked. Underside primarily greyish-white with striations ranging from dark brown to light greyish-brown.

Pale Mottle.Name: Pale Mottle
Pale Mottle.Description: Underside with a distinct, irregularly marked and mottled appearance. Upperside is bluish grey with a black apex.

Apefly.Name: Apefly
Apefly.Description: Underside greyish buff with dark striations and a clearly defined brown-edged white spot in the forewing cell. Upperside is dark brown and unmarked, except for a small whitish patch in the middle of the forewing.

Common Faun.Name: Common Faun
Common Faun.Description: Deep brown underside with a series of small white spots and dark lines across both wings. Upperside is orange-brown.

Palm King.Name: Palm King
Palm King.Description: Multiple brown bands across both wings, each separated by thin white streaks. Hindwing also contains two widely separated eyespots.

Saturn.Name: Saturn
Saturn.Description: Underside resembles a leaf, with two large hindwing eyespots and a dark central line. Males have iridescent blue patches on uppersides, which are absent in females.

Dark Blue Jungle Glory.Name: Dark Blue Jungle Glory
Dark Blue Jungle Glory.Description: Underside dark brown, with several white streaks and two prominent black-filled eyespots. Males have a greater extent of blue patches on the upperside.

Common Duffer.Name: Common Duffer
Common Duffer.Description: Has a dark central line and two hindwing eyespots on a mottled brown underside. Few bluish spots on upperside of males, while females have a series of pale orange and whitish spots.

Painted Lady.Name: Painted Lady
Painted Lady.Description: Primarily orange on its upperside with black and white markings. Mottled underside with grey patches and an orange patch on its forewing.

Indian Red Admiral.Name: Indian Red Admiral
Indian Red Admiral.Description: Upperside dark grey-brown, with orange, black and white markings on edges. Underside has a blotched appearance with shades and patterns of brown, grey and orange.

Malayan Eggfly.Name: Malayan Eggfly
Malayan Eggfly.Description: Upperside reddish brown while underside darker brown. Exists in several forms, but identifiable on underside by lack of costal black spot and presence of two white spots near apex of hindwing.

Danaid Eggfly.Name: Danaid Eggfly
Danaid Eggfly.Description: Black with several blue-bordered white patches on its upperside. Its diagnostic feature is the black costal spot on the underside of its hindwing.

Great Eggfly.Name: Great Eggfly
Great Eggfly.Description: Similar to the Jacintha Eggfly. Thicker submarginal borders in females. Lacks the V-shaped appearance in the Jacintha Eggfly.

Jacintha Eggfly.Name: Jacintha Eggfly
Jacintha Eggfly.Description: Similar to the Great Eggfly. The submarginal borders of females are more reduced than in the Jacintha Eggfly, giving a V-shaped appearance.

Autumn Leaf.Name: Autumn Leaf
Autumn Leaf.Description: Leaf-like appearance. Told apart from other subspecies of Autumn Leaf by the absence of several small white spots on the forewing apex of its underside.

Chocolate Pansy.Name: Chocolate Pansy
Chocolate Pansy.Description: Upperside reddish brown, while underside dark brown. Both sides are lined with orange eyespots.

Grey Pansy.Name: Grey Pansy
Grey Pansy.Description: Wings  grey on both sides, but slightly paler on the underside. Both sides are lined with grey or orange-and-black eyespots.

Peacock Pansy.Name: Peacock Pansy
Peacock Pansy.Description: Orange on both sides, but slightly paler on the underside. Both sides contain prominent eyespots.

Blue Pansy (M).Name: Blue Pansy (M)
Blue Pansy (M).Description: The male Blue Pansy has a bright blue hindwing on the upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots observed on both sides.

Blue Pansy (F).Name: Blue Pansy (F)
Blue Pansy (F).Description: The female Blue Pansy has a sombre brown upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots can be observed on both sides.

Angled Castor.Name: Angled Castor
Angled Castor.Description: A deep brown butterfly with wavy black lines on both sides of its wings. Has a diagnostic white spot near the forewing apex.

Vagrant.Name: Vagrant
Vagrant.Description: Tailed. Upperside orange-brown with a narrow black border, black markings on the forewing and small black spots on the hindwing. Underside consists of purplish brown, dark and pale orange-brown patches.

Common Birdwing.Name: Common Birdwing
Common Birdwing.Description: Similar to Malayan Birdwing, but with primarily dark forewing, sometimes with faint whitish streaks. Females have many black spots on hindwing.

Malayan Birdwing.Name: Malayan Birdwing
Malayan Birdwing.Description: Similar to Common Birdwing, but with stronger whitish streaks on forewing. Females have many black spots on hindwing.

Common Rose.Name: Common Rose
Common Rose.Description: Has a diagnostic red body and a full series of red spots along underside margins of hindwing.

Common Mime.Name: Common Mime
Common Mime.Description: A moderately large butterfly with black and white stripes.

Lime Butterfly.Name: Lime Butterfly
