Lime Butterfly.Description: Upperside black with pale yellow spots and band; underside yellow with distinctive orange spots encircled by blue and black edges.

Banded Swallowtail.Name: Banded Swallowtail
Banded Swallowtail.Description: Tailed, with pale green band across both wings.

Red Helen.Name: Red Helen
Red Helen.Description: Tailed, marked with red marginal markings along underside of hindwing. Similar to Common Rose and the polytes form of the Common Mormon, but differ in position of white patch.

Great Helen.Name: Great Helen
Great Helen.Description: A large tailed butterfly with distinctive blue patches above tornal red spots.

Common Mormon.Name: Common Mormon
Common Mormon.Description: Tailed, with prominent white band across entire underside of hindwing. Females vary in form. The cyrus form resembles the male, but with red tornal bar.

Common Mormon (F).Name: Common Mormon (F)
Common Mormon (F).Description: Females of the polytes form mimick the Common Rose, but lacks red body. Central white patch and  series of red spots along margin on underside of hindwings.

Great Mormon.Name: Great Mormon
Great Mormon.Description: A large butterfly with prominent red patches near the base and tornus of its underside. Exist in several forms, mostly tailless.

Blue Helen.Name: Blue Helen
Blue Helen.Description: Tailed, with characteristic blue and orange spots behind white band on underside of hindwing.

Common Bluebottle.Name: Common Bluebottle
Common Bluebottle.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with distinctive blue band spanning both wings. Tailless.

Blue Jay.Name: Blue Jay
Blue Jay.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with black stripes. Lacks red costal spot on underside. Has small yellowish green patch separated from larger white patch.

Common Jay.Name: Common Jay
Common Jay.Description: An arrowhead-shaped, striped butterfly with a distinctive red costal bar on underside, as opposed to the red costal spot in the Great Jay.

Tailed Jay.Name: Tailed Jay
Tailed Jay.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with distinctive apple-green spots on predominantly black wings.

Striped Jay.Name: Striped Jay
Striped Jay.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with black stripes. Continuous dark central line bisects white band in hindwing.

Great Jay.Name: Great Jay
Great Jay.Description: An arrowhead-shaped, striped butterfly with a distinctive red costal spot on underside, as opposed to the red costal bar in the Common Jay.

Five Bar Swordtail.Name: Five Bar Swordtail
Five Bar Swordtail.Description: Has green and black stripes on its forewing. Identified by its characteristic long tail.

Red Base Jezebel.Name: Red Base Jezebel
Red Base Jezebel.Description: Underside of hindwing primarily yellow with long red basal patch.

Redspot Sawtooth.Name: Redspot Sawtooth
Redspot Sawtooth.Description: Has white and yellow patches on underside of hindwing and a red costal streak near the base.

Painted Jezebel.Name: Painted Jezebel
Painted Jezebel.Description: Has red, white and yellow patches on underside. Base of hindwing is yellow on the underside.

Psyche.Name: Psyche
Psyche.Description: Small, has rounded wings with thin green-grey streaks on underside, giving a mottled appearance.

Cabbage White.Name: Cabbage White
Cabbage White.Description: Predominantly white, has black spots and black forewing tips on upperside. Markings vary between males and females.

Plain Puffin.Name: Plain Puffin
Plain Puffin.Description: White, with a broad black apical region on the upperside forewing containing two small white spots, and a black subapical band across the underside forewing.

Lesser Albatross.Name: Lesser Albatross
Lesser Albatross.Description: White, with a black apical area containing a series of white subapical spots on the upperside forewing. Upperside hindwing veins end with a series of black marginal spots in males or a broad black margin in females.

Chocolate Albatross.Name: Chocolate Albatross
Chocolate Albatross.Description: Underside has strong dark brown border lining its white forewing and yellow hindwing.

Malaysian Albatross.Name: Malaysian Albatross
Malaysian Albatross.Description: Has a creamy yellow appearance with pointed forewings.

Striped Albatross (M).Name: Striped Albatross (M)
Striped Albatross (M).Description: Males white with black veins on underside. Underside of females dusted with yellow and brown colours.

Striped Albatross (F).Name: Striped Albatross (F)
Striped Albatross (F).Description: Males white with black veins on underside. Underside of females dusted with yellow and brown colours.

The Wanderer (M).Name: The Wanderer (M)
The Wanderer (M).Description: Upperside of males  pale greenish with a black border and blackened veins. Underside whiter and barely marked.

The Wanderer (F).Name: The Wanderer (F)
The Wanderer (F).Description: Upperside of females striped with a yellow wing base, which mimics the Yellow Glassy Tiger, but with fainter colours on the underside.

Great Orange Tip.Name: Great Orange Tip
Great Orange Tip.Description: Has a white upperside with a black-bordered orange band on apex. Underside resembles a dead leaf.

Malay Gem.Name: Malay Gem
Malay Gem.Description: Underside of both sexes brown, with darker brown striations. Males have metallic blue upperside with black spots scattered around; females have a blackish brown upperside.

Sumatran Gem.Name: Sumatran Gem
Sumatran Gem.Description: Underside of both sexes reddish-brown, with pale striations. Males have a metallic blue upperside with a continuous black patch; females have a light purple upperside with reddish streaks.

Dark Flat.Name: Dark Flat
Dark Flat.Description: Upperside dark brown, with dark blotchy spots on both wings. Has two or three small subapical spots on the forewing.

Hieroglypic Flat.Name: Hieroglypic Flat
Hieroglypic Flat.Description: Its yellow-orange upperside is framed by thick black lines on both wings. Underside similar in pattern but paler.

Fulvous Pied Flat.Name: Fulvous Pied Flat
Fulvous Pied Flat.Description: Upperside reddish-brown. Males have a large V-shaped spot on the forewing cell, while females have smaller spots.

Black and White Flat.Name: Black and White Flat
Black and White Flat.Description: Blackish brown with a number of spots on the forewing. The hindwing has a small white discal patch, that are separated, unlike in Gerosis sinica minima.

Gerosis sinica minima.Name: Gerosis sinica minima
Gerosis sinica minima.Description: Blackish brown with a number of spots on the forewing. The hindwing has a broad white band crossing the abdomen, unlike in the Black and White Flat.

Common Snow Flat.Name: Common Snow Flat
Common Snow Flat.Description: Upperside dark brown, with a series of spots on the forewing. Darker brown discal markings and dark sub-marginal border can be found on both wings.

Large Snow Flat.Name: Large Snow Flat
Large Snow Flat.Description: Upperside dark brown, with a series of spots on the forewing. Tornal region of hindwings whitened with diffused black spots.

Ultra Snow Flat.Name: Ultra Snow Flat
Ultra Snow Flat.Description: Upperside dark brown, with two series of spots on the forewing. Tornal region of hindwing white, but with additional tornal black spots compared to the Malayan Snow Flat.

Malayan Snow Flat.Name: Malayan Snow Flat
Malayan Snow Flat.Description: Upperside dark brown, with two series of spots on the forewing. Tornal region of hindwing white, but lacking the tornal black spots like in the Ultra Snow Flat.

Chestnut Angle.Name: Chestnut Angle
Chestnut Angle.Description: Upperside chestnut-brown, with a complex cryptic pattern.

Yellow Flat.Name: Yellow Flat
Yellow Flat.Description: Upperside blackish brown. Identifiable by the distinctive yellow tornal region on its hindwing.

White Banded Flat.Name: White Banded Flat
White Banded Flat.Description: Upperside reddish-brown, with a prominent post-discal white band and several subapical spots on the forewing.

Spotted Judy.Name: Spotted Judy
Spotted Judy.Description: Reddish brown, with a blunt tail like the Malay Tailed Judy, but with a disjointed hindwing discal band.

Malay Tailed Judy.Name: Malay Tailed Judy
Malay Tailed Judy.Description: Reddish brown, with a blunt tail like the Spotted Judy, but with a smooth and continuous discal band.

Malayan Plum Judy.Name: Malayan Plum Judy
Malayan Plum Judy.Description: A beige-brown butterfly with two white bands on the forewing underside, and a single white band and two apical black spots on hindwing underside.

Lesser Harlequin.Name: Lesser Harlequin
Lesser Harlequin.Description: Underside of both sexes orange-brown, with blue and black spots. Distinguishable from the Harlequin by spots on the forewing apex. Males are darkly coloured on the upperside while females have similar uppersides and undersides.

The Harlequin.Name: The Harlequin
The Harlequin.Description: Upperside of both sexes orange-brown, with silver and black spots. Distinguishable from the Lesser Harlequin by the lack of spots on its forewing apex. Males are darkly coloured on the upperside while females are similar on both sides.

Common Evening Brown.Name: Common Evening Brown
Common Evening Brown.Description: This medium-sized butterfly can be identified by distinctive wing shapes, eyespots and fine dark stripes on its underside.

Tawny Palmfly.Name: Tawny Palmfly
Tawny Palmfly.Description: Can be identified by its series of white-centred black spots on the underside of hindwings, appearing on a pale buff border.

Common Palmfly.Name: Common Palmfly
Common Palmfly.Description: Has an uneven wing border unlike the Pointed Palmfly and usually has a white costal spot on its hindwing.

Pointed Palmfly.Name: Pointed Palmfly
Pointed Palmfly.Description: Has the most pointed forewing apex and smoothest wing borders among all palmflies in Singapore.

Bamboo Tree Brown.Name: Bamboo Tree Brown
Bamboo Tree Brown.Description: Has lilac eyespots and white bands on its brown underside.

Malayan Bush Brown.Name: Malayan Bush Brown
Malayan Bush Brown.Description: The two reddish brown stripes on its orange underside allows it to be distinguished from other Bush Browns.

Dingy Bush Brown.Name: Dingy Bush Brown
Dingy Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains four relatively even-sized eyespots. The four hindwing eyespots closest to the dorsum are not aligned in a straight line, pointing slightly inwards, unlike in other bush browns.

Burmese Bush Brown.Name: Burmese Bush Brown
Burmese Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains one particularly large and several smaller eyespots. Distinguished from the Long Brand Bush Brown by its more jagged white band surrounding the eyespots and a more extended dark discal line in the hindwing.

Dark Brand Bush Brown.Name: Dark Brand Bush Brown
Dark Brand Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains two prominent and two obscure eyespots.

Long Brand Bush Brown.Name: Long Brand Bush Brown
Long Brand Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains one particularly large and several smaller eyespots. Distinguished from Mycalesis perseoides perseoides by its more regular white band surrounding the eyespots and a shorter dark discal line in the hindwing.

Purple Bush Brown.Name: Purple Bush Brown
Purple Bush Brown.Description: Can be identified by its yellow wash around the marginal areas on its underside. Forewing contains five relatively even-sized eyespots.

Dark Grass Brown.Name: Dark Grass Brown
Dark Grass Brown.Description: This butterfly resembles the bush browns, but has a more prominent white stripe on its dark brown underside. Has fewer, relatively larger eyespots.

Common Four-Ring.Name: Common Four-Ring
Common Four-Ring.Description: A small grey-brown butterfly with a mottled underside. Distinguishable from other ring butterflies by having four eyespots on the underside of its hindwings.

Malayan Six-Ring.Name: Malayan Six-Ring
Malayan Six-Ring.Description: Hindwing eyespots are small and lined up almost in a straight line. Has an additional eyespot compared to the five-rings.

Common Five-Ring.Name: Common Five-Ring
Common Five-Ring.Description: Lacks an eyespot compared to the Malayan Six-Ring. Second hindwing eyespot is always bigger than the first.

Malayan Five-Ring.Name: Malayan Five-Ring
Malayan Five-Ring.Description: Lacks an eyespot compared to the Malayan Six-Ring. Middle pair of eyespots on hindwings are smaller and separated.

Common Three-Ring.Name: Common Three-Ring
Common Three-Ring.Description: Small grey-brown butterfly with a mottled underside. Distinguishable from other ring butterflies by having three eyespots on the underside of its hindwings.

Bush Browns.Name: Bush Browns
Bush Browns.Description: Small, brown or orange-brown butterflies with a series of eyespots along their margins on the underside.

Mottled Emigrant.Name: Mottled Emigrant
Mottled Emigrant.Description: Underside greenish white with faint brown streaks, giving a mottled appearance. Upperside greenish white.

Lemon Emigrant.Name: Lemon Emigrant
Lemon Emigrant.Description: Represented by several forms; varied patterns present on wings. Distinguished from other emigrants by pale yellow or white upperside.

Orange Emigrant.Name: Orange Emigrant
Orange Emigrant.Description: Underside pale yellow. Upperside forewing white while hindwing deep orange.

No Brand Grass Yellow.Name: No Brand Grass Yellow
No Brand Grass Yellow.Description: Has no cell spots on underside forewing and many tiny freckles throughout underside.

Common Grass Yellow.Name: Common Grass Yellow
Common Grass Yellow.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside lacks the large brown apical spot found in the Forest Grass Yellow.

Forest Grass Yellow.Name: Forest Grass Yellow
Forest Grass Yellow.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside has a large partially divided, brown apical spot.

Three Spot Grass Yellow.Name: Three Spot Grass Yellow
Three Spot Grass Yellow.Description: Has three cell spots on underside forewing.

Anderson\u2019s Grass Yellow.Name: Anderson’s Grass Yellow
Anderson\u2019s Grass Yellow.Description: Has a single cell spot on underside of forewing.  Unlike the Chocolate Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is not completely darkened on the underside.

Chocolate Grass Yellow.Name: Chocolate Grass Yellow
Chocolate Grass Yellow.Description: Has a single cell spot on its forewing underside.  Unlike the Anderson's Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is completely darkened on the underside.

Grass Yellows.Name: Grass Yellows
Grass Yellows.Description: Small yellow butterflies with irregular black borders on the upperside and small dark spots on the underside.

Plain Tiger.Name: Plain Tiger
Plain Tiger.Description: The only tiger butterfly in Singapore without veins on both sides of hindwing. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white.

Common Tiger.Name: Common Tiger
Common Tiger.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins and exists in two forms. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white. Submarginal bands narrower than Black Veined Tiger

Black Veined Tiger.Name: Black Veined Tiger
Black Veined Tiger.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins. Unlike the Common Tiger, its hindwing is white without any orange. With a broader sub-marginal border than the Common Tiger.

Dark Glassy Tiger.Name: Dark Glassy Tiger
Dark Glassy Tiger.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Blue Glassy Tiger, but differs in direction of black streak within its forewing cell.

Blue Glassy Tiger.Name: Blue Glassy Tiger
Blue Glassy Tiger.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Dark Glassy Tiger, but has a black bar transversing its forewing cell.

Tawny Coster.Name: Tawny Coster
Tawny Coster.Description: Orange upperside with a black border and black spots, but paler in females. Its thorax and hindwing border are black with white spots.

Leopard.Name: Leopard
Leopard.Description: Orange-brown on upperside with many black spots. Underside a lighter shade of orange with a purplish sheen in the side light.

Lesser Grass Blue.Name: Lesser Grass Blue
Lesser Grass Blue.Description: Upperside purplish-blue in males, while brown in females. The misaligned spot in the hindwing helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Pygmy Grass Blue.Name: Pygmy Grass Blue
Pygmy Grass Blue.Description: Upperside of males dull blue, while dark brown in females. The V-shaped marking on the forewing sub-apical region helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Pale Grass Blue.Name: Pale Grass Blue
Pale Grass Blue.Description: Upperside of males light blue, while dark greyish-blue in females. The more pronounced spots on the underside, particularly the sub-marginal spots along both wings help distinguish it from the other grass blues.

Grass Blues.Name: Grass Blues
Grass Blues.Description: Extremely small butterflies with a black spotted pale grey underside. Upperside blue or brown depending on sex and species.

Blues and Caeruleans.Name: Blues and Caeruleans
Blues and Caeruleans.Description: The group of butterflies with a shining blue or brown upperside and grey undersides marked with streaks and bands.

Chocolate Pansy.Name: Chocolate Pansy
Chocolate Pansy.Description: Upperside reddish brown, while underside dark brown. Both sides are lined with orange eyespots.

Peacock Pansy.Name: Peacock Pansy
Peacock Pansy.Description: Orange on both sides, but slightly paler on the underside. Both sides contain prominent eyespots.

Blue Pansy (M).Name: Blue Pansy (M)
Blue Pansy (M).Description: The male Blue Pansy has a bright blue hindwing on the upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots observed on both sides.

Blue Pansy (F).Name: Blue Pansy (F)
Blue Pansy (F).Description: The female Blue Pansy has a sombre brown upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots can be observed on both sides.

Common Birdwing.Name: Common Birdwing
Common Birdwing.Description: Similar to Malayan Birdwing, but with primarily dark forewing, sometimes with faint whitish streaks. Females have many black spots on hindwing.

Common Rose.Name: Common Rose
Common Rose.Description: Has a diagnostic red body and a full series of red spots along underside margins of hindwing.

Common Mime.Name: Common Mime
Common Mime.Description: A moderately large butterfly with black and white stripes.

Lime Butterfly.Name: Lime Butterfly
Lime Butterfly.Description: Upperside black with pale yellow spots and band; underside yellow with distinctive orange spots encircled by blue and black edges.

Common Mormon.Name: Common Mormon
Common Mormon.Description: Tailed, with prominent white band across entire underside of hindwing. Females vary in form. The cyrus form resembles the male, but with red tornal bar.

Common Mormon (F).Name: Common Mormon (F)
Common Mormon (F).Description: Females of the polytes form mimick the Common Rose, but lacks red body. Central white patch and  series of red spots along margin on underside of hindwings.

Painted Jezebel.Name: Painted Jezebel
Painted Jezebel.Description: Has red, white and yellow patches on underside. Base of hindwing is yellow on the underside.

Psyche.Name: Psyche
Psyche.Description: Small, has rounded wings with thin green-grey streaks on underside, giving a mottled appearance.

Striped Albatross (M).Name: Striped Albatross (M)
Striped Albatross (M).Description: Males white with black veins on underside. Underside of females dusted with yellow and brown colours.

Striped Albatross (F).Name: Striped Albatross (F)
Striped Albatross (F).Description: Males white with black veins on underside. Underside of females dusted with yellow and brown colours.

Common Palmfly.Name: Common Palmfly
Common Palmfly.Description: Has an uneven wing border unlike the Pointed Palmfly and usually has a white costal spot on its hindwing.

Malayan Bush Brown.Name: Malayan Bush Brown
Malayan Bush Brown.Description: The two reddish brown stripes on its orange underside allows it to be distinguished from other Bush Browns.

Dingy Bush Brown.Name: Dingy Bush Brown
Dingy Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains four relatively even-sized eyespots. The four hindwing eyespots closest to the dorsum are not aligned in a straight line, pointing slightly inwards, unlike in other bush browns.

Burmese Bush Brown.Name: Burmese Bush Brown
Burmese Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains one particularly large and several smaller eyespots. Distinguished from the Long Brand Bush Brown by its more jagged white band surrounding the eyespots and a more extended dark discal line in the hindwing.

Dark Brand Bush Brown.Name: Dark Brand Bush Brown
Dark Brand Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains two prominent and two obscure eyespots.

Long Brand Bush Brown.Name: Long Brand Bush Brown
Long Brand Bush Brown.Description: Forewing underside contains one particularly large and several smaller eyespots. Distinguished from Mycalesis perseoides perseoides by its more regular white band surrounding the eyespots and a shorter dark discal line in the hindwing.

Purple Bush Brown.Name: Purple Bush Brown
Purple Bush Brown.Description: Can be identified by its yellow wash around the marginal areas on its underside. Forewing contains five relatively even-sized eyespots.

Dark Grass Brown.Name: Dark Grass Brown
Dark Grass Brown.Description: This butterfly resembles the bush browns, but has a more prominent white stripe on its dark brown underside. Has fewer, relatively larger eyespots.

Common Four-Ring.Name: Common Four-Ring
Common Four-Ring.Description: A small grey-brown butterfly with a mottled underside. Distinguishable from other ring butterflies by having four eyespots on the underside of its hindwings.

Malayan Six-Ring.Name: Malayan Six-Ring
Malayan Six-Ring.Description: Hindwing eyespots are small and lined up almost in a straight line. Has an additional eyespot compared to the five-rings.

Common Five-Ring.Name: Common Five-Ring
Common Five-Ring.Description: Lacks an eyespot compared to the Malayan Six-Ring. Second hindwing eyespot is always bigger than the first.

Malayan Five-Ring.Name: Malayan Five-Ring
Malayan Five-Ring.Description: Lacks an eyespot compared to the Malayan Six-Ring. Middle pair of eyespots on hindwings are smaller and separated.

Common Three-Ring.Name: Common Three-Ring
Common Three-Ring.Description: Small grey-brown butterfly with a mottled underside. Distinguishable from other ring butterflies by having three eyespots on the underside of its hindwings.

Bush Browns.Name: Bush Browns
Bush Browns.Description: Small, brown or orange-brown butterflies with a series of eyespots along their margins on the underside.

Malayan Grisette.Name: Malayan Grisette
Malayan Grisette.Description: This damselfy is generally restricted to forested areas of the nature reserves. It is light brownish throughout with pale spots along the abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance, but the female is paler.

Common Flashwing.Name: Common Flashwing
Common Flashwing.Description: This common large damselfly has distinct transparent wings with a bluish iridescence. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Charming Flashwing.Name: Charming Flashwing
Charming Flashwing.Description: Similar to the Common Flashwing, the two species can only be distinguished by their male anal appendages. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Fiery Gem.Name: Fiery Gem
Fiery Gem.Description: The male of this striking species has a stout red abdomen, and yellow markings on its black thorax. It has a dark apical spot on its forewings. Females have yellowish or greyish-olive markings on its black thorax and abdomen.

Clearwing Gem (M).Name: Clearwing Gem (M)
Clearwing Gem (M).Description: This rare species has only been recorded at Nee Soon freshwater swamp forest. Mature males have a bluish-purple abdomen. Immature males have a bluish-grey abdomen.

Clearwing Gem (F).Name: Clearwing Gem (F)
Clearwing Gem (F).Description: Mature females have a dark abdomen with pale markings on the thorax.

Golden Gem (M).Name: Golden Gem (M)
Golden Gem (M).Description: Males of this species can be identified by the bright yellow segments on its abdomen. They also have a dark apical spot on their forewings.

Golden Gem (F).Name: Golden Gem (F)
Golden Gem (F).Description: Females of this species is are light greenish. They also have a dark apical spot on their forewings.

Blue Slim.Name: Blue Slim
Blue Slim.Description: This is a very rare species in Singapore, and has only beeen occasionally encountered in the Central Catchment and Bukit Timah Nature Reserves, as well as Pulau Tekong.

Variable Wisp (M).Name: Variable Wisp (M)
Variable Wisp (M).Description: Individuals of this species change colour as they mature. Young males have a greenish thorax, and a black abdomen with an orange tip. They will lose this orange tip as they mature. Mature males have a white thorax and a dark coloured abdomen.

Variable Wisp (F).Name: Variable Wisp (F)
Variable Wisp (F).Description: Immature females are red, and become olive as they mature. Mature females look like young males, but are duller in colour.

Dwarf Wisp (M).Name: Dwarf Wisp (M)
Dwarf Wisp (M).Description: This is the smallest damselfly in Singapore. Males have a blue thorax and abdomen.

Dwarf Wisp (F).Name: Dwarf Wisp (F)
Dwarf Wisp (F).Description: Females have a green thorax and blue abdomen.

Wandering Wisp.Name: Wandering Wisp
Wandering Wisp.Description: Similar to the Variable Wisp, this species changes colour as it matures. Males lose the orange tip at the end of their abdomen and the thorax takes on a blue-white colouration. Females start off reddish-brown, and become increasingly green.

Will-o-Wisp (M).Name: Will-o-Wisp (M)
Will-o-Wisp (M).Description: This uncommon species can be found near swamp forests. It has a very slender abdomen. Males have a metallic green thorax and almost translucent anal appendages.

Will-o-Wisp (F).Name: Will-o-Wisp (F)
Will-o-Wisp (F).Description: Immature females are red while mature females are olive green.

Blue-nosed Sprite.Name: Blue-nosed Sprite
Blue-nosed Sprite.Description: This species has blue markings on its abdomen and thorax, and is a relatively weak flier. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Rebecca's Sprite.Name: Rebecca's Sprite
Rebecca's Sprite.Description: The Rebecca's Sprite is similar to the Violet Sprite, but has lighter blue markings.

Violet Sprite.Name: Violet Sprite
Violet Sprite.Description: Violet Sprites have prominent blue markings on their thorax and the end of the abdomens. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Variable Sprite (M).Name: Variable Sprite (M)
Variable Sprite (M).Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Mature males are dark with bright blue markings on their abdomen and thorax.

Variable Sprite (F).Name: Variable Sprite (F)
Variable Sprite (F).Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Adult females lack the blue markings at the ends of their abdomens, which males have.

Fiery Coraltail (M).Name: Fiery Coraltail (M)
Fiery Coraltail (M).Description: Males have a bright red abdomen.

Fiery Coraltail (F).Name: Fiery Coraltail (F)
Fiery Coraltail (F).Description: Females are a dark olive green.

Ornate Coraltail.Name: Ornate Coraltail
Ornate Coraltail.Description: This species has a pale blue head and thorax, and a dark abdomen with orange markings on both ends. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Common Bluetail (M).Name: Common Bluetail (M)
Common Bluetail (M).Description: Males have green markings on their thorax, and blue markings on the last two segments of their abdomen.

Common Bluetail (F).Name: Common Bluetail (F)
Common Bluetail (F).Description: Females have a few morphs: one generally olive green, and the other with a orange thorax. Females can also look similar to males.

Arthur's Midget (M).Name: Arthur's Midget (M)
Arthur's Midget (M).Description: Males could either have yellow or blue stripes on their thorax.

Arthur's Midget (F).Name: Arthur's Midget (F)
Arthur's Midget (F).Description: Females are dark with blue stripes on their thorax, but are generally paler compared to the males.

Hooked Midget (M).Name: Hooked Midget (M)
Hooked Midget (M).Description: Looks similar to the Arthur's Midget, although males can be discerned by their down-curved superior appendages.

Hooked Midget (F).Name: Hooked Midget (F)
Hooked Midget (F).Description: Females have a reddish-brown thorax with blue stripes.

Shorttail (M).Name: Shorttail (M)
Shorttail (M).Description: This species has a short abdomen and dense spines on its long legs. Mature males have a purplish-blue thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Shorttail (F).Name: Shorttail (F)
Shorttail (F).Description: Mature females are dark with yellowish-white stripes on the thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Dryad.Name: Dryad
Dryad.Description: The Dryad has a long abdomen and a thorax which is yellow on both sides and black on top. Males have short, dark brown wing tips. Females have white wing tips.

Look-alike Sprite (M).Name: Look-alike Sprite (M)
Look-alike Sprite (M).Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Males have blue eyes and thorax, and blue markings on their abdomen.

Look-alike Sprite (F).Name: Look-alike Sprite (F)
Look-alike Sprite (F).Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Females are light brownish-yellow.

Blue Sprite (M).Name: Blue Sprite (M)
Blue Sprite (M).Description: Males have a bright blue thorax, abdomen and eyes.

Blue Sprite (F).Name: Blue Sprite (F)
Blue Sprite (F).Description: Females are light brown with green markings.

Grey Sprite.Name: Grey Sprite
Grey Sprite.Description: Males have a bright blue thorax, abdomen and eyes. Females are light brown with green markings.

Orange-faced Sprite.Name: Orange-faced Sprite
Orange-faced Sprite.Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have orange faces. Orange-faced Sprites have only been recorded in Nee Soon Freshwater Swamp Forest and Toa Payoh Town Garden. Females are orange-yellow from head to thorax.

Red-tailed Sprite.Name: Red-tailed Sprite
Red-tailed Sprite.Description: The Red-tailed Sprite has a red thorax, and a largely dark abdomen which is red on the last few segments. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Blue-sided Satinwing (M).Name: Blue-sided Satinwing (M)
Blue-sided Satinwing (M).Description: Males have a thorax with blue-coloured sides, and a distinct dark patch on their hindwings.

Blue-sided Satinwing (F).Name: Blue-sided Satinwing (F)
Blue-sided Satinwing (F).Description: Females have an olive-grey and black thorax, with wings that are narrow and clear.

Crenulated Spreadwing.Name: Crenulated Spreadwing
Crenulated Spreadwing.Description: This species prefers open habitats such as reservoirs and large ponds, and typically rests with its wings held open. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Blue-spotted Flatwing.Name: Blue-spotted Flatwing
Blue-spotted Flatwing.Description: This species has bright blue markings on their thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

White-tailed Sylvan (M).Name: White-tailed Sylvan (M)
White-tailed Sylvan (M).Description: As its name suggests, the White-tailed Sylvan has a distinct white 'tip' at the end of its abdomen.

White-tailed Sylvan (F).Name: White-tailed Sylvan (F)
White-tailed Sylvan (F).Description: Females of this species have a dorsally brown abdomen.

Telephone Sylvan.Name: Telephone Sylvan
Telephone Sylvan.Description: This damselfly gets its curious name from the markings on top of its thorax, which resembles two telephone handsets facing each other. The female's telephone-shaped markings are not as clearly seen and at times fragmented.

Yellow Featherlegs.Name: Yellow Featherlegs
Yellow Featherlegs.Description: This species gets its name from its yellow legs. It is commonly found near streams and swamps near forest edges. Immatures individuals have white bodies and legs. Males and females are similar in appearance, but females are paler in colour.

Variable Featherlegs.Name: Variable Featherlegs
Variable Featherlegs.Description: This species has yellow legs, similar to the Yellow Featherlegs, but has irregular green markings on its thorax. It has fewer white markings on its abdomen tip than do the Yellow Featherlegs. Immature individuals are mostly white, and are known as "ghost forms". Males and females are similar in appearance, except females are brownish where the males are black.

Singapore Shadowdamsel.Name: Singapore Shadowdamsel
Singapore Shadowdamsel.Description: This species was first found in Singapore and was only recently found in Johor. The 8th and 9th segments of the male's abdomen are blue. Females have a very small blue colouration at the tip of its abdomen.

Collared Threadtail (M).Name: Collared Threadtail (M)
Collared Threadtail (M).Description: This species may be confused with the Crescent Threadtail, but can be identified by its blue anal appendages.

Collared Threadtail (F).Name: Collared Threadtail (F)
Collared Threadtail (F).Description: Females are paler and have narrower stripes on the thorax.

Orange-striped Threadtail (M).Name: Orange-striped Threadtail (M)
Orange-striped Threadtail (M).Description: The males of this species have orange stripes on its thorax.

Orange-striped Threadtail (F).Name: Orange-striped Threadtail (F)
Orange-striped Threadtail (F).Description: Females have pale stripes which are not orange.

Interrupted Threadtail.Name: Interrupted Threadtail
Interrupted Threadtail.Description: Males have interrupted (broken) blue bands on the top of their thorax, and blue markings on the end of their abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance, but females are paler in colour.

Crescent Threadtail (M).Name: Crescent Threadtail (M)
Crescent Threadtail (M).Description: This species may be confused with the Collared Threadtail, but can be identified by its black anal appendages.

Crescent Threadtail (F).Name: Crescent Threadtail (F)
Crescent Threadtail (F).Description: Females have narrower blue markings on the thorax.

Emperor.Name: Emperor
Emperor.Description: This large species has a dark abdomen and a blue-green thorax. Emperor females lay their eggs in plant tissue. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Spoon-tailed Duskhawker.Name: Spoon-tailed Duskhawker
Spoon-tailed Duskhawker.Description: The distinguishing feature of this rare species is its spoon-shaped anal appendages. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Small Duskhawker.Name: Small Duskhawker
Small Duskhawker.Description: A rare species in Singapore, this duskhawker has a dark abdomen with a green thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Spear-tail Duskhawker.Name: Spear-tail Duskhawker
Spear-tail Duskhawker.Description: This is a rare forest species and has a pair of bright green eyes and thorax. The shape of its abdomen is similar to that of the Dingy Duskhawker. The inferior appendage is largely yellowish-white. Females are duller.

Dingy Duskhawker.Name: Dingy Duskhawker
Dingy Duskhawker.Description: This species can be found in rainforests, and can be recognised by its distinct, dark T-shaped mark on the upper surface of the frons. Females are paler.

Nighthawker.Name: Nighthawker
Nighthawker.Description: Males have a bright green thorax, while females are generally brownish.

Lesser Nighthawker.Name: Lesser Nighthawker
Lesser Nighthawker.Description: The Lesser Nighthawker is similar to the Spear-tail Duskhawker, except the former has anal appendages that are flat and broad. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Giant Hawker.Name: Giant Hawker
Giant Hawker.Description: A rarely seen species, this large dragonfly has a reddish-brown body. Males have a brown streak on each long, broad wing. Females are bigger, more commonly seen than males, and have large dark patches near the tips of all its wings.

Pond Cruiser.Name: Pond Cruiser
Pond Cruiser.Description: This large species has yellow markings on its dark thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Stream Cruiser (M).Name: Stream Cruiser (M)
Stream Cruiser (M).Description: The Stream Cruiser has large blue-green eyes and a distinct white line across the thorax between its wings.

Stream Cruiser (F).Name: Stream Cruiser (F)
Stream Cruiser (F).Description: Males and females are similar in appearance.

Lesser Stream Cruiser.Name: Lesser Stream Cruiser
Lesser Stream Cruiser.Description: This species is similar to the Stream Cruiser, but can be distinguished by a yellow band at the base of its abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance, but females have a larger body.

Emerald.Name: Emerald
Emerald.Description: This very rare species has a slender abdomen and is generally a dark metallic green. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Shadowdancer.Name: Shadowdancer
Shadowdancer.Description: The Shadowdancer is a small species with brilliant green eyes, an emerald thorax and a dark abdomen. There is a yellow band at the side of its green thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Lesser Splayed Clubtail.Name: Lesser Splayed Clubtail
Lesser Splayed Clubtail.Description: This species has prominent yellow markings on its mostly-black thorax and abdomen.

Malayan Grappletail.Name: Malayan Grappletail
Malayan Grappletail.Description: This species has blue-green eyes and a green-sided thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Common Flangetail.Name: Common Flangetail
Common Flangetail.Description: The Common Flangetail is common in open habitats. It has green-yellow bands on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Ris' Clubtail.Name: Ris' Clubtail
Ris' Clubtail.Description: This species has a slender abdomen that is mostly black, and has two yellow strips on the sides of its thorax.

Forktail.Name: Forktail
Forktail.Description: The front part of the thorax has two large yellow squarish patches, and the abdomen has several orange rings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Malayan Spineleg.Name: Malayan Spineleg
Malayan Spineleg.Description: The Malayan Spineleg has green-yellow stripes on the top and side of its thorax. The superior anal appendages are whitish.

Tiny Sheartail.Name: Tiny Sheartail
Tiny Sheartail.Description: This species has a yellow triangular patch on either side of its thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Banded Hooktail.Name: Banded Hooktail
Banded Hooktail.Description: This species has a rather stout abdomen with thick yellow stripes. It has unique scimitar-like appendages. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Trumpet Tail (M).Name: Trumpet Tail (M)
Trumpet Tail (M).Description: The Trumpet Tail has a trumpet-shaped abdomen. Males are blue with dark markings.

Trumpet Tail (F).Name: Trumpet Tail (F)
Trumpet Tail (F).Description: Females are greenish-yellow with similar markings as males.

Blue Adjudant.Name: Blue Adjudant
Blue Adjudant.Description: The Blue Adjudant is a small dragonfly. The thorax and part of the abdomen of both the mature male and female are bright blue. In the male, the last four abdominal segments are dark. In the female, the last five abdominal segments are dark.

Scarlet Adjudant (M).Name: Scarlet Adjudant (M)
Scarlet Adjudant (M).Description: The Scarlet Adjudant is a small red dragonfly. Males have a short bright red abdomen. The "knees" on the hind legs are red in colour.

Scarlet Adjudant (F).Name: Scarlet Adjudant (F)
Scarlet Adjudant (F).Description: Females are brown-yellow with yellowish "knees" on the hind legs.

Pond Adjudant (M).Name: Pond Adjudant (M)
Pond Adjudant (M).Description: The Pond Adjudant male is a small powdery blue dragonfly. It can be differentiated from the larger Blue Dasher by how only the last two abdominal segments are dark.

Pond Adjudant (F).Name: Pond Adjudant (F)
Pond Adjudant (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown with black markings.

Grenadier.Name: Grenadier
Grenadier.Description: This species has mottled yellow markings on its thorax and the top half of its abdomen is red. Females are similar in appearance to the males, but slightly duller.

Handsome Grenadier (M).Name: Handsome Grenadier (M)
Handsome Grenadier (M).Description: Males have distinct blue, black and red segments on the abdomen.

Handsome Grenadier (F).Name: Handsome Grenadier (F)
Handsome Grenadier (F).Description: Females are mostly dark with dull yellowish-orange markings.

Blue Dasher (M).Name: Blue Dasher (M)
Blue Dasher (M).Description: This species has a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males have a powdery blue body with a black tip on its abdomen (on the last three abdominal segments).

Blue Dasher (F).Name: Blue Dasher (F)
Blue Dasher (F).Description: Females are brownish-yellow with a dark streak along its abdomen.

Pixie (M).Name: Pixie (M)
Pixie (M).Description: The males of this rare species are mainly orange with a white patch on the abdomen. The last three segments are black.

Pixie (F).Name: Pixie (F)
Pixie (F).Description: The females of this rare species are light brown.

Common Amberwing (M).Name: Common Amberwing (M)
Common Amberwing (M).Description: Males have a reddish-gold tint on their wings and have an orange abdomen. Immature males are similar to females in appearance.

Common Amberwing (F).Name: Common Amberwing (F)
Common Amberwing (F).Description: Females are light brown and have yellowish-orange wing spots.

Sultan.Name: Sultan
Sultan.Description: Males of this large species have a distinct red patch on one-third of the wings. Females of this large species are brownish-orange.

Green-eyed Percher.Name: Green-eyed Percher
Green-eyed Percher.Description: This species is uniformly dark blue and has a thin abdomen with a slightly swollen base. The female is similar to the male in appearance.

Lined Forest-skimmer.Name: Lined Forest-skimmer
Lined Forest-skimmer.Description: The Lined Forest-skimmer has yellow stripes on its thorax. Only females have dark wing tips.

Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (M).Name: Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (M)
Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (M).Description: Both males and females have dark wing tips and a dark blue body, with a broken yellow line along the thorax.

Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (F).Name: Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (F)
Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (F).Description: Females can be distinguished by the lack of the light blue segments on their abdomen.

Common Scarlet (M).Name: Common Scarlet (M)
Common Scarlet (M).Description: Males are red with a dark line along the abdomen, which distinguishes them from the Common Redbolt.

Common Scarlet (F).Name: Common Scarlet (F)
Common Scarlet (F).Description: Females have a light brown body with a similar dark line along its abdomen.

Black-tipped Percher (M).Name: Black-tipped Percher (M)
Black-tipped Percher (M).Description: Males are blue with dark wing tips. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Black-tipped Percher (F).Name: Black-tipped Percher (F)
Black-tipped Percher (F).Description: Females are yellow with a dark band down their abdomen. The wings are clear. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Blue Percher (M).Name: Blue Percher (M)
Blue Percher (M).Description: Males are mostly dark blue, with the last three abdominal segments black. They have distinct white anal appendages. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Blue Percher (F).Name: Blue Percher (F)
Blue Percher (F).Description: Females have yellow-green markings on both the thorax and abdomen, as well as distinct white anal appendages. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Water Monarch.Name: Water Monarch
Water Monarch.Description: This species is brownish and has an irregular dark band on its hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Restless Demon.Name: Restless Demon
Restless Demon.Description: This rare species has a blackish thorax and dark-bluish abdomen. Its wings are dark at the tips and base. The female is paler and less commonly observed.

Scarlet Grenadier.Name: Scarlet Grenadier
Scarlet Grenadier.Description: The Scarlet Grenadier has a yellow-striped thorax and bright red abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Coastal Glider (M).Name: Coastal Glider (M)
Coastal Glider (M).Description: Males are red with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark line is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'. Immature males and females are similar in appearance.

Coastal Glider (F).Name: Coastal Glider (F)
Coastal Glider (F).Description: Females are orange-yellow with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark line is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'.

Scarlet Pygmy (M).Name: Scarlet Pygmy (M)
Scarlet Pygmy (M).Description: This is the smallest dragonfly in Singapore. Males have a bright red abdomen and thorax. The immature male has a brownish-yellow body.

Scarlet Pygmy (F).Name: Scarlet Pygmy (F)
Scarlet Pygmy (F).Description: This is the smallest dragonfly in Singapore. Females are mostly dark with white bands across the abdomen.

Striped Grenadier.Name: Striped Grenadier
Striped Grenadier.Description: Males of this species have a distinct red lower abdomen with black bands, and a thorax with yellow stripes. Females have a dark brown abdomen and similar markings as males do on their thorax. Immature females have a red abdomen.

Common Parasol (M).Name: Common Parasol (M)
Common Parasol (M).Description: Males have a dark red colouration on their wings and clear wing tips. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Common Parasol (F).Name: Common Parasol (F)
Common Parasol (F).Description: Females are light brown with dark markings along the sides of its abdomen. Its wings are clear. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Riverhawk.Name: Riverhawk
Riverhawk.Description: A very rare species with a mostly dark body and yellow markings on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Blue Sentinel.Name: Blue Sentinel
Blue Sentinel.Description: This rare species has only been recorded at Nee Soon freshwater swamp forest. The male looks similar to the blue form of the Variable Sentinel, but it has a thinner, longer abdomen with more white colour.

Variable Sentinel (M).Name: Variable Sentinel (M)
Variable Sentinel (M).Description: This species has many colour morphs and males can have a red abdomen with or without white markings, or a black abdomen with white markings.

Variable Sentinel (F).Name: Variable Sentinel (F)
Variable Sentinel (F).Description: This species has many colour morphs and females can either be red or dark-coloured, or be yellow when young.

Spine-tufted Skimmer (M).Name: Spine-tufted Skimmer (M)
Spine-tufted Skimmer (M).Description: This species can be easily confused with the Scarlet Skimmer, but can be distinguished by its brown thorax and dark grey eyes.

Common Blue Skimmer (M).Name: Common Blue Skimmer (M)
Common Blue Skimmer (M).Description: While adult males have a generally blue body with a darkened tip, immature males are usually yellow-brown and resemble the females.

Slender Blue Skimmer (M).Name: Slender Blue Skimmer (M)
Slender Blue Skimmer (M).Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have a slender blue abdomen and also posess light blue eyes. Immature males and females are light brown.

Variegated Green Skimmer.Name: Variegated Green Skimmer
Variegated Green Skimmer.Description: This common species can be found in many habitats, and has distinct yellowish-green markings on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Scarlet Skimmer (M).Name: Scarlet Skimmer (M)
Scarlet Skimmer (M).Description: Males have a bright red thorax and abdomen and a red patch near the base of their wings.

Scarlet Skimmer (F).Name: Scarlet Skimmer (F)
Scarlet Skimmer (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown with clear wings.

Wandering Glider.Name: Wandering Glider
Wandering Glider.Description: This common species can often be seen flying in open areas and is one of the most widespread species in the world. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Mangrove Marshal.Name: Mangrove Marshal
Mangrove Marshal.Description: This species is mostly found in mangroves. Mature males have a white pruinescence on their thorax. Females have a thorax with olive colour on its sides.

Common Chaser (M).Name: Common Chaser (M)
Common Chaser (M).Description: Males have a striking blue thorax with a yellow and black abdomen.

Common Chaser (F).Name: Common Chaser (F)
Common Chaser (F).Description: Females have black and yellow stripes on their thorax. The abdomen is black with dull orange markings. Notably, it has conspicuous flaps near the tip of the abdomen.

Banded Skimmer (M).Name: Banded Skimmer (M)
Banded Skimmer (M).Description: Males are black with a white patch on the first few segments of their abdomens.

Banded Skimmer (F).Name: Banded Skimmer (F)
Banded Skimmer (F).Description: Females have a yellow abdomen with black markings.

Mangrove Dwarf (M).Name: Mangrove Dwarf (M)
Mangrove Dwarf (M).Description: This species looks similar to the Blue Dasher but is smaller and does not have the amber tint at the base of its wings. Found only in mangrove areas.

Mangrove Dwarf (F).Name: Mangrove Dwarf (F)
Mangrove Dwarf (F).Description: Females have yellow markings along the thorax and the abdomen. Found only in mangrove areas.

Common Redbolt (M).Name: Common Redbolt (M)
Common Redbolt (M).Description: Males are bright red throughout, including the eyes.

Common Redbolt (F).Name: Common Redbolt (F)
Common Redbolt (F).Description: Females are brown with a bright yellow streak that extends from the thorax to the top of the abdomen.

Bronze Flutterer.Name: Bronze Flutterer
Bronze Flutterer.Description: The Bronze Flutterer has striking opaque iridescent wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Yellow-barred Flutterer.Name: Yellow-barred Flutterer
Yellow-barred Flutterer.Description: This is one of the easiest species to identify with a distinct dark-coloured and yellow pattern on the base of its hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Sapphire Flutterer.Name: Sapphire Flutterer
Sapphire Flutterer.Description: The Sapphire Flutterer can be easily identified by the blue patches on its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Potbellied Elf.Name: Potbellied Elf
Potbellied Elf.Description: This rare species is restricted to swampy forests. A distinctive feature is its curved abdomen which is swollen at the first two segments. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Elf.Name: Elf
Elf.Description: This species looks similar to the Potbellied Elf, but does not have a curved abdomen. Females are similar in appearance to the male, but has a thicker abdomen and greater amount of yellow markings.

White-barred Duskhawk (M).Name: White-barred Duskhawk (M)
White-barred Duskhawk (M).Description: Males have a distinct light brown and white patch on their hindwings. Immature males lack this wing pattern and are generally pale brown, similar to the female in appearance.

White-barred Duskhawk (F).Name: White-barred Duskhawk (F)
White-barred Duskhawk (F).Description: Females are generally pale brown with clear wings.

Saddlebag Glider.Name: Saddlebag Glider
Saddlebag Glider.Description: The veins on the base of this species' hindwings are red. Two black spots are present at tip of its abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Crimson Dropwing (M).Name: Crimson Dropwing (M)
Crimson Dropwing (M).Description: Males have a luminous pink abdomen, red wing veins and an amber tint at the wing base.

Crimson Dropwing (F).Name: Crimson Dropwing (F)
Crimson Dropwing (F).Description: Females are light brown with yellow veins on the base of their hindwings, and black markings along the sides of their abdomen.

Indigo Dropwing (M).Name: Indigo Dropwing (M)
Indigo Dropwing (M).Description: This common species can be found near streams and rivers. Males are dark blue, and have a half-blackish abdoment with yellow spots.

Indigo Dropwing (F).Name: Indigo Dropwing (F)
Indigo Dropwing (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown with dark markings on the thorax and abdomen.

Dancing Dropwing.Name: Dancing Dropwing
Dancing Dropwing.Description: This species has distinct yellow markings on its thorax and abdomen, and a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Treehugger (M).Name: Treehugger (M)
Treehugger (M).Description: Males are very distinct with their blue bodies and broad metallic blue patch at the base of their hindwings.

Treehugger (F).Name: Treehugger (F)
Treehugger (F).Description: Females are light brown and have black markings on their abdomens.

Scarlet Basker (M).Name: Scarlet Basker (M)
Scarlet Basker (M).Description: Males have two diamond-shaped spots at the end of the abdomen.

Scarlet Basker (F).Name: Scarlet Basker (F)
Scarlet Basker (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown in colour with an amber patch at the base of the hindwings.

Slender Duskdarter.Name: Slender Duskdarter
Slender Duskdarter.Description: Males have green eyes, and a slender abdomen. Females have a slightly thicker abdomen. The species is most active at dusk and dawn.

Variable Wisp (M).Name: Variable Wisp (M)
Variable Wisp (M).Description: Individuals of this species change colour as they mature. Young males have a greenish thorax, and a black abdomen with an orange tip. They will lose this orange tip as they mature. Mature males have a white thorax and a dark coloured abdomen.

Variable Wisp (F).Name: Variable Wisp (F)
Variable Wisp (F).Description: Immature females are red, and become olive as they mature. Mature females look like young males, but are duller in colour.

Variable Sprite (M).Name: Variable Sprite (M)
Variable Sprite (M).Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Mature males are dark with bright blue markings on their abdomen and thorax.

Variable Sprite (F).Name: Variable Sprite (F)
Variable Sprite (F).Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Adult females lack the blue markings at the ends of their abdomen which males have.

Fiery Coraltail (M).Name: Fiery Coraltail (M)
Fiery Coraltail (M).Description: Males have a bright red abdomen.

Fiery Coraltail (F).Name: Fiery Coraltail (F)
Fiery Coraltail (F).Description: Females of this species are a dark olive green.

Ornate Coraltail.Name: Ornate Coraltail
Ornate Coraltail.Description: This species has a pale blue head and thorax, and a dark abdomen with orange markings on both ends. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Common Bluetail (M).Name: Common Bluetail (M)
Common Bluetail (M).Description: Males have green markings on their thorax, and blue markings on the last two segments of their abdomen.

Common Bluetail (F).Name: Common Bluetail (F)
Common Bluetail (F).Description: Females have a few morphs: one generally olive green, and the other with a orange thorax. Females can also look similar to males.

Arthur's Midget (M).Name: Arthur's Midget (M)
Arthur's Midget (M).Description: Males could have either yellow or blue stripes on their thorax.

Arthur's Midget (F).Name: Arthur's Midget (F)
Arthur's Midget (F).Description: Females are dark with blue stripes on their thorax, but are generally paler compared to the males.

Shorttail (M).Name: Shorttail (M)
Shorttail (M).Description: This species has a short abdomen and dense spines on its long legs. Mature males have a purplish blue thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Shorttail (F).Name: Shorttail (F)
Shorttail (F).Description: This species has a short abdomen and dense spines on its long legs. Mature females are dark with yellowish-white stripes on the thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Look-alike Sprite (M).Name: Look-alike Sprite (M)
Look-alike Sprite (M).Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Males have blue eyes and thorax, and blue markings on their abdomen.

Look-alike Sprite (F).Name: Look-alike Sprite (F)
Look-alike Sprite (F).Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Females are light brownish-yellow.

Blue Sprite (M).Name: Blue Sprite (M)
Blue Sprite (M).Description: Males have a bright blue thorax, abdomen and eyes.

Blue Sprite (F).Name: Blue Sprite (F)
Blue Sprite (F).Description: Females are light brown with green markings.

Orange-faced Sprite.Name: Orange-faced Sprite
Orange-faced Sprite.Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have orange faces. Orange-faced Sprites have only been recorded in Nee Soon Freshwater Swamp Forest and Toa Payoh Town Garden. Females are orange-yellow from head to thorax.

Crescent Threadtail (M).Name: Crescent Threadtail (M)
Crescent Threadtail (M).Description: This species may be confused with the Collared Threadtail, but can be identified by its black anal appendages.

Crescent Threadtail (F).Name: Crescent Threadtail (F)
Crescent Threadtail (F).Description: Females have narrower blue markings on the thorax.

Emperor.Name: Emperor
Emperor.Description: This large species has a dark abdomen and a blue-green thorax. Emperor females lay their eggs in plant tissue. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dingy Duskhawker.Name: Dingy Duskhawker
Dingy Duskhawker.Description: This species can be found in rainforests, and can be recognised by its distinct, dark T-shaped mark on the upper surface of the frons. Females are paler.

Pond Cruiser.Name: Pond Cruiser
Pond Cruiser.Description: This large species has yellow markings on its dark thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Common Flangetail.Name: Common Flangetail
Common Flangetail.Description: The Common Flangetail is common in open habitats. It has green-yellow bands on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Trumpet Tail (M).Name: Trumpet Tail (M)
Trumpet Tail (M).Description: The Trumpet Tail has a trumpet-shaped abdomen. Males are blue with dark markings.

Trumpet Tail (F).Name: Trumpet Tail (F)
Trumpet Tail (F).Description: Females are greenish-yellow with similar markings as males.

Blue Adjudant.Name: Blue Adjudant
Blue Adjudant.Description: The Blue Adjudant is a small dragonfly. The thorax and part of the abdomen of both the mature male and female are bright blue. In the male, the last four abdominal segments are dark. In the female, the last five abdominal segments are dark.

Scarlet Adjudant (M).Name: Scarlet Adjudant (M)
Scarlet Adjudant (M).Description: The Scarlet Adjudant is a small red dragonfly. Males have a short bright red abdomen. The "knees" on the hind legs are red in colour.

Scarlet Adjudant (F).Name: Scarlet Adjudant (F)
Scarlet Adjudant (F).Description: Females are brown-yellow with yellowish "knees" on the hind legs.

Pond Adjudant (M).Name: Pond Adjudant (M)
Pond Adjudant (M).Description: The Pond Adjudant male is a small powdery blue dragonfly. It can be differentiated from the larger Blue Dasher by how only the last two abdominal segments are dark.

Pond Adjudant (F).Name: Pond Adjudant (F)
Pond Adjudant (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown with black markings.

Grenadier.Name: Grenadier
Grenadier.Description: This species has mottled yellow markings on its thorax and the top half of its abdomen is red. Females are similar to males, but slightly duller.

Blue Dasher (M).Name: Blue Dasher (M)
Blue Dasher (M).Description: This species has a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males have a powdery blue body with a black tip on its abdomen (on the last three abdominal segments).

Blue Dasher (F).Name: Blue Dasher (F)
Blue Dasher (F).Description: Females are brownish-yellow with a dark streak along its abdomen.

Common Amberwing (M).Name: Common Amberwing (M)
Common Amberwing (M).Description: Males have a reddish-gold tint on their wings and have an orange abdomen. Immature males are similar to females in appearance.

Common Amberwing (F).Name: Common Amberwing (F)
Common Amberwing (F).Description: Females are light brown and have yellowish-orange wing spots.

Sultan.Name: Sultan
Sultan.Description: Males of this large species have a distinct red patch on one-third of the wings. Females of this large species are brownish-orange.

Green-eyed Percher.Name: Green-eyed Percher
Green-eyed Percher.Description: This species is uniformly dark blue and has a thin abdomen with a slightly swollen base. The female is similar to the male in appearance.

Common Scarlet (M).Name: Common Scarlet (M)
Common Scarlet (M).Description: Males are red with a dark line along the abdomen, which distinguishes them from the Common Redbolt.

Common Scarlet (F).Name: Common Scarlet (F)
Common Scarlet (F).Description: Females have a light brown body with a similar dark line along its abdomen.

Black-tipped Percher (M).Name: Black-tipped Percher (M)
Black-tipped Percher (M).Description: Males are blue with dark wing tips. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Black-tipped Percher (F).Name: Black-tipped Percher (F)
Black-tipped Percher (F).Description: Females are yellow with a dark band down their abdomen. The wings are clear. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Blue Percher (M).Name: Blue Percher (M)
Blue Percher (M).Description: Males are mostly dark blue, with the last three abdominal segments black. They have distinct white anal appendages. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Blue Percher (F).Name: Blue Percher (F)
Blue Percher (F).Description: Females have yellow-green markings on both the thorax and abdomen, as well as distinct white anal appendages. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Water Monarch.Name: Water Monarch
Water Monarch.Description: This species is brownish and has an irregular dark band on its hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Scarlet Grenadier.Name: Scarlet Grenadier
Scarlet Grenadier.Description: The Scarlet Grenadier has a yellow-striped thorax and bright red abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Coastal Glider (M).Name: Coastal Glider (M)
Coastal Glider (M).Description: Males are red with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'. Immature males and females are similar in appearance.

Coastal Glider (F).Name: Coastal Glider (F)
Coastal Glider (F).Description: Females are orange-yellow with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark line is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'.

Common Parasol (M).Name: Common Parasol (M)
Common Parasol (M).Description: Males have a dark red colouration on their wings and clear wing tips. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Common Parasol (F).Name: Common Parasol (F)
Common Parasol (F).Description: Females are light brown with dark markings along the sides of its abdomen. Its wings are clear. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Spine-tufted Skimmer (M).Name: Spine-tufted Skimmer (M)
Spine-tufted Skimmer (M).Description: This species can be easily confused with the Scarlet Skimmer, but can be distinguished by its brown thorax and dark grey eyes.

Common Blue Skimmer (M).Name: Common Blue Skimmer (M)
Common Blue Skimmer (M).Description: While adult males have a generally blue body with a darkened tip, immature males are usually yellow-brown and resemble the females.

Slender Blue Skimmer (M).Name: Slender Blue Skimmer (M)
Slender Blue Skimmer (M).Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have a slender blue abdomen and also posess light blue eyes. Immature males and females are light brown.

Variegated Green Skimmer.Name: Variegated Green Skimmer
Variegated Green Skimmer.Description: This common species can be found in many habitats, and has distinct yellowish-green markings on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Scarlet Skimmer (M).Name: Scarlet Skimmer (M)
Scarlet Skimmer (M).Description: Males have a bright red thorax and abdomen and a red patch near the base of their wings.

Scarlet Skimmer (F).Name: Scarlet Skimmer (F)
Scarlet Skimmer (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown with clear wings.

Wandering Glider.Name: Wandering Glider
Wandering Glider.Description: This common species can often be seen flying in open areas and is one of the most widespread species in the world. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Common Chaser (M).Name: Common Chaser (M)
Common Chaser (M).Description: Males have a striking blue thorax and yellow and black abdomen.

Common Chaser (F).Name: Common Chaser (F)
Common Chaser (F).Description: Females have black and yellow stripes on their thorax. The abdomen is black with dull orange markings. Notably, it has conspicuous flaps near the tip of the abdomen.

Banded Skimmer (M).Name: Banded Skimmer (M)
Banded Skimmer (M).Description: Males are black with a white patch on the first few segments of their abdomens.

Banded Skimmer (F).Name: Banded Skimmer (F)
Banded Skimmer (F).Description: Females have a yellow abdomen with black markings.

Mangrove Dwarf (M).Name: Mangrove Dwarf (M)
Mangrove Dwarf (M).Description: This species looks similar to the Blue Dasher but it is smaller and does not have the amber tint at the base of its wings. Found only in mangrove areas.

Mangrove Dwarf (F).Name: Mangrove Dwarf (F)
Mangrove Dwarf (F).Description: Females have yellow markings along the thorax and the abdomen. Found only in mangrove areas.

Common Redbolt (M).Name: Common Redbolt (M)
Common Redbolt (M).Description: Males are bright red throughout, including the eyes.

Common Redbolt (F).Name: Common Redbolt (F)
Common Redbolt (F).Description: Females are brown, with a bright yellow streak that extends from the thorax to the top of the abdomen.

Bronze Flutterer.Name: Bronze Flutterer
Bronze Flutterer.Description: The Bronze Flutterer has striking opaque iridescent wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Yellow-barred Flutterer.Name: Yellow-barred Flutterer
Yellow-barred Flutterer.Description: One of the easiest species to identify with a distinct dark and yellow pattern on the base of their hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Sapphire Flutterer.Name: Sapphire Flutterer
Sapphire Flutterer.Description: The Sapphire Flutterer can be easily identified by the blue patches on its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

White-barred Duskhawk (M).Name: White-barred Duskhawk (M)
White-barred Duskhawk (M).Description: Males have a distinct light brown and white patch on their hindwings. Immature males lack this wing pattern and are generally pale brown, similar to the female.

White-barred Duskhawk (F).Name: White-barred Duskhawk (F)
White-barred Duskhawk (F).Description: Females are generally pale brown with clear wings.

Saddlebag Glider.Name: Saddlebag Glider
Saddlebag Glider.Description: The veins on the base of this species' hindwings are red. Two black spots are present at tip of abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Crimson Dropwing (M).Name: Crimson Dropwing (M)
Crimson Dropwing (M).Description: Males have a luminous pink abdomen, red wing veins and an amber tint at the wing base.

Crimson Dropwing (F).Name: Crimson Dropwing (F)
Crimson Dropwing (F).Description: Females are light brown with yellow veins on the base of their hindwings, and black markings along the sides of the abdomen.

Indigo Dropwing (M).Name: Indigo Dropwing (M)
Indigo Dropwing (M).Description: This common species can be found near streams and rivers. Males are dark blue, abdomen half blackish with yellow spots.

Indigo Dropwing (F).Name: Indigo Dropwing (F)
Indigo Dropwing (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown with dark markings on the thorax and abdomen.

Dancing Dropwing.Name: Dancing Dropwing
Dancing Dropwing.Description: This species has distinct yellow markings on its thorax and abdomen, and a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Scarlet Basker (M).Name: Scarlet Basker (M)
Scarlet Basker (M).Description: Males have two diamond-shaped spots at the end of the abdomen.

Scarlet Basker (F).Name: Scarlet Basker (F)
Scarlet Basker (F).Description: Females are yellowish-brown in colour with an amber patch at the base of the hindwing.

Slender Duskdarter.Name: Slender Duskdarter
Slender Duskdarter.Description: Males have green eyes, and a slender abdomen. Females have a slightly thicker abdomen. The species is most active at dusk and dawn.

Blue-throated bee-eater.Name: Blue-throated bee-eater
Blue-throated bee-eater.Description: While similar to the blue-tailed bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its brown head and bright blue throat.

Blue-tailed bee-eater.Name: Blue-tailed bee-eater
Blue-tailed bee-eater.Description: While similar to the blue-throated bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its olive head and yellow-brown throat.

Yellow-vented bulbul.Name: Yellow-vented bulbul
Yellow-vented bulbul.Description: A common bird with brown upperparts, pale underparts, a black lore and a bright yellow vent.

Oriental magpie-robin.Name: Oriental magpie-robin
Oriental magpie-robin.Description: This songbird has black and white plumage with a long tail that is often held high.  Females are grey on upperparts and breast.

Asian paradise flycatcher.Name: Asian paradise flycatcher
Asian paradise flycatcher.Description: Breeding males have an exceptionally long tail and come in either rufous or white colour morphs. Females and non-breeding males have much shorter tail and either white or chestnut upperparts with varying amount of grey or black on head, throat and upper breast.

Common tailorbird.Name: Common tailorbird
Common tailorbird.Description: Similar to the Dark-necked Tailorbird, but has a less extensive red cap and white vent. Males have a longer tail than females.

House crow.Name: House crow
House crow.Description: This urban bird can be differentiated from the Large-billed Crow by its grey collar.

Large-billed crow.Name: Large-billed crow
Large-billed crow.Description: Similar to the House Crow except that it is entirely black and has a distinctly larger bill.

Asian koel.Name: Asian koel
Asian koel.Description: This large bird has a distinct loud call from which it derives its common name. They can be distinguished from crows with their long tails and red eyes.

Scarlet-backed flowerpecker.Name: Scarlet-backed flowerpecker
Scarlet-backed flowerpecker.Description: This common garden bird has a red crown and back, black upperparts and white underparts. Females are generally grey with a red rump.

Oriental pied hornbill.Name: Oriental pied hornbill
Oriental pied hornbill.Description: This large striking bird was once rare in Singapore, but populations have since recovered due to a successful re-introduction programme.

Common iora.Name: Common iora
Common iora.Description: Males have black upperparts and yellow underparts, while females have olive-green upperparts and yellow underparts. Two white wing bars distinctive in both sexes

White-throated kingfisher.Name: White-throated kingfisher
White-throated kingfisher.Description: A common species in Singapore, this bird can be recognised by the white-breast  and throat on its otherwise brown underparts.

Collared kingfisher.Name: Collared kingfisher
Collared kingfisher.Description: This common species has a turquoise cap, wings back and tail, and a white collar and underparts.

Scaly-breasted munia.Name: Scaly-breasted munia
Scaly-breasted munia.Description: This bird gets its common name from the scaling on its breast. Has a dark brown head and upperparts.

Eurasian tree sparrow.Name: Eurasian tree sparrow
Eurasian tree sparrow.Description: This common species has a brown cap and prominent black patches on its cheeks and chin.

Black-naped oriole.Name: Black-naped oriole
Black-naped oriole.Description: This common garden bird is unmistakable with its bright yellow plumage, black nape and wings, and pink bill.

Red junglefowl.Name: Red junglefowl
Red junglefowl.Description: This nationally-threatened species is thought to be the ancestral species of the domestic chicken. It is commonly encountered on P. Ubin.

Rock pigeon.Name: Rock pigeon
Rock pigeon.Description: This urban bird typically appears grey, but can include brown, black and white morphs.

Spotted dove.Name: Spotted dove
Spotted dove.Description: This dove may be confused with the Zebra Dove but has a spotted neck and is larger.

Zebra dove.Name: Zebra dove
Zebra dove.Description: This dove may be confused with the Spotted Dove but has a striped neck and has a slimmer build.

Pink-necked green pigeon.Name: Pink-necked green pigeon
Pink-necked green pigeon.Description: Similar colouration to the Little Green Pigeon but males have a pink neck and green wings, and are much larger. Females are mostly green.

White-breasted waterhen.Name: White-breasted waterhen
White-breasted waterhen.Description: This common waterbird has a white face and breast, and blackish upperparts and brown vent.

Tiger shrike.Name: Tiger shrike
Tiger shrike.Description: Adults have a grey head, black face mask, barred chestnut upperparts and white underparts. The more commonly encountered immatures are chestnut above and white below with heavy barring on both upperparts and underparts.

Brown shrike.Name: Brown shrike
Brown shrike.Description: Not similar to the Tiger Shrike. Adults have brown cap, white eye-brow above black face mask, unbarred brown upperparts and whitish underparts with a brownish wash.

Asian glossy starling.Name: Asian glossy starling
Asian glossy starling.Description: This bird is glossy dark green with red eyes is often seen in flocks. Juveniles are grey above and white below and covered in bold streaks.

Common myna.Name: Common myna
Common myna.Description: Despite its name, it is less common than the White-vented myna. Distinguishable by its brown body and yellow eye-patch.

Javan myna.Name: Javan myna
Javan myna.Description: The most common bird in Singapore, this species can be found in most urban areas.It has a black plumage, white vent and yellow beak.

Daurian starling.Name: Daurian starling
Daurian starling.Description: This bird is a creamy white with metallic green wings with a white wingbar.

Brown-throated sunbird.Name: Brown-throated sunbird
Brown-throated sunbird.Description: Males of this species have a beautiful metallic blue crown and back, brown throat and yellow underparts. Females are duller with olive upperparts and yellow underparts. Both sexes have red eyes, female also has distinct split yellow eye-ring.

Olive-backed sunbird.Name: Olive-backed sunbird
Olive-backed sunbird.Description: A commonly seen bird that has olive green upperparts and yellow underparts, with male birds possessing a metallic blue bib.

Oriental white-eye.Name: Oriental white-eye
Oriental white-eye.Description: A common garden bird with greenish-yellow head and upperparts, grey underparts, yellow vent and a prominent white eye-ring.

Sunda pygmy woodpecker.Name: Sunda pygmy woodpecker
Sunda pygmy woodpecker.Description: This is the smallest woodpecker species in Singapore and is well camouflaged on trees with its brown and white mottled plumage.

Common goldenback.Name: Common goldenback
Common goldenback.Description: So called for its golden-yellow plumage. Males have a red cap, while females have a black cap.

Yellow Bittern.Name: Yellow Bittern
Yellow Bittern.Description: A shy bird that is often found in pondside vegetation, the Yellow Bittern can be identified by the contrast between its yellowish brown wing coverts and black flight feathers in flight.

Cinnamon Bittern.Name: Cinnamon Bittern
Cinnamon Bittern.Description: This species has cinnamon upperparts with streaked underparts, and appears uniformly reddish-brown in flight.

Von Schrenck's Bittern.Name: Von Schrenck's Bittern
Von Schrenck's Bittern.Description: The male of this species has chestnut upperparts and pale underparts, while the females have numerous white spots on brown upperparts and are boldly streaked on their underparts.

Black Bittern.Name: Black Bittern
Black Bittern.Description: The black bittern is so called for its dark upperparts and underparts which are streaked with white.

Little Egret.Name: Little Egret
Little Egret.Description: This all-white egret can be differentiated from the other by its black bill and black legs with yellow feet.

Intermediate Egret.Name: Intermediate Egret
Intermediate Egret.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill with black tip and black legs and feet. Its S-shaped neck is roughly equal to its body length.

Great Egret.Name: Great Egret
Great Egret.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill and black legs, and can be differentiated from the others by the kink in its long S-shaped neck.

Eastern Cattle Egret.Name: Eastern Cattle Egret
Eastern Cattle Egret.Description: Eastern cattle egrets are white with a rufous head and breast. In non-breeding plumage, it is completely white and can be differentiated by its shorter neck.

Chinese Egret.Name: Chinese Egret
Chinese Egret.Description: This all-white egret can be differentiated from the others by its crest (in breeding plumage), greenish facial skin, legs and feet with two-tone bill (black upper half and yellow bottom half). Very similar to the white morph Pacific Reef Heron but the latter has distinctively shorter legs and upper mandible of bill is generally paler.

Pacific Reef Heron.Name: Pacific Reef Heron
Pacific Reef Heron.Description: This species has both a dark morph, which is unmistakably slate-grey, and a light morph, which is white. Light morph has greenish legs and feet, yellowish bill and appears shorter-legged than other white egrets.

Grey Heron.Name: Grey Heron
Grey Heron.Description: This tall bird has a light grey plumage with a black stripe above its eyes and black stripes on its neck.

Purple Heron.Name: Purple Heron
Purple Heron.Description: This heron can be easily identified by its rusty red neck and purplish grey plumage.

Great-billed Heron.Name: Great-billed Heron
Great-billed Heron.Description: This heron get its name from its large bill and is the tallest bird in Singapore at 115 cm. It has dark grey pluamge with pale streaks on its wings and neck.

Malayan Night Heron.Name: Malayan Night Heron
Malayan Night Heron.Description: This heron has a black crown and reddish-brown plumage with streaked underparts. Juveniles have mottled brown upperparts with numerous white spots and black barring on their underparts.

Striated Heron.Name: Striated Heron
Striated Heron.Description: A small heron with dark crown, grey mantle and underparts and yellowish legs. It can be confused with the Black-crowned Night Heron.

Black-crowned Night Heron.Name: Black-crowned Night Heron
Black-crowned Night Heron.Description: This distinctive heron has a black crown and back, red eyes and white underparts.

Javan Pond Heron.Name: Javan Pond Heron
Javan Pond Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a pale rufous head, brown breast, black back, and white belly. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Indian Pond Heron.Name: Indian Pond Heron
