Indian Pond Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a buffy head, neck and breast, maroon mantle and scapulars and white belly. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Chinese Pond Heron.Name: Chinese Pond Heron
Chinese Pond Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a brown head and breast, black back and white belly and wings. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Burgundy Anemone.Name: Burgundy Anemone
Burgundy Anemone.Description: Burgundy or dark red in color. Short tentacles that taper off at its ends. Some may have five yellow spots around its mouth.

Snaky Anemone.Name: Snaky Anemone
Snaky Anemone.Description: Has purplish-grey, green or brown colored tentacles that are tightly curled together. Looks like udon noodles.

Striped Sand Anemone.Name: Striped Sand Anemone
Striped Sand Anemone.Description: Has parallel dark bars down and white stripes across its semi-transparent tentacles. Easily confused with the Striped Bead Anemone, but has shorter tentacles and a light-colored body column.

Striped Bead Anemone.Name: Striped Bead Anemone
Striped Bead Anemone.Description: Has parallel dark lines down its semi-transparent tentacles and white bars across. Easily confused with the Striped Sand Anemone, but has longer tentacles and a tan or green body column.

Whelk-hitching Anemone.Name: Whelk-hitching Anemone
Whelk-hitching Anemone.Description: Small body. Brown with white stripes. Attached to the shells of whelks.

Swimming Anemone.Name: Swimming Anemone
Swimming Anemone.Description: Many tentacles - something striped in red/white, or sometimes plain yellow or brown. Can swim - for about 15 seconds each time, though they do not really swim much at low tide.

Common Peachia Anemone.Name: Common Peachia Anemone
Common Peachia Anemone.Description: Small anemone with 16 fat tentacles having white, pink, beige or brown chevron patterns near its mouth. Cream-colored body column.

Giant Carpet Anemone.Name: Giant Carpet Anemone
Giant Carpet Anemone.Description: Densely covered with short tentacles, resembling a carpet. Usually brown or purple in color, with tips of the tentacles in a lighter shade. Bright pink bumps sometimes seen on the underside.

Haddon's Carpet Anemone.Name: Haddon's Carpet Anemone
Haddon's Carpet Anemone.Description: Has long-short tentacles with bulbous tips at the circumference of its outer disk. Generally green, blue, grey or purple in color.

Mini Carpet Anemone.Name: Mini Carpet Anemone
Mini Carpet Anemone.Description: Small carpet anemone about the size of one's palm. Has short tentacles that can be green, brown or grey.

Lined Bead Anemone.Name: Lined Bead Anemone
Lined Bead Anemone.Description: This tiny, grey anemone is seldom seen with its tentacles, making it look like a bead with fine white/orange/red stripes. The Lined Bead Anemone is commonly found all over the world, as it is easily dispersed by ships.

Very Long-armed Brittle Star.Name: Very Long-armed Brittle Star
Very Long-armed Brittle Star.Description: Long arms - sometimes stretching up to 30 cm long. Small central disk that is about 1-2 cm in diameter. Flat arms have spines laterally extended. Arms may have a faint banded pattern.

Tiny Colorful Brittle Star.Name: Tiny Colorful Brittle Star
Tiny Colorful Brittle Star.Description: Comes in a variety of colors and patterns, usually mimicking that of the animal it is on. Arms have small spines along its length. Central disk is colorfully patterned.

Copperband Butterflyfish.Name: Copperband Butterflyfish
Copperband Butterflyfish.Description: Distinct body pattern of orange/ yellow stripes with black and white edges. Has a flat body and a long snout. Characterised by a black eye spot on its dorsal fin.

Kite Butterflyfish.Name: Kite Butterflyfish
Kite Butterflyfish.Description: Kite-shaped. Distinct body pattern of 4 brown stripes (juvenile ones have 5) and a black eye spot on its dorsal fin. Has a flat body and a short snout.

Batavia Batfish.Name: Batavia Batfish
Batavia Batfish.Description: Characterised by its flat body and small mouth. Is usually silver with a dark bar vertically down its eye. A lighter-colored bar is seen behind the dark bar.

Bengal Sergeant.Name: Bengal Sergeant
Bengal Sergeant.Description: Rounded tail fins. White or yellow body with 6-7 black or grey vertical bars across its body. The bars end right before the tail of the fish.

Clear Sundial Snail.Name: Clear Sundial Snail
Clear Sundial Snail.Description: Grey and yellowish brown with alternating bands of dark brown and white. Flat circular shell with whorls. Bottom view resembles a spiral staircase.

Button Snail.Name: Button Snail
Button Snail.Description: Identified by circular glossy shells. Can be found in a variety of colors and patterns.

Cerianthid Phoronid Worm.Name: Cerianthid Phoronid Worm
Cerianthid Phoronid Worm.Description: Grey or pinkish-black in color. Possesses a pair of feathery spiraling tentacles. Extremely shy and retreat once they sense danger.

Fluted Giant Clam.Name: Fluted Giant Clam
Fluted Giant Clam.Description: 5-6 rows of open flutes on its valves. Shell opening faces upwards. Hinged side is firmly attached to the rock surface.

Pacific Yellow Cockle.Name: Pacific Yellow Cockle
Pacific Yellow Cockle.Description: Characterised by thick and spherical shells with vertical ribs. Yellowish shell often seen with dark stains on it.

Common File Clam.Name: Common File Clam
Common File Clam.Description: Fan-shaped thick shell. Usually white and yellow. Rough with coarse scaly ribs and long sticky tentacles.

Big Brown Mactra Clam.Name: Big Brown Mactra Clam
Big Brown Mactra Clam.Description: Smooth and triangular. Usually unmarked and is buried just beneath the surface of the ground with an extended siphon sticking out.

Lettered Venus Clam.Name: Lettered Venus Clam
Lettered Venus Clam.Description: Shaped like a trapezium. Smooth and thin clam is white with small black dots.

Black-lipped Conch.Name: Black-lipped Conch
Black-lipped Conch.Description: Narrow shell with wavy flared lips. Black edges around its shell opening. Green body with white or beige spots.

Gong-gong.Name: Gong-gong
Gong-gong.Description: White pearly shell with a flared lip. Body is olive green. Has a brown-orange tentacle connected to a large eye. Interestingly, the snail hops instead of creeping along surfaces.

Spiral Melongena.Name: Spiral Melongena
Spiral Melongena.Description: Large shell with a black body. Shell is covered by a fine layer of hairs. Hairs only fall off after the snail dies, revealing an orange shell underneath.
Spiral Melongena.Habitat: Mudflat, Sandy beach, Rocky shore, Seagrass, Mangrove

Margined Conch.Name: Margined Conch
Margined Conch.Description: Thick shell with wavy flared lips. Shell is usually white with brown streaks.

Zebra Coral.Name: Zebra Coral
Zebra Coral.Description: A type of encrusting hard coral that thrives even in the murkiest waters. Aptly named the Zebra Coral due to its white ring on a black background.

Red-eyed Reef Crab.Name: Red-eyed Reef Crab
Red-eyed Reef Crab.Description: Oval body that is reddish to purplish brown. Bright red eyes. Moves fast.

Velcro Crab.Name: Velcro Crab
Velcro Crab.Description: Body in the shape of a tear-drop. Often disguised under bits and pieces of sponges, seagrass, coral rubble and shell.

Spotted Moon Crab.Name: Spotted Moon Crab
Spotted Moon Crab.Description: Circular, pale white/yellow body with little dark spots. Long spikes on its sides. Its paddle-shaped walking legs allow the crab to quickly burrow into the sand.

Stone/Thunder Crab.Name: Stone/Thunder Crab
Stone/Thunder Crab.Description: Large pincers with brown-black tips. Bright green eyes, encircled with red. Upperside of its body is dull grey, but the underside is orange.

Maroon Stone Crab.Name: Maroon Stone Crab
Maroon Stone Crab.Description: Reddish-brown to maroon in color. Black tips on its pincers. Eyes are completely red, unlike the Stone crab which has green eyes.

Horn-eyed Ghost Crab.Name: Horn-eyed Ghost Crab
Horn-eyed Ghost Crab.Description: Aptly named the Ghost Crab given its elusive nature. Can run up to 2m/s. Box-shaped body with markings shaped like a ‘H’. Adults have darker colored 'horns' on top of each eyestalk.

Orange Fiddler Crab.Name: Orange Fiddler Crab
Orange Fiddler Crab.Description: Males identified by an enlarged pincer, with the lower pincer orange or yellow but the upper pincer white. Females do not have an enlarged pincer. Body color varies from green to grey.

Spotted-belly Forceps Crab.Name: Spotted-belly Forceps Crab
Spotted-belly Forceps Crab.Description: Enlarged pincer that has grinding teeth (‘molar’) like humans. Smooth red/purple brown body on the upperside, pale orange with dark spots on the underside.
Spotted-belly Forceps Crab.Habitat: Rocky shore, Coral reef, Coral rubble, Sea wall

Painted Porcelain Crab.Name: Painted Porcelain Crab
Painted Porcelain Crab.Description: Not a true crab! Small and white with purplish polka dots on the pincers and upper body. Often found in pairs.

Purple-legged Swimming Crab.Name: Purple-legged Swimming Crab
Purple-legged Swimming Crab.Description: Last pair of legs on this crab is padde-shaped, allowing it to swim expertly. Comes in various colors, with walking legs in purple and claws in orange with black tips.

Flower Crab.Name: Flower Crab
Flower Crab.Description: Males have attractive bright colors and white spots on their body. Females are dull green/brown and have a bigger abdomen on the underside to carry eggs.

Blue Swimming Crab.Name: Blue Swimming Crab
Blue Swimming Crab.Description: Padde-shaped legs on the last pair of legs allows this crab to swim expertly. Distinct rectangular, blue body. 6 rounded lobes between its widely-spaced eyes.

Blue-spined Swimming Crab.Name: Blue-spined Swimming Crab
Blue-spined Swimming Crab.Description: Bright blue-black tips on its pincers and 5 spines next to its eyes. 6 rounded lobes between its widely-spaced eyes.

Red Swimming Crab.Name: Red Swimming Crab
Red Swimming Crab.Description: Bright orange/red in color, but sometimes brown. Has 5 spines with black tips on the side of its body. Last pair of paddle-shaped walking legs can be blue in color.

Mangrove Tree-dwelling Crab.Name: Mangrove Tree-dwelling Crab
Mangrove Tree-dwelling Crab.Description: Half-circular body. Green eyes spaced widely far apart on the non-circular side of its body. Yellow body with dark brown patches.

Smooth Spooner Crab.Name: Smooth Spooner Crab
Smooth Spooner Crab.Description: Pincers are smooth with spoon-shaped tips. Left pincer is slightly larger than the right. Usually come in a wide variety of colors - brown, beige, and grey.

Leaf Porter Crab.Name: Leaf Porter Crab
Leaf Porter Crab.Description: Commonly found using leaves, clam shells or wood for camouflage. Has long, thin legs and small pincers which are tucked close to its body.

Soldier Crab.Name: Soldier Crab
Soldier Crab.Description: Move around in groups at low tide. Has long eyestalks with slender and long pincers which fold downward.

Common Hairy Crab.Name: Common Hairy Crab
Common Hairy Crab.Description: Crab is covered with long, soft 'hair' which helps the crab to camouflage as drifting flotsam. Has distinct red eyes. Fun fact: The Common Hairy Crab is also known as the Teddy Bear Crab!

Zoned Cerith.Name: Zoned Cerith
Zoned Cerith.Description: Conical-shaped shell with a brown band spiraling down its white or beige-colored shell.
Zoned Cerith.Habitat: Sandy beach, Coral rubble, Coral reef

Obelisk Creeper Snail.Name: Obelisk Creeper Snail
Obelisk Creeper Snail.Description: Conical-shaped shell. Can take on two types of spiral patterns - fine spirals with small dots or wide spirals with regular bumps. Has a sharp pointed tip.

Javan Turrid Snail.Name: Javan Turrid Snail
Javan Turrid Snail.Description: Identified by the spirals on its shell with regular pointed bumps. Shell is pale brown or beige. Body is pale with brown spots.

Glittering Cuttlefish.Name: Glittering Cuttlefish
Glittering Cuttlefish.Description: Smooth and oval. Has glittering spots on each side of its body.

Red Egg Crab.Name: Red Egg Crab
Red Egg Crab.Description: Red in color with an egg-shaped body. Has obvious white dots on its body. It is poisonous! Do not eat or touch them.

Mosaic Reef Crab.Name: Mosaic Reef Crab
Mosaic Reef Crab.Description: Orange/red body with striking white mosaic-like patterns. Do not touch or eat, it is poisonous!

Fire Anemone.Name: Fire Anemone
Fire Anemone.Description: This anemone has thick and fleshy tentacles and its central oral disk has white stripes with small, dark spots. The colour of this animal can vary from green, yellow, purple, blue and brown. This anemone can give a powerful and painful sting as its name suggests, beware not touch them!

Three-spined Toadfish.Name: Three-spined Toadfish
Three-spined Toadfish.Description: Do not touch! There are sharp spines on the side of its head which can be painful. Best identified by its large eyes, wide mouth and big, flat head. Has greyish-brown bars on its sides.
Three-spined Toadfish.Habitat: Rocky shore, Coral rubble, Sandy beach

Longspined Waspfish.Name: Longspined Waspfish
Longspined Waspfish.Description: A pair of spines can be spotted next to its mouth. Dorsal fin starts from above the eyes of the animal. Do not touch with bare hands! This fish has prickly dorsal spines that can be painful!

Hollow-cheeked Stonefish.Name: Hollow-cheeked Stonefish
Hollow-cheeked Stonefish.Description: Do not touch! This fish can be fatal to humans! Resembles a stone, and is very well camouflaged. Can be identified by its downturned mouth that resembles a frown.
Hollow-cheeked Stonefish.Habitat: Sea wall, Coral reef, Coral rubble

Black Eeltail Catfish.Name: Black Eeltail Catfish
Black Eeltail Catfish.Description: Do not touch! It has venomous spines on its dorsal and pectoral fins. Best identified by four pairs of 'whiskers' around its mouth and flat eel-like tail.

Cone Snail.Name: Cone Snail
Cone Snail.Description: This snail is identified by its conical shell that looks similar to an ice cream cone. The shell opens in a narrow slit and the operculum (opening) is a long and horn-like. The snail is about 5-10 cmand slow-moving but uses its radula that shoots out like a harpoon to inject a potent toxin to hunt for prey. Although this animal may look harmless like other types of snails, but it is one of the most dangerous animals on our shores and the effects of their sting can be fatal. Do not handle any snails with a similar conical shell and make sure to be in proper footwear and attire.

Reef Bristleworm.Name: Reef Bristleworm
Reef Bristleworm.Description: Green, brown or pink body lined with long bristles. Often found hiding under stones. Do not touch! Bristles are filled with toxins and can cause burning pain when touched.

Golden Fireworm.Name: Golden Fireworm
Golden Fireworm.Description: Extremely beautiful with colorful hairy bistles. Do not touch! Sharp bristles are filled with toxins and can easily penetrate bare skin.

Estuarine Moray Eel.Name: Estuarine Moray Eel
Estuarine Moray Eel.Description: Long body and flattened at the tail. Resembles a snake in both appearance and movement. Usually blue-grey, brown, or reddish-brown with yellow-white spots all over its body.

Carpet Eel-blenny.Name: Carpet Eel-blenny
Carpet Eel-blenny.Description: Contrary to its name and appearance, it is neither an eel nor a snake. Identified as a fish by its fins and scales, but also has a flat eel-like tail. Has a large mouth with thick lips. Green in color.

Delicate Feathery Green Seaweed.Name: Delicate Feathery Green Seaweed
Delicate Feathery Green Seaweed.Description: Each feathery structure is 5 – 7 cm long with long fine branches with pointed tips on a cylindrical central stem. This seawwed is found in clumps and can cover an area of 40 - 50 cm.

Taxifolia Feathery Green Seaweed.Name: Taxifolia Feathery Green Seaweed
Taxifolia Feathery Green Seaweed.Description: Each feather structure is around 3 – 15 cm long and has flat branches with pointed tips on a flat central stem. This seaweed can also be found in clumps, covering an area of 40 - 50 cm but does not blanket the shore.

Red Feather Star.Name: Red Feather Star
Red Feather Star.Description: Has about 30 distinct bright red, feathery arms, as well as some yellowish parts.

Tropical Silverside.Name: Tropical Silverside
Tropical Silverside.Description: Color can range from silvery grey to blue. Streamlined-shaped with large eyes. Often has a long silver line along the length of its side.

Diamond Tuskfish.Name: Diamond Tuskfish
Diamond Tuskfish.Description: Characterised by its pointed snout and sharp teeth. Is usually silver or green in color and can be found with red, blue and yellow markings that form 4-5 bars across its body.

Gold-spotted Mudskipper.Name: Gold-spotted Mudskipper
Gold-spotted Mudskipper.Description: Obvious orange spots on its cheeks and the sides of its body. Males have an orange and black dorsal fin with elongated spikes.
Gold-spotted Mudskipper.Habitat: Mangrove, Rocky shore, Seagrass, Coral rubble

Brown Shore Goby.Name: Brown Shore Goby
Brown Shore Goby.Description: Chubby-faced with small eyes. Has a body covered with irregular pale spots.

Head Stripe Lagoon Goby.Name: Head Stripe Lagoon Goby
Head Stripe Lagoon Goby.Description: Colorful goby with dark spots and stripes on its head. Luminous blue stripes on the side of its body.

Ornate Lagoon Goby.Name: Ornate Lagoon Goby
Ornate Lagoon Goby.Description: Fat round snout with thick lips. Has dashed lines on its sides, red and blue speckles on its body. Can be differentiated from the Black-spotted lagoon goby which has black spots instead.

Peacock Sole.Name: Peacock Sole
Peacock Sole.Description: Challenging to spot this fish due to its high ability to camouflage. Fish has a flat and 2D-shape body with white circles all over its body.

Commerson's Sole.Name: Commerson's Sole
Commerson's Sole.Description: Usually plain brown or beige with no markings, and can camouflage easily in sandy areas. Flat and elongated and tapers off at the tail.

Seagrass Filefish.Name: Seagrass Filefish
Seagrass Filefish.Description: Identified by irregular curved yellow or white line from the front of its body to the middle of its upper body. The line forms a 'smile' on the side of its body.

Black-spot Tuskfish.Name: Black-spot Tuskfish
Black-spot Tuskfish.Description: Characterised by the black spot in the middle of its dosal fin.

Orange-striped Hermit Crab.Name: Orange-striped Hermit Crab
Orange-striped Hermit Crab.Description: Orange stripes on its brown walking legs. Black body with white spots. Can be found in any type of shell (as long as they fit).

Blue-striped Hermit Crab.Name: Blue-striped Hermit Crab
Blue-striped Hermit Crab.Description: Blue stripes on its brown walking legs. Can be found in any type of shell (as long as they fit).

Banded Hermit Crab.Name: Banded Hermit Crab
Banded Hermit Crab.Description: Black bands on its pale yellow walking legs, body and antennae. Right pincer is larger than the left.
Banded Hermit Crab.Habitat: Coral rubble, Living coral, Sea fan

Mangrove Horseshoe Crab.Name: Mangrove Horseshoe Crab
Mangrove Horseshoe Crab.Description: Identified by a short telson (tail) that is circular in cross-section. Smooth, brown shell with short spines on the side of its body.

Coastal Horseshoe Crab.Name: Coastal Horseshoe Crab
Coastal Horseshoe Crab.Description: Identified by a long telson (tail) that is triangular in cross-section. Grey-brown shell with long spines on sides of the body.

Flat False Limpet.Name: Flat False Limpet
Flat False Limpet.Description: Thick and flat shell with 20 or more thick ribs on it. Ribs have the same color as the shell. No hole at the top of its shell.

Star Limpet.Name: Star Limpet
Star Limpet.Description: Thick shell with 5 or 6 raised white ribs creating a star-like pattern.

Tape Seagrass.Name: Tape Seagrass
Tape Seagrass.Description: Identified by its inrolled leaf edges. Long ribbon-like leaves with smooth round tips. Found covering large areas on sand and mud banks.

Fern Seagrass.Name: Fern Seagrass
Fern Seagrass.Description: Leaf made up by up to 20 pairs of tiny leaflets on a single stem, creating its fern-like appearance. Found in small patches.
Fern Seagrass.Status: Critically Endangered (2008 Singapore Red Data Book)

Sickle Seagrass.Name: Sickle Seagrass
Sickle Seagrass.Description: Curved sickle-shaped with smooth and round tips. Has cross hatched veins. Found scattered in patches.
Sickle Seagrass.Status: Critically Endangered (2008 Singapore Red Data Book)

Sea Lettuce.Name: Sea Lettuce
Sea Lettuce.Description: Sea lettuce is a thin and translucent seaweed and it can range from sheets, ribbon- or net-like. They often cover a large area of the shore and floats freely.
Sea Lettuce.Size: Approximately 1 - 2 cm (narrow strips) or more than 20 cm (sheets)

Cake Sand Dollar.Name: Cake Sand Dollar
Cake Sand Dollar.Description: Circular with fine hairs around the edges. Usually found in large quantities. Sometimes have a star-shaped pattern in the centre.

Singapore Scallop.Name: Singapore Scallop
Singapore Scallop.Description: Both long and short tentacles seen when submerged in water. Many tiny eyes.

White-rumped Sea Cucumber.Name: White-rumped Sea Cucumber
White-rumped Sea Cucumber.Description: White/grey rear ends on a smooth brown body. Rear end is actually its anus that is surrounded by 5 yellow 'teeth'. Sometimes completely brown; other times seen with white marks on its surface.

Beige Sea Cucumber.Name: Beige Sea Cucumber
Beige Sea Cucumber.Description: White or beige in color with 5 small brown spots along the length of its upperside. Has distinguishable soft, short projections all along its upperside. Underside is flat with translucent tube feet.

Black Long Sea Cucumber.Name: Black Long Sea Cucumber
Black Long Sea Cucumber.Description: Black and long. Tapered ends on a tube-like body. Has tube feet surrounding the length of its body, without a distinct upper or underside.

Remarkable Sea Cucumber.Name: Remarkable Sea Cucumber
Remarkable Sea Cucumber.Description: Looks like long sausage with one end more tapered than the other. Found in many colors such as yellow, brown, orange, or white - but all have irregular dark spots around its body.

Sandfish Sea Cucumber.Name: Sandfish Sea Cucumber
Sandfish Sea Cucumber.Description: Shaped like a loaf of garlic bread. Beige with black bars, distinct square-ish ends.

See-through Sea Cucumber.Name: See-through Sea Cucumber
See-through Sea Cucumber.Description: Translucent body that is smooth and slippery. Internal muscles and organs can be seen. Species lacks tube feet.

Sea Apple Sea Cucumber.Name: Sea Apple Sea Cucumber
Sea Apple Sea Cucumber.Description: Upperside is red and purple in color. Underside is usually pale to white in color. Sausage-like appearance, but inflates itself into a round ball when stressed.

Pink Warty Sea Cucumber.Name: Pink Warty Sea Cucumber
Pink Warty Sea Cucumber.Description: Pink and yellow in color. Soft and leathery with irregular bumps. Looks similar to the Thorny Sea Cucumber but has less red on its body.

Thorny Sea Cucumber.Name: Thorny Sea Cucumber
Thorny Sea Cucumber.Description: Looks similar to the Pink Warty Sea Cucumer but has soft thorns and rarely has yellow on its body Usually red or orange in color with grey lines along its body.

Orange Sea Cucumber.Name: Orange Sea Cucumber
Orange Sea Cucumber.Description: Mostly orange appearance due to the orange stripes on its dark blue body. Soft and leathery.

Plasticky Sea Cucumber.Name: Plasticky Sea Cucumber
Plasticky Sea Cucumber.Description: Appears plasticky. Pale blue or grey with dark-colored lines along its U-shaped body. Feet has bright orange tips.

Durian Sea Cucumber.Name: Durian Sea Cucumber
Durian Sea Cucumber.Description: Resembles a durian with its thorny appearance. Grey-colored with spine-shaped structures.
Durian Sea Cucumber.Size: Approximately About 20 cm, up to 50 cm

Asparagus Sea Fan.Name: Asparagus Sea Fan
Asparagus Sea Fan.Description: Red/orange/yellow/white stems. Looks like an asparagus when polyps retract.

Gnarled sea fan.Name: Gnarled sea fan
Gnarled sea fan.Description: Red/orange/maroon/pink stems. Looks rough and twisted when polyps retract.

Spiky Sea Pen.Name: Spiky Sea Pen
Spiky Sea Pen.Description: The spiky sea pen has a thick white stem with feather-like structures supported by spines, resembling a quilted pen. It is about 15 – 20 cm long and may have brown spots or an orange foot that is usually buried. The tiny painted porcelain crab is often found hiding in this sea pen.

Plain Sand Star.Name: Plain Sand Star
Plain Sand Star.Description: Sea star with bright orange spines on the edge of its arms. Upperside is brown with a darker brown centre and line down each of its arms. Underside is plain white.

Painted Sand Star.Name: Painted Sand Star
Painted Sand Star.Description: Sea star with white spines along the edge of its arms. On the upperside, it is lined with an orange or dark blue stripe down its arms. Tip of each arm is black.

Eight-armed Luidia Sea Star.Name: Eight-armed Luidia Sea Star
Eight-armed Luidia Sea Star.Description: Has 8 arms that are 12 - 20 cm long with irregular black bars. Usually beige in color, star-shaped black mark in the centre. Underside is white.

Common Sea Star.Name: Common Sea Star
Common Sea Star.Description: Upperside can be in various colors - beige, grey, or brown with variable patterns. Has long arms.

Cake Sea Star.Name: Cake Sea Star
Cake Sea Star.Description: Underside is pale with a chevron pattern of dark bars. Upperside is covered with small pincer-like appendages.

Biscuit Sea Star.Name: Biscuit Sea Star
Biscuit Sea Star.Description: Resembles a baked biscuit with its brown-beige color and smooth, cookie-cutter rounded arm tips. Upperside has blue edges running along the arms towards a dark center.

Spiny Sea Star.Name: Spiny Sea Star
Spiny Sea Star.Description: Upperside has spiny bumps and large plate-like pincers. Underside is pale without any patterns.

Knobbly Sea Star.Name: Knobbly Sea Star
Knobbly Sea Star.Description: Also named 'Chocolate Chip Sea star'. Has dark knobs along the arms and in a circle at the center.

White Salmacis Urchin.Name: White Salmacis Urchin
White Salmacis Urchin.Description: Short sharp white spines with bands in green/purple/brown. Commonly found camouflaging with leaves, seagrass or shells stuck on its spines.

Passion Salmacis Urchin.Name: Passion Salmacis Urchin
Passion Salmacis Urchin.Description: Short sharp purple spines with white tips. Spines around the mouth may be banded in white or maroon color.

Black Sea Urchin.Name: Black Sea Urchin
Black Sea Urchin.Description: Short, black spines about 1 cm in length radiating from its body. Has translucent tube feet that sometimes extends past its spines, helping it to move away from predators.

Long-spined Black Sea Urchin.Name: Long-spined Black Sea Urchin
Long-spined Black Sea Urchin.Description: Skinny, long, black spines can prick through clothing, gloves and even shoes. Upperside has a sac with an orange ring, five white spots, and a v-shaped pattern of tiny bright blue spots.
Long-spined Black Sea Urchin.Habitat: Sandy beach, Rocky shore, Coral rubble
Long-spined Black Sea Urchin.Size: Approximately Spines up to 30 cm long

Estuarine Seahorse.Name: Estuarine Seahorse
Estuarine Seahorse.Description: Refrain from touching as this can damage the protective mucus on the seahorse’s skin. Segmented body armour with no obvious spines, an upright posture and a curled tail.

Peacock-tail Anemone Shrimp.Name: Peacock-tail Anemone Shrimp
Peacock-tail Anemone Shrimp.Description: Translucent orange body with white spots. Characterized by 5 eyespots on its tail that is orange with a black ring around.

Extraordinary Sea Hare.Name: Extraordinary Sea Hare
Extraordinary Sea Hare.Description: Tentacles on its head resemble the ears of a rabbit. Smooth body and dark body flaps with irregular white blotchy bars and dots.

Geographic Sea Hare.Name: Geographic Sea Hare
Geographic Sea Hare.Description: Olive and yellow body with tiny white spots. Has large tentacles that looked similar to rabbit ears. Usually only found during low tides or during night time.

Spotted Sea Hare.Name: Spotted Sea Hare
Spotted Sea Hare.Description: Body is large and smooth. Brown-colored with thin, white bars on the inner edge of its 'wings'.

Hairy Sea Hare.Name: Hairy Sea Hare
Hairy Sea Hare.Description: Brown body with bright blue dots. Can easily camouflage with seaweeds and seagrasses. Species is covered with many finger-like projections, giving it a hairy appearance.

Jolly Green Giant Nudibranch.Name: Jolly Green Giant Nudibranch
Jolly Green Giant Nudibranch.Description: Large horn-like lobe at the front of its gills. Green body outlined in white with yellow bumps all over its body.

Polka-dot Nudibranch.Name: Polka-dot Nudibranch
Polka-dot Nudibranch.Description: White oval body with black circular markings, looking like polka-dots. Black tipped feathery gills on its back.

Pimply Phyllid Nudibranch.Name: Pimply Phyllid Nudibranch
Pimply Phyllid Nudibranch.Description: Black bodies covered with bright blue, pink, grey, red, or green bumps.

Starry-mouthed Nudibranch.Name: Starry-mouthed Nudibranch
Starry-mouthed Nudibranch.Description: Oral tentacles with star-shaped tips. White-colored with a net-like pattern of red or orange lines. Has orange-tipped appendages, which protects its feathery white gills.

Moon-headed Sidegill Slug.Name: Moon-headed Sidegill Slug
Moon-headed Sidegill Slug.Description: Resembles a chocolate chip pancake. Beige with irregular brown spots. Has a large flap of skin known as the veil with sensory 'hairs' to help them detect preys.

Ornate Leaf Slug.Name: Ornate Leaf Slug
Ornate Leaf Slug.Description: Bears some resemblance to seaweeds. Body color can vary from green, yellow to white. Black margin on the edge of a pair of large 'wings' it possesses. Black or white spots on its body.

Dubious Nerite Snail.Name: Dubious Nerite Snail
Dubious Nerite Snail.Description: No two shells of the species look identical. Smooth and glossy shell with a large opening.

Scaly Nerite Snail.Name: Scaly Nerite Snail
Scaly Nerite Snail.Description: Scaly shell with uneven spiralling ribs that makes its surface rough. Unlike other similar nerite snails, the spire (where you can find the tip of the shell) is not sticking out.

Waved Nerite Snail.Name: Waved Nerite Snail
Waved Nerite Snail.Description: Thick shell with irregular dark patches and fine, narrow, and smooth ribs. 3-4 'teeth' at the shell opening and occasionally a large 'tooth' at the outer lip of the opening.

Lined Nerite Snail.Name: Lined Nerite Snail
Lined Nerite Snail.Description: Distinctively identified by the spiraling black ribs on its shell. Has a smooth and white underside. Has a thick operculum that is covered with small pink and black bumps.

Flat Slipper Snail.Name: Flat Slipper Snail
Flat Slipper Snail.Description: Usually spotted in the shells of Hermit crabs. Flat and white shell. Commonly found in pairs.

Conical Slipper Snail.Name: Conical Slipper Snail
Conical Slipper Snail.Description: Usually found on the shell of Hermit crabs. Thin and pointed shell with colors varying from white, pink, to red.

Grey Bonnet Snail.Name: Grey Bonnet Snail
Grey Bonnet Snail.Description: Resembles a bonnet. Smooth helmet-shaped shell with a pointed end. Operculum is shaped like a fan and brightly yellow in color.

Miliaris Cowrie.Name: Miliaris Cowrie
Miliaris Cowrie.Description: Pear-shaped shell that is beige to light-brown in color. White spots on the shell. Base has a white perimeter.

Ovum Cowrie.Name: Ovum Cowrie
Ovum Cowrie.Description: Pear-shaped shell that is pale blue in color with three broad brown bands. Tiny brown speckles on the shell.

Fig Snail.Name: Fig Snail
Fig Snail.Description: Resembles a fig. Shell has a white spiral pattern with irregular dark bands and has a large opening.

Knobbly Periwinkle Snail.Name: Knobbly Periwinkle Snail
Knobbly Periwinkle Snail.Description: Conical-shaped shell with knobs arranged in a spiral pattern. Shell is usually black or bleached white.

Ball Moon Snail.Name: Ball Moon Snail
Ball Moon Snail.Description: Spherical shell that is smooth and plain with pearly pastel shades. Looks similar to the Oval moon snail, but can be distinguished by a brown patch and a small depression on its underside.

Spotted Moon Snail.Name: Spotted Moon Snail
Spotted Moon Snail.Description: Smooth thick shell with a spiral tip. Beige, grey or orange with many irregular dark bands. White body with many dark spots.

Tiger Moon Snail.Name: Tiger Moon Snail
Tiger Moon Snail.Description: Shell pattern resembles a leopard. Pear-shaped. White or beige shell with dark spots in a spiral pattern.

Eggwhite Moon Snail.Name: Eggwhite Moon Snail
Eggwhite Moon Snail.Description: Smooth glossy shell. White, yellow, orange, or brown in color. Underside has a U-shaped depression. Resembles a hard boiled egg.

Oval Moon Snail.Name: Oval Moon Snail
Oval Moon Snail.Description: Resembles a tear-drop. Smooth white shell with a spiral tip. Usually plain, can have patches of yellow, orange, brown, or black at times. Grey bands can be seen on shell.

Lined Moon Snail.Name: Lined Moon Snail
Lined Moon Snail.Description: White or beige shell with fine brown lines. Body is white or beige with short brown tentacles.
Lined Moon Snail.Habitat: Near seagrass, Sandy beach, Muddy bottoms

Common Triton Snail.Name: Common Triton Snail
Common Triton Snail.Description: Beige or brown shell with dark brown spiral patterns of beaded dots and lines.

Spiral Babylonia Snail.Name: Spiral Babylonia Snail
Spiral Babylonia Snail.Description: Distinctive spirals with orange or brown spots on the shell. Shell can vary from brown to white color.

Waved Mitre Snail.Name: Waved Mitre Snail
Waved Mitre Snail.Description: Bullet-shaped shell with fine ridges arranged in a cross-hatched manner. Shell has a layer of skin which can be peeled off.

Creno Whelk.Name: Creno Whelk
Creno Whelk.Description: Conical shell with fine pointed bumps and fine brown lines.

Prickly Whelk.Name: Prickly Whelk
Prickly Whelk.Description: Pointed fine bumps on its conical shell. Usually white with fine brown lines.

Mud Whelk.Name: Mud Whelk
Mud Whelk.Description: Conical shell with bumpy ridges on the spire (where the tip is). Found in shades of brown, white and green, usually with a brown band on the shell.

Common Whelk.Name: Common Whelk
Common Whelk.Description: Conical-shaped shell with neat and regular ridges. Alternating bands of white and brown. Can commonly see tiny sea anemones on its shell.

Olive Whelk.Name: Olive Whelk
Olive Whelk.Description: Brown or olive green shell with smooth spiralling ridges. Has a very long siphon and short tentacles.

Lined Whelk.Name: Lined Whelk
Lined Whelk.Description: Purple line lining the spirals of the shell. Shell is conical-shaped and yellow in color.

Olive Weasel Snail.Name: Olive Weasel Snail
Olive Weasel Snail.Description: Resembles a bullet. Fine brown zig-zag lines on beige-colored shell. Opening of shell is violet in color.

Noble Volute.Name: Noble Volute
Noble Volute.Description: Wide brown zig-zag lines on beige, yellow, or orange shell. Body is black with orange or yellow spots.

Baler Volute.Name: Baler Volute
Baler Volute.Description: Thin and fragile shell that is usually beige or orange with brown bands. Body is brown with white stripes.
Baler Volute.Habitat: Muddy bottoms, Near seagrass, Near mangrove

Turtle Dove Snail.Name: Turtle Dove Snail
Turtle Dove Snail.Description: Pale white/ beige shell with a dark net-like pattern. Occasionally, a second shell can be spotted at its shell opening.

Dotted Dove Snail.Name: Dotted Dove Snail
Dotted Dove Snail.Description: Thick shell with black and yellow patterns.

False Scorpionfish.Name: False Scorpionfish
False Scorpionfish.Description: Large backward pointing spines above its mouth that can hurt. Hard to spot the fish as it is good at camouflaging and staying motionless.

Chocolate Sponge.Name: Chocolate Sponge
Chocolate Sponge.Description: Chocolate brown with a smooth, velvety texture. Tiny brittle stars can be found in the small holes of the sponge.
Chocolate Sponge.Habitat: Muddy bottoms of lagoons, Near reefs

Blue Spatula Sponge.Name: Blue Spatula Sponge
Blue Spatula Sponge.Description: Pale blue with a prickly texture. Can be spotted in a wide range of forms, including looking like leaves of a lettuce or spatula-like fingers.

Daisy Sponge.Name: Daisy Sponge
Daisy Sponge.Description: Wide range of colors - yellow, purple, brown, green, and black. Usually has 1 or 2 hollow cones in the middle and is encircled by upright long structures.

Orange Prickly Sponge.Name: Orange Prickly Sponge
Orange Prickly Sponge.Description: Orange-colored with prickly projections. Has many tiny holes of about 0.5 cm. Can be found covering rocks and stones or forming branches on their own.

Champagne Sponge.Name: Champagne Sponge
Champagne Sponge.Description: Pink in color. Rough texture due to the tiny spikes on it. Holes may be found along the length of its branches.

Spoon Seagrass.Name: Spoon Seagrass
Spoon Seagrass.Description: Spoon-shaped seagrass with smooth edges. Found in large quantities.

Hairy Spoon Seagrass.Name: Hairy Spoon Seagrass
Hairy Spoon Seagrass.Description: Spoon-shaped with minute hairs on both sides of its leaves. Has thin, smooth and white stems. Leaves appear in pairs from the stems.

Ribbed Turban Snail.Name: Ribbed Turban Snail
Ribbed Turban Snail.Description: Thick shell has many smooth spirals and an operculum that resembles a 'cat's eye'. Operculum is usually a green ring with yellow or white margins and a dark centre.

Toothed Top Shell Snail.Name: Toothed Top Shell Snail
Toothed Top Shell Snail.Description: Assymmetrical grey shell with spiraling round bumps. A white tooth structure at its shell opening.

Spotted Top Shell Snail.Name: Spotted Top Shell Snail
Spotted Top Shell Snail.Description: Thick conical shell with spiraling bumps. Has a yellow underside with dark spots in spirals.
Spotted Top Shell Snail.Habitat: Rocky shore, Sea wall, Coral reef

Watering Pot Shell.Name: Watering Pot Shell
Watering Pot Shell.Description: Broader end has many small holes like the spout of a watering can. Resembles an upside-down carrot when buried.
Watering Pot Shell.Status: Presumed Nationally Extinct (2008 Singapore Red Data Book)

Very Long Ribbon Worm.Name: Very Long Ribbon Worm
Very Long Ribbon Worm.Description: Very long. White body with 4-5 black stripes along the entire length of its body.

Olive Flatworm.Name: Olive Flatworm
Olive Flatworm.Description: Olive-colored on one side, pale on its underside. White outer margin and black inner margin.

Blue-lined Flatworm.Name: Blue-lined Flatworm
Blue-lined Flatworm.Description: White body with a blue margin and a central blue stripe (sometimes yellow).

Straw Tubeworm.Name: Straw Tubeworm
Straw Tubeworm.Description: This animal is a complex worm that lives inside a tube that it builds. The tube resembles a straw and it is usually embedded in the substrate and about 2 – 3 cm exposed aboveground. The straw is 0.5 cm in diameter and often found in large numbers covering large distances.

Banded File Snake.Name: Banded File Snake
Banded File Snake.Description: Baggy skin enclosed by tiny uneven scales, head is not apparent. Its tail recede and condenses to a point. Body covered with black and white stripes across.

Earless Agamid.Name: Earless Agamid
Earless Agamid.Description: Body very slender with long slender limbs and tail. Relatively large head. Brown, mature males have a blue iris, females have a white one.

Green Crested Lizard.Name: Green Crested Lizard
Green Crested Lizard.Description: Head slender and tail very long. Spiny crest over middle of neck. Body colour is usually bright green, sometimes with a bluish tinge. However, when threatened, colour may change to dark brown or grey. Blackish eye-ring and ear. Part of the tail is often brown.

Changeable Lizard.Name: Changeable Lizard
Changeable Lizard.Description: Top of the head is pointed along the middle of the neck and the back. Brownish to greenish yellow with blackish streaks radiating from the eyes and brown bands along the back with a whitish stripe on the sides. Males are bigger with swollen cheeks. During breeding season, the males develop an orange head and a black blotch over the cheeks and throat.

Black-Bearded Flying Dragon.Name: Black-Bearded Flying Dragon
Black-Bearded Flying Dragon.Description: Body very slender with small scales and long slender limbs. Topside of body olive or green with greyish brown bars or diamond-shaped blotches. Throat flap of males black and orange.

Sumatran Flying Dragon.Name: Sumatran Flying Dragon
Sumatran Flying Dragon.Description: Topside of body light brown with dark brown bloches and whitish mottling, patagium (membrane that helps the animal to glide) black with irregular brownish and greenish blotches. The male has a bluish head and a large yellow throat flap.

Hawksbill Turtle.Name: Hawksbill Turtle
Hawksbill Turtle.Description: Husk is oval and brown, overlapping scutes with sporadic yellow and orange speckles. Upper lip bulging ahead of lower lip.

Bigeye Green Whip Snake.Name: Bigeye Green Whip Snake
Bigeye Green Whip Snake.Description: Head is apparent from a slim body, nose is sharp. Lime green body, with a white underside with three green stripes.

Oriental Whip Snake.Name: Oriental Whip Snake
Oriental Whip Snake.Description: Head is apparent from a slim body, nose is sharp. Adults are bright fluorescent green topside, juveniles yellow to pale brown. Snout twice as long as width of the eye.

Dog-Toothed Cat Snake.Name: Dog-Toothed Cat Snake
Dog-Toothed Cat Snake.Description: Head is apparent from a slim body very slender and flat. Body yellowish or brown with sporadic black cross bars, some are nearly completely black. Head light brown with a black line behind the eye.

Gold-ringed Cat Snake.Name: Gold-ringed Cat Snake
Gold-ringed Cat Snake.Description: Body shiny black with a sequence of narrow bright yellow bands, distributed along the body. The local subspecies, has bands which do not meet over the back. Scales on the throat and across the lips bright yellow.

White-spotted Cat Snake.Name: White-spotted Cat Snake
White-spotted Cat Snake.Description: One is mainly green with pale green lines, the other is mainly brown with wide lines of orange and white. Juveniles may exhibit black smudges on top of the head.

Variable Reed Snake.Name: Variable Reed Snake
Variable Reed Snake.Description: Head is not apparent from the body, tail somewhat short and smooth. Body is dark brown, consistently with white or yellow line along the side. Underside with black and yellowish white bands. Young have a pink head and thin white streaks across the back and belly. Five upper labial scales

Pink-headed Reed Snake.Name: Pink-headed Reed Snake
Pink-headed Reed Snake.Description: Head is not apparent from body, tail is short and smooth. It has a bright pink head, topside of body and tail is black and white on the underside. Five upper labial scales.

Paradise Gliding Snake.Name: Paradise Gliding Snake
Paradise Gliding Snake.Description: Slim and circular body, head, with five yellow bands, is compressed and is apparent from the body. Body is black above with a green or yellow spot on each dorsal scale. Some have clusters of red spots to form a pattern down the middle of the back. The belly is yellowish-green.

Common Malayan Racer.Name: Common Malayan Racer
Common Malayan Racer.Description: Head is recognisable from the body, blackish brown with a sequence of black streaks on the sides beside the front of the body. A wide yellowish brown stripe along the middle of the back, enclosed by black streaks darkens as it approached the end. Two black streaks behind and below eye, and along the neck, lips, white streaks.

Striped Bronzeback.Name: Striped Bronzeback
Striped Bronzeback.Description: Black stripe on light background at the sides of the snake. Topside of body brown with six narrow black stripes from the neck to the tail, belly is greenish yellow with black stripe under the tail.

Elegant Bronzeback.Name: Elegant Bronzeback
Elegant Bronzeback.Description: Often confused with Blue Bronzeback. Body long and extremely slender. Topside of the body is bronze brown, a wide black streak across the snout, eye, and partly down the sides. Blue skin runs between the scales, along the sides, belly is yellowish green. Three thin, black lines are present along the tail, which is lacking in Blue Bronzeback.

Kopstein's Bronzeback.Name: Kopstein's Bronzeback
Kopstein's Bronzeback.Description: Body is bronze brown with the neck region bright orange-red. A black streak runs on the side of the head to the top part of the nape. Downside is yellowish green on the front half, then turns to dull green and brown on the tail.

Painted Bronzeback.Name: Painted Bronzeback
Painted Bronzeback.Description: Topside of the body is bronze, belly is yellowish or greenish, and a white streak down each side of the body. A black stripe runs from the start of the snake through the sides, above the white streak. When threatened, the scales of its neck and front of the body expands, exposing the blue skin under the scales.

Malayan Bridle Snake.Name: Malayan Bridle Snake
Malayan Bridle Snake.Description: Body is yellow-grey, with thick, regular brown bands on the top which do not continue to the bottom. A second form has alternating brown and yellow stripes. Scales on the belly are kneeled while the scales along the back are smooth.

Keel-bellied Whip Snake.Name: Keel-bellied Whip Snake
Keel-bellied Whip Snake.Description: Slender body is flattened sideways. Body is greyish or ruddy-brown, with black spots speckled along its back. Belly is beige with brown specks. Tongue is bright red and a wide brown streak runs behind the eyes.

Red-tailed Racer.Name: Red-tailed Racer
Red-tailed Racer.Description: Body is broad and flat, top of head is darker green, topside usually is bright green, underside paler. Tail is orange-red. Other less-common colour forms occur.

House Wolf Snake.Name: House Wolf Snake
House Wolf Snake.Description: Topside of head is dark brown, flat and has a thick yellowish band around the neck. The back of the body is purplish brown with various white specks. The belly is white.

Banded Wolf Snake.Name: Banded Wolf Snake
Banded Wolf Snake.Description: Topside of body is dark brown or black with white streaks across the front part, and darkens towards the tail.

Striped Kukri Snake.Name: Striped Kukri Snake
Striped Kukri Snake.Description: Head is not recognisable from large and smooth body. Topside is greyish brown with a red streak along the middle of the back, which is bounded by three black stripes on each side. Topmost two stripes joined at the top of the head, a black streak runs across the eyes and the belly is pink in colour.

Barred Kukri Snake.Name: Barred Kukri Snake
Barred Kukri Snake.Description: Topside of the body is dark-brown with red streaks of different shapes, the streaks will join to form a chevron pattern on the head. Underside is reddish-pink.

Dwarf Reed Snake.Name: Dwarf Reed Snake
Dwarf Reed Snake.Description: Body hardly recognisable from its body, nose is sharp and the tail is short. Topside of the body is in lustrous black and smooth. Some have a pale yellow collar with a pair of pale spots on the neck.

Keeled Rat Snake.Name: Keeled Rat Snake
Keeled Rat Snake.Description: Head is recognisable from slim and smooth body. Topside is brown blackish at the front sometimes with yellow streaks. Back of the body is yellowish brown with a specific web pattern, tail is black with yellow speckles. Sides of the head and neck is white.

White-bellied Rat Snake.Name: White-bellied Rat Snake
White-bellied Rat Snake.Description: Head is recognisable from slim and smooth body. Topside of the body is brown with a reddish brown stripe down the back towards the tail. A broad black line along the sides near the tail. Underside usually yellow or white.

Estuarine Crocodile.Name: Estuarine Crocodile
Estuarine Crocodile.Description: Snout long and relatively broad, tail muscular and compressed. Body yellow, olive or grey above with black checker-spots, and white below.

Brown Anole.Name: Brown Anole
Brown Anole.Description: Male colour differs from light grey to stark-black and have a dewlap that is orange-red. Females have dark-coloured triangular pattern along a white stripe which runs down the back.

Banded Krait.Name: Banded Krait
Banded Krait.Description: Head is somewhat recognisable from large and smooth body, body has triangular sub-sections. Topside on body is white or yellow with various black bands which runs until the belly, alternating with the white sections. Both head and tail are rounded.

Blue Malayan Coral Snake.Name: Blue Malayan Coral Snake
Blue Malayan Coral Snake.Description: A small head that is somewhat recognisable from a very slim body. Topside of body is dark navy blue with sky blue streak that runs by the sides, underside is red. Head and tail bright coral red.

Banded Malayan Coral Snake.Name: Banded Malayan Coral Snake
Banded Malayan Coral Snake.Description: Small head hardly recognisable from slim body. Topside of body is dark brown with a red streak down the middle. Belly is white with black rings, underside of tail is coloured red, with black streaks across.

Red-eared Slider.Name: Red-eared Slider
Red-eared Slider.Description: Husk is greenish brown with yellowish lines, bottom side of husk is yellow with black specks on each scute. Head green streaked with yellow, a wide bright red smudge behind the eye. Limbs and tail green with yellow lines. Adult males have claws at front limbs.

Peters\u2019s Bent-toed Gecko.Name: Peters’s Bent-toed Gecko
Peters\u2019s Bent-toed Gecko.Description: Black or brownish body above with narrow, irregular white bands across body and tail. Bands become dark-edged in adults. Symmetrical arrangement of pale or cream reticulations present on head.

Singapore Bent-toed Gecko.Name: Singapore Bent-toed Gecko
Singapore Bent-toed Gecko.Description: Body pinkish grey with black blotches down the back, tail blackish with pale bands. Pale yellow mottling on head.

Frilly Gecko.Name: Frilly Gecko
Frilly Gecko.Description: Distinctly mottled with brown and grey above, yellowish below. Colouration may be variable, very well camouflaged. Flattened tail and flaps of skin along the flanks.

Peninsular Rock Gecko.Name: Peninsular Rock Gecko
Peninsular Rock Gecko.Description: Snout long, broad and slightly upturned. Yellow above with dark brown and white blotches and streaks. Previously known as Kendall's Rock Gecko.

Spotted House Gecko.Name: Spotted House Gecko
Spotted House Gecko.Description: Body covered with warts, pale greyish-brown with seven to nine pairs of blackish blotches along the back, and a series of blackish bars on the tail.

Four-clawed Gecko.Name: Four-clawed Gecko
Four-clawed Gecko.Description: Translucent pinkish brown with gold and blackish flecks. Tail smooth.

Tokay.Name: Tokay
Tokay.Description: Similar to Large Forest Gecko, discernible by size. Body blue-grey spotted with orange.

Spiny-tailed House Gecko.Name: Spiny-tailed House Gecko
Spiny-tailed House Gecko.Description: Highly variable species. Can be distinguished by the presence of whorls of small spines on original tail. Colour variable, but tends to be uniformed shade of brown or brown with darker markings.

Flat-tailed Gecko.Name: Flat-tailed Gecko
Flat-tailed Gecko.Description: Tail relatively flat. Colour variable, ranging from pale gret to gret with dark grey mottles and streaks.

Lowland Dwarf Gecko.Name: Lowland Dwarf Gecko
Lowland Dwarf Gecko.Description: Body very slender with short limbs. Body brown above with blackish markings over the back. Tail slender, pale brown or yellow with a yellowish blotch at the base.

Mourning Gecko.Name: Mourning Gecko
Mourning Gecko.Description: Body slender with ornate greyish-brown marbling. Pattern often presents in the form of chevrons on the back. Broad tail with a series of irregular black-edged yellowish bands on top.

Malayan Box Terrapin.Name: Malayan Box Terrapin
Malayan Box Terrapin.Description: Husk is rounded and black in coloured, bottom part of the husk is yellowish, with a pivot that allows the turtle to completely hide inside the husk. Topside of the head is black with a yellow streak across the eyes.

Asian Leaf Terrapin.Name: Asian Leaf Terrapin
Asian Leaf Terrapin.Description: Husk is oval shaped and coloured brown with five vertebral scutes, sides of the husk is jagged and slighly curved upwards. Head and nape dark brown with orange strokes.  Infants have greyish brown, compressed husk with thick black specks.

Spiny Terrapin.Name: Spiny Terrapin
Spiny Terrapin.Description: Rosy brown husk that is leveled at the top with jagged edges and a light brown backbone through the husk, with five vertebral scutes. Head, arms and legs are dark grey with reddsh speck on two sides of the head. Husks for young are leveled and heart-shaped with jagged edges. Young have the bottom side of the husk in intense yellow, streaked with black, and jagged borders.

Black Marsh Terrapin.Name: Black Marsh Terrapin
Black Marsh Terrapin.Description: Husk has smooth sides, black, while the bottom side of husk is black with brown stripes. Husk is rounded when seen from the side and jagged at the end, with five vertebral scutes. The head is black spotted white.

Cantor's Water Snake.Name: Cantor's Water Snake
Cantor's Water Snake.Description: Very slim body that is yellow with thick black or brown smudges. Some have back end of the body nearly totally black.

Sunda Dog-faced Water Snake.Name: Sunda Dog-faced Water Snake
Sunda Dog-faced Water Snake.Description: Wide head, topside of body is grey, brown or green. A dark line crosses the eyes and continues to the neck, eyes and nose are on the top of the head.

Rainbow Water Snake.Name: Rainbow Water Snake
Rainbow Water Snake.Description: Topside of body is brownish, a flat head and neck is greener than the other part of the body, with a pair of paler lines running through which meets at the head. Underside is light coloured with a thin brown line along the middle.

Crab-eating Water Snake.Name: Crab-eating Water Snake
Crab-eating Water Snake.Description: Head is blunt and not recognisable from the circular body, with a short tail. Topside is plurplish brown dimming to white to the underside.

Yellow-lipped Water Snake.Name: Yellow-lipped Water Snake
Yellow-lipped Water Snake.Description: Blunt head that is somewhat recognisable from the circular body, topside is grey and light brown underside with a black streak down the middle. Upper lips are yellow, which continues along the side of the body.

Puff-faced Water Snake.Name: Puff-faced Water Snake
Puff-faced Water Snake.Description: Wide head that is recognisable from thick and circular body. Topside is grey rigged with black and dark brown blotches across the body. Nose is black with a black streak cutting across the eyes, belly is white with tiny black smudges. The topside of a young is orange with black blotches.

Blackwater Mud Snake.Name: Blackwater Mud Snake
Blackwater Mud Snake.Description: Rich brown to greyish black colour patterned with thin, broken bright yellow bands on the side of the body. Bright yellow belly. Thin Yellow band between its eyes with numerous small yellow spots through body and tail.

Spotted Keelback.Name: Spotted Keelback
Spotted Keelback.Description: Head is recognisable from the body and scales are strongly kneeled. Topside is dark brown or grey, squared black smudges on the neck. A wide dark brown streak with black spots runs down the back, alternating with squared yellow speckles. Slightly red at the sides and yellow on the belly, rigged with black edges.

Striped Keelback.Name: Striped Keelback
Striped Keelback.Description: Head is recognisable from the body and scales are strongly kneeled. Topside is black with four yellowish brown streaks running through. Belly is white, segmented with wide black rings.

White-spotted Slug Snake.Name: White-spotted Slug Snake
White-spotted Slug Snake.Description: Head is recognisable from broad and compressed body. Topside is grey or brown with various white and black specks together, neck is bounded by a ring of reddish collar. Belly is white and spotted with black specks

Reticulated Python.Name: Reticulated Python
Reticulated Python.Description: Head is recognisable from broad and smooth body. Eyes are orange and topside is greyish brown with a web of sporadic lines, white belly. The sides are spotted white interchanging with black lines, a thin black line runs down the centre of the head, and another from eye towards the neck.

Many-lined Sun Skink.Name: Many-lined Sun Skink
Many-lined Sun Skink.Description: Body bronze-brown with possible arrays of thin black stripes along the back. Sides either blackish with white spots or wrap with orange from the ear to the back legs. Underside of the head yellow on some individuals.

Striped Sun Skink.Name: Striped Sun Skink
Striped Sun Skink.Description: Body brown or olive-green on top, usually with 5 to 7 yellowish stripes or series of spots, greenish-white below.

Striped Tree Skink.Name: Striped Tree Skink
Striped Tree Skink.Description: Body slim and draped in shiny smooth, overlapping flakes; symmetrical arrangement of large scales on top of the head with an outstretched snout. Body and head with a broad yellow stripe bounded by black stripes along the back; tail long and orange.

Brown Tree Skink.Name: Brown Tree Skink
Brown Tree Skink.Description: Strong body that is enclosed with glossy, rigged overlapping scales. Symmetrical scales patterned above the head. Body olive brown above with sporadic, thin black bands and white spots. Young are black and yellowish bands along the back, tail yellow with thin black bands.

Mangrove Skink.Name: Mangrove Skink
Mangrove Skink.Description: Slim body with smooth overlapping scales, symmetrical arrangement of large scales above the head. Greyish brown on the back, bluish with a blackish stripe along the sides. Tail and limbs are covered with whitish spots at the top. Orange bellies are seen in some.

Garden Supple Skink.Name: Garden Supple Skink
Garden Supple Skink.Description: Slim body wrapped in glossy, smooth and rigged overlapping scales. Arms and legs are tiny, tail is long and chunky. Body bronze-brown on the back enclosed by yellow stripes with bright yellow belly. Sides are black with white spots and a red smudge around the arms.

Singapore Swamp Skink.Name: Singapore Swamp Skink
Singapore Swamp Skink.Description: Upperside ground colour is dark brown, with faint pale markings extending in lines from the head to the base of the tail. Underside surface is beige. Juveniles are paler than adults and somewhat pinkish.

Asian Softshell Turtle.Name: Asian Softshell Turtle
Asian Softshell Turtle.Description: Husk is somewhat squarish, leathery, various spines can be spotted externally. Husk is greyish-brown with sporadic blackish bands. Various yellow specks on head and limbs, with some on the husk, belly is white. Nose is elongated, with a long neck and webbed feet with claws.

Brahminy Blind Snake.Name: Brahminy Blind Snake
Brahminy Blind Snake.Description: The body is totally dark brown to black. The rounded head, with tiny eyes, is not recognisable from the body with a short tail.

Clouded Monitor.Name: Clouded Monitor
Clouded Monitor.Description: Its has a slim and splitted tongue, small snout with nostrils midway between the eye and the tip of the snout. Greyish brown heavily spotted yellow.

Malayan Water Monitor.Name: Malayan Water Monitor
Malayan Water Monitor.Description: Adults are greyish brown, nostrils are ajacent to the tip of snout. Young are black with pale fronts, and bands made up of rows of yellow spots down their backs and tails.

Shore Pit-viper.Name: Shore Pit-viper
Shore Pit-viper.Description: Head is widely angled from the top and is recognisable from bulky body, bounded in kneeled scales. Body purplish-brown, bounded by thin white streaks at the sides. The young are rein with dark brown streaks.

Wagler's Pit-viper.Name: Wagler's Pit-viper
Wagler's Pit-viper.Description: Head widely angular from top view and is recognisable from the bulky body bounded in kneeled scales. Topside of adult females black spotted with green and yellow streaks, underside greenish white with yellow smudges. Young and adult males are green with white blotches or lines, red and white streak also runs down the side and has a red tail.

Iridescent Earth Snake.Name: Iridescent Earth Snake
Iridescent Earth Snake.Description: Compressed head is not recognisable from the body. Topside of body black to brown, belly is white. Tail recedes and short. Infants have a white band binding the nape.
